key = { path = "/details[at0001]/items[openEHR-DEMOGRAPHIC-CLUSTER.person_identifier.v2]/items[at0001]", type = "guid" }
user_name = { path = "/details[at0001]/items[openEHR-DEMOGRAPHIC-CLUSTER.person_identifier.v2]/items[at0001]", type = "scim_user_name" }
external_id = { path = "/details[at0001]/items[openEHR-DEMOGRAPHIC-CLUSTER.person_identifier.v2]/items[at0001]", type = "scim_external_id" }

[[authz.party_binding.person.attribute]]
scim = "name.formatted"
oidc = "name"
jit = true
name = true
path = { "FerroEHR professional" = "/identities[openEHR-DEMOGRAPHIC-PARTY_IDENTITY.person_name.v1]/details[at0001]/items[at0002]" }

[authz.party_binding.professional_role]
template_id = "FerroEHR professional role"

[authz.party_binding.group]
template_id = "FerroEHR care team"
external_id = { path = "/details[at0001]/items[at0001]", type = "scim_external_id" }
display_name = "/identities[at0002]/details[at0003]/items[at0004]"

[authz.party_binding.membership]
archetype_id = "openEHR-DEMOGRAPHIC-PARTY_RELATIONSHIP.membership.v1"

[authz.party_binding.representation]
archetype_id = "openEHR-DEMOGRAPHIC-PARTY_RELATIONSHIP.representation.v1"
relationship_codes = { at0010 = "254", at0011 = "264" }

With Microsoft Entra ID, map the object id to externalId (Entra’s matching) and to the binding-key attribute (the binding): two attributes, two selectors. The key’s [[auth.party]] identifier_type is guid, so a key differing only in case binds one login.

Boot refuses, naming the key: no or two default tables; a selector path that does not compile; two equal selectors; a key whose scheme [privacy.identifier_protection] protects; any selector under the Dutch BSN namespace (OID 2.16.840.1.113883.2.4.6.3); a key fed by an email address, a phone number, preferred_username, name, upn or unique_name; a template that is absent, rooted at another class or lacks a mapped path; a path whose type cannot carry its source; and a representation type with no subject_relationship code. Deleting a template the mapping names is refused with 409.

The parties the binding relies on are protected: a PERSON of a mapped template carrying a selector identifier, its professional ROLE, a representation relationship, and a GROUP of the group template. Only an administrator (authz.rbac.admin_role) writes one through the demographic API, including the creation of a party that carries a selector identifier. An administrator’s version that leaves a protected identifier out is refused with 422. A present binding key is immutable (RFC 7643 §2.2): a version that changes it is refused with 403, and POST /admin/party/binding-key is the one change. Each selector value binds one live party: a commit that gives a binding key, a userName (compared after RFC 8265 width mapping, lower case and NFC), an externalId or a group displayName a second party is refused with 409. A deleted PERSON leaves its key as a tombstone that refuses the login until an administrator binds the key again.

Changing the mapping

The side table is filled from the configured mapping and the party versions. The first boot fills it and stores the mapping’s digest; a replica whose mapping digest differs from the stored one refuses to start, naming both digests. Each running replica holds a lease it renews every 20 seconds. A mapping change is a stop-the-world step:

  1. Stop every replica. With Helm, scale the deployment to zero first: a rolling upgrade would start new replicas beside old ones.
  2. Run ferroehr party-binding refill with the new configuration. It refuses while a replica’s lease was renewed within the last minute, and refuses a store in which two parties carry one selector value, naming both.
  3. Start the replicas with the new mapping. A replica still holding the old mapping refuses to start.

How a login is looked up

Every request of a person is looked up in the binding side table of the party store, on the party database role, with no cache, so a change to a party takes effect on the next request on every instance. The table holds the binding key of each PERSON of a mapped template that performs a professional ROLE (a ROLE of the mapped role template that its roles list, that names it as performer, whose state is complete or incomplete and whose time_validity holds today’s date in UTC) or that is the source of a representation relationship. A key of type guid or uuid is compared in lower case. The table is written in each party commit’s transaction and can be rebuilt from the party versions alone.

The request is refused with 403 and the binding code in the problem body when the login matches two parties (refused-ambiguous), when its party is inactive (refused-inactive) or abandoned (refused-abandoned), when its key belongs to a deleted party (refused-deprovisioned), when the token carries no key claim (refused-key-claim-missing), when the party lacks the marker the caller’s kind needs (refused-wrong-marker), when the groups a token asserts cannot be read (refused-groups-unavailable), when a guest comes from an issuer whose table does not set guests (refused-guest), and when a representative’s token names a subject its party has no live representation relationship to (refused-representation-unrecorded). A party store or an identity provider that cannot answer is answered 503, with Retry-After when the identity provider gave one.

A person whose login matches no party is refused with 403 and refused-unbound on every request, reads and writes alike; only the public endpoints outside the auth layer answer. The problem names the identifier issuer to provision the person under, and the refusal of a token without the key claim names the missing claim instead. No setting serves an unbound person under a login-only committer, so provision every professional (through SCIM or the demographic API) before you add a persons issuer, or let the issuer create a provisional PERSON at the first login (just-in-time creation). Each refusal writes one warn line naming the issuer and the outcome, never the claim value, and counts into the binding_refusals metric by issuer and outcome.

A representative reaches only the EHR whose EHR_STATUS.subject.external_ref names the subject it represents: the issuer’s representation claim carries the subject’s party id, matched without regard to case, and the subject must be the target of one of the representative’s live relationships, so a representative of an issuer no [[auth.party]] table binds is refused. Every composition, EHR_STATUS, directory, contribution and query request is held to that EHR, whatever the token’s scopes cover; a query must name it with ehr_id. Templates stay readable. A persons token whose only clinical scopes are patient/ is a professional confined to its launch EHR, and its commits record the professional, never PARTY_SELF.

Just-in-time creation

Just-in-time creation lets a professional with no party work under their own account at their first login, before SCIM or an administrator completes the record. It is off by default and enabled per persons issuer in one [[authz.party_binding.issuer]] table. When a login of that issuer matches no party, FerroEHR commits one PERSON of the default template with lifecycle state 553|incomplete|, which RM common §Incomplete Content allows for “incomplete demographic details”, and its professional ROLE in the same demographic contribution, then serves the request bound to it. The next request binds to that PERSON and creates nothing. When a login creates a party is FerroEHR’s own design: no openEHR specification governs it.

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
issuerstringrequiredA persons issuer an [[auth.party]] table binds.
jitbooleanfalseWhether a first login with no party creates a provisional PERSON.
guests_jitbooleanfalseWhether a guest is created too; needs jit and the issuer’s [[auth.party]] guests.
user_name_claimstringthe profile’s person_keyThe claim the userName is read from. It must be one the issuer controls: an email address, a phone number, preferred_username, name, upn and unique_name refuse the start.
idp_claimstringidpThe dotted claim path the identity provider is read from (the Microsoft Entra idp claim).
admit_idplist of strings[]The identity providers whose logins are created.
admit_groupslist of strings[]The groups, read from the [[auth.party]] group_claim, of which a created login holds one.
admit_roleslist of strings[]The roles, read from [auth] role_claims, of which a created login holds one.
admit_assurancelow, substantial or highunsetThe lowest [authz.assurance] level a created login carries.

jit = true needs at least one admission condition, and a login must meet every condition the table declares. It also needs a default person template with a user_name selector, [authz.party_binding.professional_role], and an attribute that maps an OpenID Connect name claim (name, given_name, family_name, middle_name or nickname) to the default template; boot refuses the table otherwise.

[[authz.party_binding.issuer]]
issuer = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0"
jit = true
admit_groups = ["5f2a9c1e-0000-4000-8000-00000000c11a"]
admit_assurance = "substantial"

What it writes is the attribution minimum: the binding key, the userName and the name claims the token carries. Any other mapped attribute is written only where its [[authz.party_binding.person.attribute]] sets jit = true (GDPR Art. 25(2), data protection by default), and externalId is never written, since RFC 7643 §3.1 leaves it to the provisioning client. The version is committed with change type 249|creation|, a description naming just-in-time creation and the issuer, and the person’s own committer: the name, the login identifier and an external_ref naming the new PERSON. FerroEHR reads every value from the access token only (RFC 9068 §2.2.2), so the issuer must put the name claims in the access token.

It runs only for a person or a delegated caller of the issuer, never for a representative, a patient, a system or a federation caller, and never for a login whose outcome is anything other than unbound: an ambiguous, inactive, abandoned or deprovisioned party, a token without the key claim and a party with the wrong marker are refused as before. A PERSON a SCIM client deleted is never created again by a later login, whatever the identity provider still issues. A login that fails an admission condition, or whose token carries no mapped name claim, is refused with 403 and refused-unbound.

Concurrent first requests of one login commit one PERSON: the binding key’s unique index refuses the second commit, and that request binds to the first one’s PERSON. A login whose userName another party already holds is refused with 403 and binds nothing. Just-in-time creation only creates: it never updates, deactivates or deletes a PERSON, so a later login with changed claims changes nothing.

A PERSON whose latest version is incomplete is provisional. The access record of each of its requests carries binding = provisional, a demographic read and an AQL query over VERSION/lifecycle_state show it, and ferroehr party-binding check reports the provisional persons older than provisional_report_after under side_table.provisional. What a provisional person may do is decided by their SMART scopes and roles, as for anyone. A SCIM client whose binding_issuer is the issuer’s identifier_issuer completes the PERSON: it finds it by userName, with a binding key equal to its own, writes the externalId with a PATCH, and a complete PUT completes it. SCIM active = false abandons it.

The lawful basis for the attribution minimum (key, userName, name) is GDPR Art. 6(1)(c): EHDS Art. 13(4) and the logging duties need the professional identified. An operator who opts a contact attribute in with jit = true names its own basis, Art. 6(1)(b) or (f). Because the data come from the identity provider and not from the person, tell the professionals what Art. 14 asks: what is copied, from which source, and why. On a realm or tenant that creates persons, make the name attributes administrator-controlled, as the key is; Enterprise identity providers shows the settings per identity provider.

[authz.import] and [[authz.system_client]]

[authz.import] trusted_systems lists the creating_system_id values whose wrapped committers may name a local party on import; this node’s own [api] system_id is refused.

Each OAuth client-credentials client that commits is declared in one [[authz.system_client]] table, keyed by issuer (a machines or persons issuer) and client_id. A Basic user is never a system client. A system caller with no table reads under its system/ scopes and commits nothing into an EHR (403); a declared one commits a COMPOSITION only of a template its writes lists, at a facility its facilities lists, as the caller kinds describe.

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
issuer, client_idstringrequiredThe client, as its tokens name it. A duplicate pair refuses the start.
provider{ issuer, id }requiredThe healthcare provider it acts for, recorded on every system access (EHDS Annex II 3.2(a)).
facilitieslist of { issuer, id } or { issuer, id_prefix }[]The facility identifiers it may commit for.
writeslist of template ids[]The templates it may commit; a template the store does not hold refuses the start.
originslist of relay, devicerequiredrelay: it relays another system’s record of a human act, such as HL7 v2. device: a device registers with no human acting, which needs device_identifier_issuers.
device_identifier_issuerslist of string[]The issuers of the device identifiers a device client names.

[[authz.federation.agreement]]

What a federation issuer’s verified external persons, or its organisation, may do here. Each table is keyed by issuer and accessor and admits only its own accessor kind; every agreement is listed on the boot line and in GET /management/info, and one that runs without a named person is logged at warn on every boot.

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
issuerstringrequiredThe federation issuer.
accessorperson or organisationrequiredNamed persons, or the organisation without a named person. A duplicate (issuer, accessor) pair refuses the start.
name, versionstring""The agreement; required for an organisation.
jurisdictionISO 3166-1 alpha-2""An issuer with profile = "nl" implies NL.
exchangestring""The kind of exchange the agreement covers.
purposecare or keuringunsetWhat the exchange is for. Required for every NL agreement, and an NL agreement for a keuring (a medical examination for employment, insurance or a licence) refuses the start, since a keurend arts has no access to an exchange system (Wabvpz Art. 15f(2)).
legal_ground{ gdpr_6_1, gdpr_9_2, national }unsetThe GDPR Art. 6(1) point (a to f), the Art. 9(2) point (a to j) and the national provision; in the Netherlands Art. 9(2)(h) with UAVG Art. 30(3)(a). Required for an organisation.
consentmitz or localunsetThe source of the consent the exchange is conditioned on, never its legal ground. A read under it needs the consent decision reference the token carries in the field its [[auth.federation]] table maps to consent.reference, and is refused with 403 without it. Required for every NL agreement with reads (Wabvpz Art. 15a(1)); an organisation may not take it from Mitz, whose closed question needs a responsible professional.
readslist of patient/ scopes[]The most an external caller may read; a user/ or system/ scope refuses the start.
writeslist of template ids[]The templates an external person may commit; an organisation agreement takes none (EHDS Art. 13(4)), and a template the store does not hold refuses the start.
discard, discard_windowbool, intfalse, 24Whether an external person may discard a dispensation of the same point of care within the window (MyHealth@EU Requirements Catalogue 10.0.0, requirement 07.04).
ehdsi_servicepatient_summary, eprescription or orcdunsetThe MyHealth@EU service a contact_point issuer’s person agreement serves, whose *_NOT_FOUND code a request outside the patient of the treatment relationship confirmation answers (the contact-point route). Required on a contact point’s person agreement; on any other agreement it refuses the start.
caller_rate{ requests_per_second, burst }requiredThe admission rate per caller, keyed on the token’s subject and kept per replica: each caller gets burst requests at once and requests_per_second after that, and a request above it is answered 429 with Retry-After before any patient lookup, a contact point’s included, and counted into the caller’s summary record.
opt_out_overrideboolfalseWhether a professional may read an opted-out EHR under national vital-interest access (EHDS Art. 10(2)); never on an organisation agreement.
access_classautomated or chainedunsetFor an organisation, required: no natural person views the data, or the requester logs the person and every request carries its correlation id as an attested claim. A chained agreement needs its issuer’s [[auth.federation]] table to map correlation_id from a claim or an attested authorization_details member (a constant refuses the start); a request without the id is refused with 403 and recorded as refused-correlation-missing, a request header never stands in for it, and the access record carries the id with its source.
chained_log_retentioncalendar periodunsetFor chained, required: how long the requester keeps its log ("P5Y"), at least [audit.store]’s retention.

An organisation agreement on a MyHealth@EU contact_point issuer refuses the start.

[authz.rbac]

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
enabledbooltrueThe coarse role gate (active when authentication is enabled). Off, every authenticated caller may use every enabled surface, reported as the rbac_off deployment gap. ehr_access_default and admin_role apply either way.
admin_rolestringADMINRole required for admin-class operations. A blank value is a boot error.
readonly_rolestringREADONLYRole marking a principal read-only: refused on every write operation (create/update/delete/upload), even alongside granting roles. Reads and AQL queries are still allowed.
emergency_access_rolestringunsetRole that reads data under an EHDS Art. 8 access restriction when the caller also declares one of [audit] emergency_purpose_codes (EHDS Art. 11(5)); the access record then carries the emergency mark. Unset, nobody may override a restriction. See restriction of access.
access_service_roleslist of strings[]Roles of the EHDS Art. 10 access-service callers: the Art. 4 access service of persons and the Art. 12 health professional access service. A caller holding one reads an EHR whose person opted out as absent, unless it declares one of [audit] emergency_purpose_codes and does not act for the person (Art. 10(2)). Empty, the opt-out holds for nobody and recording one is refused. Environment: FERROEHR__AUTHZ__RBAC__ACCESS_SERVICE_ROLES, comma-separated. See opt-out from the access services.
identifier_reader_rolestringunsetRole that may read a party’s protected national identifiers through GET /ferroehr/rest/extensions/v1/admin/party/identifiers, beside the admin role. Every read is an access record naming the reader, the party and the scheme. Unset, nobody may. See reading a party’s protected identifiers.
subject_audit_rolestringunsetRole that may read the access log for one subject at a time: GET /fhir/r4/AuditEvent with the patient parameter required, refused without it. The grant a patient portal holds to serve a person’s right to know who accessed their record (GDPR Art. 15, EHDS Art. 9), instead of an admin credential over every patient’s log. Unset, the log stays admin-only. See Audit trail.
import_rolestringunsetRole that may import an EHR or an EHR extract (message_import_ehr, message_import_ehr_extract).
role_issuerslist of string[]The persons issuers whose role claims may grant admin_role, emergency_access_role, import_role and identifier_reader_role. A token of any other issuer never holds them, and a Basic user keeps the roles its own table grants. An issuer of another kind refuses the start. Empty, no token grants them.
ehr_access_defaultenum{open,restricted}openWhat an EHR carrying no ACCESS_CONTROL_SETTINGS admits. restricted is object-level default-deny: only admin_role reaches a setting-less EHR, so an operator can still author the settings that open it. It is enforced whether enabled is on or off. With [auth] enabled = false nothing could enforce restricted, so that combination is a boot error. See Security.

Note

The management surface is not configured under [authz.rbac]. [management.endpoints] owns it, one level per endpoint, with no global default beside it: an endpoint you do not name is off and is not mounted. Only the admin_only level consults authz.rbac.admin_role.

[authz.abac]

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
enabledboolfalseMaster ABAC switch. The table keeps enabled where other optional features use the table’s presence, because organization_claim applies while it is off: the access log records it.
engineenum{cedar,remote}cedarEmbedded Cedar, or a remote decision point.
organization_claimstringorganization_idJWT claim carrying the caller’s organization.
patient_claimstringpatient_idJWT claim carrying the patient id. Set, it scopes every request to the patient it names (see below). Empty turns the patient scope off.
patient_namespacestringunsetThe subject namespace (EHR_STATUS.subject.external_ref.namespace) the patient ids in patient_claim are issued in. Set, a claim names the EHR whose subject is that id under this namespace. Unset, a claim names the EHR holding that id only when no other namespace holds the same id.
check_directoryboolfalseSubmit DIRECTORY (FOLDER) operations to the decision point. Engine-independent, so it works under Cedar as well as a remote PDP.

The patient scope. With ABAC on and patient_claim set, a token without that claim is refused with 403. With the claim:

  • A route that names an EHR (/ehr/{ehr_id}/…) answers 403 unless the claim names that EHR’s subject. An EHR that records no subject is in no patient’s scope and is refused.
  • Without patient_namespace, an id held under two or more namespaces names none of those subjects, so it reaches none of their EHRs. Set patient_namespace to read the claim in one namespace.
  • An AQL query returns rows only from EHRs the claim names, whatever the query selects, including SELECT e/ehr_id/value FROM EHR e.

After a query runs, the decision point receives the subject ids of every EHR the query touched as its patient attribute, so a patient-keyed policy applies to queries whether or not patient_claim is set. Without patient_namespace, a query that touches a subject id held under several namespaces is refused with 403, because a bare id would name both subjects.

  • [authz.abac.cedar]: policy_dir (path, required when engine = "cedar" and ABAC is on) and reload_interval (duration, unset, an optional hot-reload interval).
  • [authz.abac.remote.endpoint]: the policy service, as the family’s endpoint table: url (required when engine = "remote", and it must end with /, because the policy name is appended; credentials embedded in it are masked in every rendering), connect_timeout ("2s" here), timeout ("5s" here), retry (a call that got no answer or a 5xx is asked again; a 4xx is a decision and is never asked again), tls and credentials.
  • [authz.abac.remote.endpoint.credentials.oauth]: calls the policy service as an OAuth 2.0 client instead of with HTTP Basic: FerroEHR obtains a token with the client credentials grant and sends it as a bearer token, with the grant’s keys. When the policy service refuses the token with 401, a new one is fetched and the decision asked once more; a token that cannot be obtained, or that is refused again, is no decision, and the request fails closed with a 500, never a 403. A url with credentials beside this table stops startup.
  • [authz.abac.policy.<kind>]: one entry per resource kind, with kind ∈ ehr, ehr_status, composition, contribution, query, directory. Keys: name (string, the policy to evaluate) and parameters (list of enum{organization,patient,template}). A key that is not one of those six kinds is a boot error, and template is rejected on ehr and ehr_status, since neither carries a template.

Warning

With engine = "remote", every resource kind the enforcement point consults needs a policy entry: ehr, ehr_status, composition, contribution, query, plus directory when check_directory = true. A missing one is a boot error. At runtime a kind with no policy can only be denied, since there is no policy to ask and permitting would be a silent hole, so the misconfiguration is caught at startup rather than turning into blanket 403s on live traffic. The Cedar engine reads its policies from authz.abac.cedar.policy_dir and needs no entries here.

[api] admin

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
adminboolfalseMount the ADMIN API (physical, irreversible delete). Off ⇒ every admin route answers 405 Method Not Allowed with an empty Allow header, never 403, and never touches the backend.

Physical deletion is irreversible, so the group stays off by default. With it on, /admin also joins the group list the OPTIONS System-Options manifest advertises, so the manifest never names a group that answers 404.

[auth.scim]

FerroEHR is a SCIM 2.0 service provider (RFC 7644) at /scim/v2/, the endpoint an identity provider provisions each professional through. It is off by default.

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
public_base_urlstringnoneThe externally reachable origin, such as https://cdr.example.com, that every meta.location and discovery document names as <public_base_url>/scim/v2 (RFC 7643 §3.1). Required; it carries no userinfo, query or fragment.
filter_max_resultsinteger100The most resources one list response returns, which ServiceProviderConfig declares as filter.maxResults. At least 1.
max_deactivationsinteger100The most Users one client deactivates or deletes per window. Past it, a deactivation or deletion is 429 with Retry-After and logged at error. The count is kept in the database, so every replica shares one bound. At least 1.
deactivation_windowduration"1h"The length of that window. At least "1min".
contact_erasure_delayduration"0s"How long after a User’s deletion the contacts of every version of its PERSON are erased (GDPR Art. 17). "0s" erases them in the deletion itself; at most "30d".
max_group_membersinteger5000The most members one Group holds. An add past it is 400 invalidValue. A membership change versions only the member’s PERSON, so its cost does not grow with the Group. At least 1.

Each [[auth.scim.client]] table declares one provisioning client:

KeyDescription
issuerThe issuer of the client’s access tokens: your own authorization server, an [[auth.issuer]] of kind machines. FerroEHR issues no tokens.
client_idThe client the token names (client_id, failing that azp).
scopeThe one scope a token of the client must hold. SMART on openEHR defines none for SCIM, so the value is yours to choose.
binding_issuerThe identifier issuer of the binding keys the client provisions: the identifier_issuer of an [[auth.party]] table. Each User belongs to the one client whose binding_issuer issues its key, so no two clients share one.

The start is refused when enabled is set without public_base_url or without a client, and for a client that misses a key, is declared twice, shares a binding_issuer, names an issuer that is not of kind machines, or names a binding_issuer no [[auth.party]] table carries. It is refused too when the party mapping lacks what a User is written with: a default person template with a user_name selector, and [authz.party_binding.professional_role].

[auth.scim]
public_base_url = "https://cdr.example.com"

[[auth.scim.client]]
issuer = "https://as.example.com"
client_id = "entra-provisioning"
scope = "ferroehr/scim"
binding_issuer = "urn:example:staff-login"

/scim/v2/ServiceProviderConfig answers without a token, so a client can read the authentication scheme before it holds one. Every other path needs a bearer token of a declared client that acts for nobody and holds its scope:

  • no token, or one that does not verify, is 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer;
  • a person’s token, a client no table declares, and a token without the scope are 403, the last with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope" (RFC 6750 §3.1).

Every refusal is an RFC 7644 §3.12 Error message in application/scim+json. The client’s requests count against [server.caller_rate] like any caller’s, so each replica gives the client an allowance of its own, and past it a request is 429 with Retry-After. /scim/v2/Schemas serves the core User schema reduced to userName, active and the SCIM attributes [[authz.party_binding.person.attribute]] maps, and FerroEHR’s extension urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:ferrohealth:2.0:User with loginIdentifier, the attribute that feeds the binding key. /ResourceTypes lists the User type at /Users.

Users

A User is a PERSON of the default person template performing the professional ROLE. The client serves these operations (RFC 7644 §3):

  • POST /scim/v2/Users creates the PERSON and its ROLE in one demographic CONTRIBUTION, under the client as committer, and answers 201 with the User, its Location and its ETag. The body carries userName and the binding key in loginIdentifier; externalId and every mapped attribute are optional. A version that fits its template in full is complete, and one that fits only with every lower limit at zero is incomplete, which the User’s lifecycleState and missingPaths name. A User created with active = false is 400 invalidValue.
  • GET /scim/v2/Users/{id} answers the User with its ETag, the weak tag of its version, and 304 to an If-None-Match naming that version.
  • GET /scim/v2/Users answers a ListResponse, an empty one with 200 when nothing matches. filter takes eq and and over userName, externalId and id; names and operators are compared in any case, and anything else is 400 invalidFilter. startIndex and count page the result, at most max_results at a time.

The User’s userName, externalId and binding key are DV_IDENTIFIERs at their selectors, issued by the client’s binding_issuer. A client sees only its own Users, the ones whose key its binding_issuer issues: every other id is 404 and absent from every list, as is a PERSON without a live professional ROLE. The userName index spans every client, so a 409 uniqueness tells one client that a userName exists under another; externalId is unique within one client. Every SCIM request is an access record of the client, with the PERSON as its object.

A User is changed and removed through these operations:

  • PUT /scim/v2/Users/{id} replaces the User (RFC 7644 §3.5.1). A mapped attribute the body leaves out is cleared; the binding key and externalId are kept, and a left-out active keeps the lifecycle state.
  • PATCH /scim/v2/Users/{id} applies the RFC 7644 §3.5.2 operations, value paths and a replace without path included, and commits the result as one version. The operation is read in any case, as the Entra ID client sends Replace.
  • DELETE /scim/v2/Users/{id} logically deletes the PERSON and its professional ROLE in one demographic CONTRIBUTION and answers 204. Every later request on the id is 404, the User leaves every list, and a new User may take its userName. The binding key stays behind as a tombstone: a login on it is refused as deprovisioned until the owning client creates a User with it again.

Each write answers with the User and its new ETag. An If-Match naming another version is 412, a changed binding key is 400 mutability, and a write without If-Match is accepted (RFC 7644 §3.14 makes entity tags a MAY). active drives the lifecycle state of the PERSON (RM common §Version Lifecycle):

Current stateactive in the requestResult
complete or incompletetrue or left outcomplete when the template holds in full, else incomplete
completefalseinactive
incompletefalseabandoned
inactivetruecomplete, or incomplete when the template does not hold
abandonedtrueincomplete, then complete in a second version when the template holds
inactive or abandonedfalse or left out, with a change400 invalidValue: reactivate the User first
inactive or abandonedfalse or left out, without a change200, no new version

An inactive or abandoned User is still read and found by a filter, so its client can reactivate it. When the second version of an abandoned User fails, the User stays incomplete and the same request completes it.

The versions of a deleted User are kept for the record-keeping duties that need the professional’s identification (GDPR Art. 6(1)(c), laid down in law as Art. 6(3) requires: in the Netherlands BW 7:454(3), twenty years, and the logging duty of the Besluit elektronische gegevensverwerking door zorgaanbieders). Outside the Netherlands, name your national retention provision. Enable the identity provider’s protection against accidental deletions beside max_deactivations.

Only the attribution minimum waits for that horizon: the name, the binding key and the identifiers, userName and externalId among them. The contacts serve no attribution, so FerroEHR erases them (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e)): with auth.scim.contact_erasure_delay = 0 the deletion removes the contacts of every version of the PERSON in the same transaction, and with a period a sweep that runs every minute removes them once the period has passed. The sweep reaches every deleted PERSON whose binding key a [[auth.scim.client]] issues, an administrator’s demographic DELETE included. Each version keeps its uid, audit and contribution, and its node rows are derived again from the erased body. A server signature on such a version is removed, because it was taken over the content the erasure changed. Each erasure is an access record, a delete of party:<id>#contacts. A login on the key is still refused as deprovisioned.

Groups

When [authz.party_binding.group] names a display_name and [authz.party_binding.membership] is set, /scim/v2/Groups is served beside /Users, and /scim/v2/ResourceTypes lists the Group. A Group is a demographic GROUP of the group template:

  • its displayName is the GROUP’s PARTY_IDENTITY, unique across the live Groups after case folding, so a duplicate is 409 uniqueness;
  • its externalId is a DV_IDENTIFIER at the external_id selector under the group_identifier_issuer of the [[auth.party]] table whose identifier_issuer is the client’s binding_issuer, so the group claim of that issuer’s tokens matches it. ferroehr config check refuses a client whose table sets no group_identifier_issuer;
  • each member holds one inline PARTY_RELATIONSHIP of the membership archetype, with its PERSON as source and the GROUP as target, stored in the member’s own version (RM demographic §Party Relationships). No ROLE is created for a Group, and a PERSON in no Group has relationships Void.

A Group belongs to the client that created it; every other client gets 404. A member is a User of the same client: a member naming another client’s User, an unknown id or a Group (nested Groups are not supported) is 400 invalidValue. What a Group allows stays with the token’s scopes and roles; the access record lists the Groups the token names that the person belongs to, and a Group in inactive or abandoned lists no member.

  • POST /scim/v2/Groups creates the GROUP with its members, if any, and answers 201 with the Group, its Location and ETag.
  • GET /scim/v2/Groups/{id} and GET /scim/v2/Groups filter with eq and and over displayName, externalId and id, and excludedAttributes=members leaves the members out. Each member is served with its value, $ref and type.
  • PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/{id} answers 204 with the new ETag (RFC 7644 §3.5.2). add of members adds the listed members; remove with the filter members[value eq "<id>"] removes that member, and remove of members with neither a filter nor a value list removes them all.
  • PUT /scim/v2/Groups/{id} replaces the displayName and the members, keeps a left-out externalId, and answers 200 with the Group.
  • DELETE /scim/v2/Groups/{id} logically deletes the GROUP with its memberships, and every later request on the id is 404.

Entra compatibility deviation. A remove of members that carries a value list removes only the listed members, the request Microsoft Entra ID sends. RFC 7644 §3.5.2.2 removes “the attribute and all values” when no filter is specified; FerroEHR follows Entra only when the value list is present.

A membership change is a new version of each member’s PERSON it touches, in one CONTRIBUTION, and the GROUP gets no version; a change costs the same whatever the Group’s size. The Group’s ETag is its GROUP version with a membership revision that moves with every membership change, so it changes whenever its members do (RFC 7644 §3.14). The member User’s ETag changes too, since its PERSON holds the membership (RFC 7643 §4.1.2); its body does not, because the User serves no groups attribute. Deleting a User deletes the memberships its PERSON holds with it. Deleting a Group drops the membership of each active member in the CONTRIBUTION that deletes the GROUP. A GROUP an administrator set inactive or abandoned keeps its version, since the version lifecycle draws no update of either state, and a SCIM write to such a Group is 400 invalidValue.

Deactivated Users leave their Groups. The version lifecycle draws no update of an inactive or abandoned PERSON (RM common master06 §Version Lifecycle), so such a PERSON cannot take a membership change, and an inactive PERSON binds to nothing. Setting a User’s active to false therefore drops all its memberships in the same version, and each Group’s ETag changes. Microsoft Entra ID often disables a user and then removes it from its groups; the later remove finds nothing to remove and answers 204. An add naming an inactive or abandoned User is 400 invalidValue (“reactivate the User first”). A reactivated User belongs to no Group until its client adds it again.

Provision from Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID provisions through a non-gallery enterprise application. FerroEHR validates the access token your own authorization server issues to it, so the steps split between the two.

  1. Map the person template. Give the default [[authz.party_binding.person.template]] a user_name and an external_id selector, and map the attributes Entra sends, for example:

    [[authz.party_binding.person.attribute]]
scim = "name.formatted"
name = true
path = { "FerroEHR professional" = "/identities[at0002]/details[at0003]/items[at0004]" }

[[authz.party_binding.person.attribute]]
scim = 'emails[type eq "work"].value'
path = { "FerroEHR professional" = "/contacts[at0005]/addresses[at0006]/details[at0007]/items[at0008]" }

    A value path such as emails[type eq "work"].value serves the value and its type. FerroEHR holds one value per type and no preference among them, so /scim/v2/Schemas declares primary read-only and the primary Entra sends is ignored (RFC 7644 §3.3).

  2. Declare the client. Add a [[auth.scim.client]] whose issuer is your authorization server, an [[auth.issuer]] of kind machines, and whose binding_issuer is the identifier_issuer of the [[auth.party]] your professionals log in through. Set public_base_url to the origin Entra reaches. In the Helm chart, config.the [auth.scim] table: true also adds the /scim/v2 path to the Ingress. ferroehr config check refuses a mapping the endpoint cannot serve.

  3. Federate Entra’s credential at your authorization server. Entra’s Workload Identity Federation presents a signed assertion, which your authorization server exchanges for a client-credentials access token (RFC 7523 §2.2). These checks are your authorization server’s, not FerroEHR’s, so verify each one there, as Microsoft’s “Workload Identity Federation for SCIM Provisioning” guide requires:

    • iss is pinned to your full tenant issuer, https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0, and the assertion verifies against that tenant’s key set.
    • aud is pinned to api://<workload-identity-app-id>, with one workload-identity application per FerroEHR deployment.
    • azp is pinned to the application id of Microsoft’s provisioning service.
    • uti is cached for the lifetime of the assertion, and an assertion whose uti was seen before is refused as a replay.
    • The access token it issues holds the client’s scope, names the client in client_id, and lives between 1 and 6 hours, the range Microsoft’s guide asks for.

    The assertion’s sub is the object id of a Microsoft application that every integration in the tenant shares, never your client_id, so it does not meet RFC 7523 §3 item 2.B. Accepting it is a deviation of your authorization server; record it there. Leaving Entra’s Secret Token blank, so that Entra uses its own token, is not supported: Microsoft reserves it for testing, and every non-gallery application in the tenant receives a token with the same iss and aud (RFC 9700 §2.3). A long-lived bearer token is not supported either.

  4. Point Entra at FerroEHR. Set the Tenant URL to <public_base_url>/scim/v2 and run Test Connection. Entra queries /Users with filter=externalId eq "<random guid>", which FerroEHR answers with an empty ListResponse, and fetches a random User and a random Group, each answered 404.

  5. Map the attributes in Entra. Map userName, externalId, active and the attributes of step 1. Map the attribute that carries the professional’s login identifier to urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:ferrohealth:2.0:User:loginIdentifier; Entra sends it without listing the extension in schemas, which FerroEHR accepts. An attribute the person template does not map is refused as undefined, so remove the rest of Entra’s default mappings.

  6. Protect against mass deactivation. Turn on Entra’s accidental deletions prevention, with a threshold at or below max_deactivations.

  7. Provision groups. Map the group’s objectId to its externalId, so the object ids Entra puts in the groups claim match, and provision only the groups assigned to the application, which keeps a person’s token under the groups overage limit. Entra creates each Group with no member, reads it with excludedAttributes=members, finds it by displayName, and adds and removes members with PATCH.

Entra writes Replace and Add with a capital letter, disables a User with active = false, sends DELETE once the user is removed, and never sends a null. A value cleared in Entra therefore stays in FerroEHR until the User is replaced or deleted, or an administrator removes it.

[privacy.access_delay]

The EHDS Art. 3(3) delay of the person’s own access to newly registered data, a Member State option: write the table only where your Member State’s rule provides for the delay; its presence turns the delay on. What it does is on delayed access by the person.

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
categorieslist of string[]The categories held at creation, named as [audit.categories] names one: a priority category of Art. 14(1) by its code (Laboratory-Reports, Medical-Imaging, …) or as `
max_delaydurationrequiredThe limit of a hold, a whole number of hours from "1h" to "8784h" (one year): new compositions of the listed categories are held from patient-context requests until a professional releases them or it passes. Absent, the person’s access is immediate (Art. 3(1)), every hold already placed stops withholding, and the admin route refuses a new hold with 400. It is the length of a hold placed at creation and the latest end a professional may give one. Art. 3(3) allows the delay “for a limited period of time” only; the period is the Member State’s to set.
 
[privacy.access_delay]
categories = ["Laboratory-Reports", "Medical-Imaging"]
max_delay = "7d"

The environment forms are FERROEHR__PRIVACY__ACCESS_DELAY__CATEGORIES (comma-separated) and FERROEHR__PRIVACY__ACCESS_DELAY__MAX_DELAY.

[auth.smart]

The SMART on openEHR scopes are enforced on every route whenever [auth] is on: each operation carries a requirement from FerroEHR’s route table, which the ferrohealth-smart crate checks against the token’s scopes or a Basic user’s scopes. There is no switch for it. This section decides what beside the route table: whether the discovery document is served, and whose grants count for what. See SMART App Launch.

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
discoveryboolfalseServe /.well-known/smart-configuration. It is built from the metadata of one [auth] issuer (the first introspected [auth] issuer, else the issuer [auth.smart] issuer_metadata_file names, else the first issuer whose metadata is read from it, else the first issuer), so it needs an issuer whose metadata names a token_endpoint (SMART App Launch 2.2.0, Conformance, §Metadata); an issuer read from a jwks_file refuses the start with discovery = true unless issuer_metadata_file supplies that metadata.
issuer_metadata_filepathunsetA JSON file holding the RFC 8414 §2 metadata of the [auth] issuer it names, whose key set is a jwks_file, read at boot. It must name an [auth] issuer, wherever it stands in the list, repeat no member name, and every endpoint it names must be https (a loopback host excepted); the discovery document takes its token_endpoint and the other endpoints from it. Set for an issuer whose metadata is read from the issuer, it is a boot error.
platform_base_urlstringunset ⇒ the REST rootThe path the discovery document hangs off, e.g. /gateway/v1.
public_base_urlstringrequired with discoveryThe server’s externally reachable origin (e.g. https://cdr.example.com), from which the discovery document’s absolute services.*.baseUrl values are built.
episode_launchboolfalseAdvertise episode context and accept the launch/episode scope and episodeId claim; applies no episode-scoped filtering.
backend_clientslist of string[]The client_ids a system/aql-* grant counts for: such a grant “would grant access to all registered and ad-hoc AQL queries system-wide” (master08 §Resource Scopes).
patient_issuerslist of string[]The issuers whose patient/ grants count, each confined to the EHR the token’s ehrId claim names (master07 §Context Selection). Empty, a patient/ grant grants nothing.
demographic_clientslist of string[]The bearer client_ids that reach the DEMOGRAPHIC API, which no SMART on openEHR scope covers. A Basic user-id never matches an entry. A caller holding [auth] product_scope reaches it too.

The launch-base64-json capability (master09) is advertised by listing it in [auth] capabilities; the base64 JSON launch object is the application’s to consume. The table is always read, since its lists apply whether or not the document is served; discovery alone turns the document on.

No smart URL may carry a user name or password, whether or not the document is served: the discovery document publishes these URLs to every application, so a credential in one would be served to anyone who asks.

[management]

The ops-introspection surface: build info, Prometheus, metric views, the effective configuration, runtime log control, and the on-demand profiler. Off by default, and every endpoint off individually.

The health probes are not configured here: /health, /health/liveness and /health/readiness are always served on the main API port without authentication, whatever this section says (see Operations → Health probes).

[management]
enabled = false
base_path = "/management"

[management.endpoints]
info = "off"
metrics = "off"
prometheus = "off"
env = "off"
loggers = "off"
flamegraph = "off"

[management.profiling]
max_duration = "30s"
max_frequency = 999
KeyTypeDefaultDescription
enabledboolfalseMount the management router.
base_pathstring/managementBase path for the management endpoints.
portintunset ⇒ share the main listenerServe management on its own listener and port. Must differ from the server.listen port, and it is plain HTTP, an internal surface.
flame_filepathunsetSpan-timing capture: write the folded stacks of every span to this file, and render offline with inferno-flamegraph. Unset, the layer is not installed. For diagnostic sessions: the file grows with span traffic.

[management.endpoints]: info, metrics, prometheus, env, loggers and flamegraph, each enum{off,admin_only,private,public}, default off.

LevelMeaning
offNot mounted at all; the route answers 404.
admin_onlyRequires an authenticated principal carrying authz.rbac.admin_role (401 unauthenticated, 403 authenticated but not admin).
privateRequires any authenticated principal.
publicServed outside authentication.

env renders the effective configuration and flamegraph starts a profiler on request, so the boot log prints exactly which endpoints a configuration turned on and at which level.

[management.profiling]: limits for the on-demand CPU flamegraph behind endpoints.flamegraph (see Operations → Profiling):

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
max_durationduration"30s"Longest sample window one request may ask for, in whole seconds. A request asking for more is refused with 400, never clamped.
max_frequencyint999Highest sampling frequency (Hz) a request may ask for. Same refusal semantics.

Warning

probes_enabled and endpoints.health do not exist. Configuration is strict, so a file or environment variable still setting either one fails at boot with an unknown-key error: delete the key; the probes are always on.

[deployment]

The commercial licence token. Every build embeds the licensor’s non-commercial grant; a deployment that holds a commercial licence installs its token here. The server behaves identically under either grant and reports the one in force on GET /management/status (licence.use, licence.licensee, licence.not_after, licence.configured_token). See Licensing & legal.

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
licence_filepathunsetThe licence token the licensor issued. A token that cannot be read or does not verify is reported as refused on /management/status; the embedded grant stays in force.

[record.signing]

VERSION signing. On by default in digest mode, with read-time verification of the server’s own signatures strict by default.

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
enabledbooltrueServer-side signing of committed versions.
modeenum{digest,pgp}digestA SHA-256 integrity digest, or an OpenPGP (RFC 4880) detached signature.
key_filepathunsetArmored secret key; required for pgp (a boot error otherwise).
key_passphrase / key_passphrase_filesecret / pathunsetKey passphrase. At most one of the pair.
retired_key_fileslist of path[]Armored public keys retired from signing and kept for verification, so versions signed before a key rotation keep verifying.
verify_on_readenum{off,warn,strict}unset ⇒ strict when signing is enabledRead-time recompute-and-compare policy for the server’s own signatures.

retired_key_files exists because a stored VERSION.signature records no key identifier and is an immutable committed fact that cannot be re-issued; keeping the retired public key is the only way history stays verifiable across a rotation, and a public key can verify but never sign. Its environment form takes a comma-separated list (FERROEHR__RECORD__SIGNING__RETIRED_KEY_FILES=/keys/a.pub.asc,/keys/b.pub.asc).

Note

verify_on_read resolves to strict when signing is enabled. On every read the server recomputes the signature of a version it signed and, on a mismatch, returns a 500 integrity fault rather than silently serving a provably corrupt record. Set it explicitly to warn (log + meter version_signature_invalid_total, still serve) or off (never check). Client-supplied signatures (an author’s own, or one carried by an imported version) are always stored verbatim and never re-verified, whatever this setting says, because the author may have signed a different agreed serialization.

Warning

pgp mode fails closed at boot if the key is missing or unusable: the server will not start. Verify the key and passphrase before switching modes.

Choose an Ed25519 signing key

The server refuses an ECDSA (P-256, P-384, P-521, secp256k1, Brainpool) or Ed448 signing key at boot: their private-key arithmetic runs on crypto-bigint 0.5, whose constant-time operations can branch on secret values (RUSTSEC-2026-0387), with no fixed release on that line. The boot error names the advisory. Move to Ed25519 with the steps below; the old certificate goes in retired_key_files, where it keeps verifying, because verification uses only public values.

An RSA signing key is accepted, but it makes every commit perform an RSA private-key operation, the operation the Marvin timing sidechannel concerns (RUSTSEC-2023-0071 / CVE-2023-49092), for which the underlying rsa crate has no fixed release. An Ed25519 key keeps that code off the signing path entirely.

The server does not refuse an RSA key: a repository whose history is already RSA-signed needs that key to keep verifying, and signatures are immutable committed facts that cannot be re-issued. Instead it logs a warning at boot naming the advisory. To clear it:

  1. Generate a new signing key: gpg --quick-generate-key "…" ed25519 sign, and export the armored secret key to key_file.
  2. Export the public half of the old certificate and add it to retired_key_files, so versions signed with it still verify (see above).
  3. Restart. New versions are signed with Ed25519; old ones keep verifying.

Rotation inside one certificate is cheaper still: add an Ed25519 signing subkey to the existing certificate, export the armored secret key again to key_file, and restart. The server signs with the newest subkey whose binding grants signing and that is neither expired nor revoked (the rule), with no retired_key_files entry needed: the certificate keeps the previous subkey, so past signatures continue to verify. For a refused ECDSA or Ed448 key this works when the new Ed25519 subkey is the one chosen. The steps above, with a new certificate, work in every case.

On Kubernetes, digest mode needs nothing; it is the default. pgp mode needs the key as a file and its passphrase as a secret, both of which the chart mounts for you:

# values.yaml
config:
  signing:
    enabled: true
    mode: pgp
    key_file: /etc/ferroehr/signing-key.asc
  files:
    signing-key.asc: |
      -----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----
      …
secrets:
  signingKeyPassphrase: "…"

Every config.files key becomes /etc/ferroehr/<key>, mounted read-only from a chart Secret at mode 0440, and that volume holds the private key, so it is never world-readable inside the container. To go back to digest, set mode: digest and drop the key material; versions already signed keep their signatures and still verify.

[record.versioning]

What a commit stores is not a setting: a version whose content equals the current version’s is committed like any other, with its own commit audit, contribution, version id and ETag, and the content is stored once (the new version reads its predecessor’s node rows). The one setting here is the answer to a repeated send of the same content.

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
record.versioning.idempotent_resendboolfalseWhen true, a PUT whose content equals the current version’s commits nothing and answers like a successful update with the existing version: 200 (or 204 under Prefer: return=minimal), and that version’s ETag and Location.

Turn it on only for the integration that needs it: with the rule on, the repeated send leaves no commit audit and no contribution, so the version history does not record that the content was confirmed again, where the default records every committal as the RM asks (RM common master06 §Committal and Audits). What the repeated send does leave is one record on the access log ([audit]), operation resend, naming the version the content matched and its content digest (<version uid>#sha256:<digest>), the committer and the time: the entry Cadasto writes for a skipped send, which says the last version was saved one more time. The content is matched against the current version only, the one If-Match names; content equal to an earlier version’s is committed as a new version. The openEHR REST API does not govern skipping an identical commit; the answer is FerroEHR’s own, chosen to match what a client sees from Cadasto.

[record.versioning]
idempotent_resend = true

Integrations

Query execution, the patient identity source and the three optional integrations: [record.query], [pixm], [record.change_feed], [terminology], [record.multimedia]. Everything except the query knobs and the identity source is off by default, and a disabled integration contacts nothing and mounts no routes. Precedence, the environment-name grammar, and file discovery are on the Configuration reference index.

  • [record.query]
  • [pixm]
  • [record.change_feed]
  • [terminology]
    • The endpoint table
    • Archetype value-set bindings at commit
  • [record.multimedia]

[record.query]

AQL execution bounds.

[record.query]
plan_cache_capacity = 256
timeout = "30s"
max_result_rows = 10000
KeyTypeDefaultDescription
plan_cache_capacityint256Maximum distinct cached query plans; 0 disables the cache and every lookup runs the full parse-and-lower path. Cache activity is reported by the aql_plan_cache_events counter.
timeoutduration"30s"Per-query database execution budget; "0s" disables it. Overrun is refused 408.
max_result_rowsint10000The largest page one query execution serves: the page of a query nothing else bounds, and the maximum an explicit LIMIT or fetch may ask for (a larger page is refused 400); 0 means unbounded.

timeout is on by default, and deliberately tighter than database.statement_timeout. Keeping this budget the tighter of the two means an overrun surfaces as the engine’s own typed 408 rather than a driver error. When it fires, or when the client disconnects or the HTTP request timeout gives up first, the query’s connection is closed instead of returned to the pool, so its pool slot frees at once and PostgreSQL stops the statement within about a second (the session’s client_connection_check_interval).

max_result_rows is the largest page one execution serves. Without it, SELECT c FROM COMPOSITION c with no fetch generates SQL with no LIMIT and materialises every matching row: one request, unbounded allocation. A query that nothing else bounds takes the ceiling as its page. An explicit AQL LIMIT or a fetch parameter is honoured as written up to the ceiling; a page larger than the ceiling is refused with 400 naming the ceiling. The refusal is deliberate: a silently shortened page would let a client that pages with its own fetch as the stride skip the rows between the shortened page and its next offset, and the RESULT_SET has nothing to say so. ITS-REST leaves both the fetch default and its maximum to the implementation. A bulk consumer pages with offset and a fetch at or below the ceiling, or the operator raises the ceiling deliberately.

[pixm]

Who translates a patient identifier into the clinical domain, so the EHR that records the patient can be found (the EHR index). The EHR itself always says whose record it is: its EHR_STATUS.subject.external_ref names the subject, and FerroEHR finds a subject’s EHR by matching that reference, which it keeps indexed beside the EHR on every EHR create and EHR_STATUS update. No openEHR specification governs where the patient’s other identifiers live: the RM’s PARTY_SELF section says the association “may be done elsewhere for security reasons”, and FerroEHR’s design puts it in an IHE patient identity source.

record.subject_index = "pixm" asks an IHE patient identity source. FerroEHR asks a PIX Manager, as a PIXm Patient Identifier Cross-reference Consumer (IHE ITI TF-2 §3.83, $ihe-pix), which identifier the clinical domain holds for a patient that another domain’s identifier names. That identifier is the pseudonym EHR_STATUS.subject carries. FerroEHR sends only what ITI-83 specifies, so any conformant PIX Manager serves; FerroPIX is the one the compose quickstart and the Helm chart run.

subject_index = "local", with no identity source, is the other supported posture, for production as much as for development, tests and the conformance suites: the subject-id and subject-namespace model. A client names a patient in EHR_STATUS.subject.external_ref by any namespace and identifier (benchmark / 1793131381), as OBJECT_REF.namespace and a local GENERIC_ID.scheme allow, and a subject resolves to itself: the openEHR REST API’s GET /ehr?subject_id=…&subject_namespace=… lookup and a cohort that names its subjects both find the EHR whose EHR_STATUS names the subject, matching namespace and identifier exactly. An EHR created over POST /ehr or PUT /ehr/{ehr_id} is found from the moment it is created, and an EHR_STATUS update that changes the subject moves it. The key has no default: unset, the server refuses to start and the refusal names both choices.

What the local posture means for pseudonymisation: with no [privacy] subject_namespaces declared, the server stores a subject reference as the client sends it, a real identifier included. Pseudonymisation then belongs to the client, or to the demographic service the reference points at (GDPR Art. 4(5)). There is no mixed mode: a deployment that declares pseudonym namespaces keeps the rule in force under local too, so every subject reference must name a declared namespace and carry a UUID, and no other namespace is accepted beside them. A production deployment runs the subject-id posture by accepting the open_subject_namespace gap by name (deployment.profile), which boot and GET /management/status then state.

subject_index alone switches the index, in the file or as FERROEHR__RECORD__SUBJECT_INDEX. A [pixm] table kept beside "local" is not used, and boot names its keys, so a configuration written for the IHE source runs locally with FERROEHR__RECORD__SUBJECT_INDEX=local and no other change; its declared pseudonym namespaces stay in force. The compose quickstart selects its local configuration with one variable (The local EHR index).

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
record.subject_indexenum{pixm,local}requiredWho translates a subject into the clinical domain.
pixm.assigning_authorityURIrequired for pixmThe clinical domain, such as urn:oid:2.999.7.1: the targetSystem of every ITI-83 query and the namespace the answered pseudonym is stored under. It must be one of privacy.subject_namespaces.
pixm.methodenum{post,get}postpost sends a Parameters body, so a patient identifier never appears in a URL or an access log; get is the form ITI-83 prescribes, for a PIX Manager that accepts no POST.
pixm.endpointendpoint tablerequired for pixmThe PIX Manager: url, its FHIR base ([base] of [base]/Patient/$ihe-pix), timeout for one ITI-83 exchange with its tries and the waits between them, the retry of an exchange that got no answer or a 5xx, the TLS and the credential.
 
[privacy]
subject_namespaces = ["urn:oid:2.999.7.1"]

[record]
subject_index = "pixm"

[pixm]
assigning_authority = "urn:oid:2.999.7.1"

[pixm.endpoint]
url = "https://pix.example.org/fhir"

[pixm.endpoint.credentials.oauth]
token_endpoint = "https://idp.example.org/realms/pix/protocol/openid-connect/token"
client_id = "ferroehr"
client_secret_file = "/run/secrets/pix-client"
scope = "system/Patient.rs"

[pixm.endpoint.credentials.oauth] is the client credentials grant every ITI-83 request carries, with the grant’s keys; a 401 is answered once more under a new token. The client id is the one the identity source mints pseudonyms in the clinical domain for, and the scope is the one its PIX Manager takes from a Consumer. [pixm.endpoint.tls] holds the client’s TLS material for a PIX Manager behind a private PKI or one that asks for mutual TLS.

How a subject a cohort names is resolved:

StepUnder iheUnder local
the subject in the clinical domainits clinical pseudonym, asked of the source; a subject already in the clinical domain names itselfthe subject as given
the EHR of that subjectthe one EHR whose EHR_STATUS names itthe one EHR whose EHR_STATUS names it

The source is never asked to resolve a pseudonym back to another domain’s identifier.

No fallback. At start the server reads the source’s CapabilityStatement and refuses to start when it does not answer. A request the source then fails, refuses or times out on answers with an error that carries what the source said, and nothing is answered from the EHR_STATUS subject instead. An answered pseudonym the [privacy] subject rule refuses, or more than one identifier in the clinical domain, is refused too.

FerroEHR does no identity work in either mode. It matches no patients, merges none and links no identifier domains; the identity source does. It asks only for the cross-reference ITI-83 answers. PDQm (ITI-78) is not used: its search answers with the demographic Patient, which FerroEHR would only discard, so asking for it breaks data minimisation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)), and its $match is patient matching.

[record.change_feed]

The commit-event outbox and its cursor feed. Off until a reader is named; the envelopes are PHI-free by design. The feed, its routes and its scope are on Change events (outbox feed).

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
readerslist of strings[]The readers of the feed, each matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$. With none, no commit writes an outbox row. Boot registers each one and marks every reader the list no longer names inactive, so it holds the prune back no longer.
retentionduration"7d"How long an acknowledged row is kept after its commit; at least a second.
prune_intervalduration"1h"How often the retention prune runs; never "0s".

[terminology]

The one FHIR terminology server the CDR asks; the table’s presence turns it on. The terminology extension API is api.terminology (bool, false).

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
endpointendpoint tablerequiredThe server: url, its FHIR R4B base URL (for FerroTERM http://ferroterm:8080/r4b; a [terminology] table without it is a boot error), timeout for one call, the retry of a call that got no answer or a 5xx, the TLS and the credential.
on_errorenum{accept,refuse}acceptWhat an unresolvable binding does to a commit: accept accepts it (fail-open), refuse rejects it.

Every key is a scalar, so the whole section is reachable through the environment: FERROEHR__TERMINOLOGY__ENDPOINT__URL, FERROEHR__TERMINOLOGY__ON_ERROR, FERROEHR__TERMINOLOGY__ENDPOINT__TIMEOUT.

[terminology]
on_error = "accept"

[terminology.endpoint]
url = "http://ferroterm:8080/r4b"

The server answers every terminology the bundled openEHR terminology does not carry: the /terminology/* extension API, AQL TERMINOLOGY(…) resolution, the ADL 2 binding check and the composition-commit binding checks below. A response that is not a valid FHIR R4B Parameters or ValueSet resource (for example an $expand result missing the required ValueSet.status or expansion.timestamp) is treated as an upstream fault rather than partially read, so it takes the same path as an unreachable server and on_error decides what the commit does.

Note

The terminology server needs the fhir build feature, which is on in the published binary and container images. A binary built with --no-default-features refuses at startup if [terminology] is configured; the in-process openEHR terminology bundle remains available.

The endpoint table

Every outbound HTTP integration, [terminology.endpoint], [pixm.endpoint], [audit.fhir_feed.endpoint] and [authz.abac.remote.endpoint], is the FerroHEALTH family’s one endpoint table, so an operator writes the same keys for each integration of each product. Each integration’s client is built from it by ferrohealth-smart’s outbound client, the one every product of the family uses.

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
urlURLrequiredThe service’s base URL. Credentials embedded in it are masked in every rendering, and a credential here beside one in credentials is a boot error: the service would receive two authorizations.
timeoutduration"10s"How long one whole call may take; never zero.
connect_timeoutdurationunsetHow long opening the connection may take; unset, only timeout bounds it.
retrytablethree attempts, a fifth of a second doubling to five secondsHow a call that got no answer, or a 5xx, is tried again: max_attempts (3) counts the first try, so 1 never retries; the wait starts at initial_backoff and doubles up to max_backoff ("5s"). A refusal the service answered on purpose is never retried.
tlstableplatform rootsThe family’s outbound TLS table: trust_roots_file, a PEM bundle trusted beside the platform’s roots for a service behind a private PKI; client_identity_file (or client_identity inline), one PEM holding the client certificate chain and its key for mutual TLS; and min_version ("1.3", or "1.2").
credentialstablenoneWhat every call carries: HTTP Basic (user with password or password_file) or the OAuth2 client-credentials grant [...credentials.oauth], never both.

The grant’s access token is cached and re-requested shortly before it expires, and a call the service answers with 401 is sent once more under a new token. Its keys:

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
token_endpointURLone of token_endpoint and issuerThe OAuth2 token endpoint. Credentials embedded in it are masked in every rendering.
issuerstringone of token_endpoint and issuerThe issuer whose metadata names the token endpoint (RFC 8414).
client_idstringrequiredThe registered client identifier. Empty is a boot error.
client_secret / client_secret_filesecret / pathone is requiredThe client secret, inline or read from a mounted file.
client_authenum{client_secret_basic,client_secret_post,private_key_jwt,tls_client_auth,self_signed_tls_client_auth}client_secret_basicHow the client authenticates at the token endpoint.
scopestringunsetThe scope request parameter.
audiencestringunsetThe audience request parameter some authorization servers read.
resourceURLunsetThe RFC 8707 resource request parameter.
private_key_filepathunsetThe PEM private key that signs the client assertion under private_key_jwt (RFC 7523).
kidstringthe RFC 7638 thumbprintThe kid the client assertion names.
assertion_algstringby key typeThe algorithm the client assertion is signed with.
assertion_audienceenum{token_endpoint,issuer}token_endpointThe aud of the client assertion; issuer needs issuer set.
tlstableplatform rootsThe token endpoint’s own TLS table, with the keys above.
refresh_marginduration"30s"How long before the token expires a new one is fetched.
timeoutduration"10s"How long one call to the authorization server may take.
 
[terminology.endpoint.credentials.oauth]
token_endpoint = "https://idp.example.org/realms/ts/protocol/openid-connect/token"
client_id = "ferroehr-cdr"
client_secret_file = "/run/secrets/ts-client"
scope = "system/*.read"

Archetype value-set bindings at commit

With [terminology] enabled, committing a COMPOSITION also resolves the archetype constraint bindings its template declares: where a template binds an ac code to an external terminology query, the coded value in the composition must be a member of the value set that query returns.

  • The code is in the value set → the commit proceeds.
  • The code is not in the value set → 422 naming the path, the code, and the bound query. That is a real constraint violation, not a service failure, so on_error does not change it.
  • The value set could not be resolved (server down, error response, unknown value set) → on_error decides: false (the default) accepts the commit and logs a warning; true rejects it with 422.

With [terminology] disabled (the default) no binding is resolved and no request is made, so commit behaviour is exactly as if this section did not exist.

Note

The composition’s terminology_id is sent verbatim as the FHIR system parameter, and no openEHR specification defines a mapping between terminology_id values (SNOMED-CT) and FHIR system URIs (http://snomed.info/sct). If your archetypes and your terminology server disagree, align them in the terminology-server configuration; the CDR does not rewrite the value.

[record.multimedia]

DV_MULTIMEDIA externalization to an S3-compatible object store. Off by default: blobs stay inline, byte-identical, and no object store is built or contacted. The table keeps enabled where other optional features use the table’s presence, because url applies while it is off: the blobs already offloaded are read back from it.

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
enabledboolfalseExternalize large multimedia data.
thresholdsize"256KiB"Decoded size strictly above which data is offloaded; at or below it stays inline.
urlsecret URLunset ⇒ default AWS endpoint resolutionS3-compatible endpoint. Must be an absolute http/https URL when set; an http:// URL is plain HTTP, development only, which production names as the plaintext_object_store gap. Credentials embedded in it are redacted from every rendering.
bucketstringopenehr-multimediaTarget bucket for content-addressed blobs.
regionstringus-east-1AWS region; S3 requires one even for non-AWS endpoints.
access_key_idstringunsetS3 access key id. Unset, with no secret key either, runs the client anonymously.
secret_access_key / secret_access_key_filesecret / pathunsetS3 secret access key. At most one of the pair.

An enabled integration whose url is set but blank, not an absolute URL, or carries a scheme other than http/https is a boot error. That case is easy to reach by accident (an unset Compose variable expanding to nothing, or an empty Helm value) and used to boot cleanly and then fail on the first multimedia commit, so it is refused where an operator can still act on it.

Warning

Offloaded blobs are PHI. The bucket must be private and encrypted, and reached over HTTPS. Multimedia externalization also needs the multimedia build feature (on in the published binary and container images); a slim build refuses at startup rather than silently keeping blobs inline.

Audit

The IHE ATNA audit trail: [audit] and its three sinks. Precedence, the environment-name grammar, and file discovery are on the Configuration reference index.

  • [audit]
    • [audit.store]: the local Audit Record Repository
    • [audit.categories]
    • [[authz.origin]]: the origins a deployment recognises
    • [audit.syslog]: the classic DICOM/syslog feed (ITI-20)
    • [audit.fhir_feed]: the RESTful-ATNA feed (ITI-20 ATX:FHIR Feed)
      • Authenticating the feed

[audit]

The IHE ATNA audit trail (see the Audit trail chapter for what a record contains and how to search it). On by default with only the local store active: every deployment gets a queryable audit trail with nothing leaving the node, and forwarding to an external Audit Record Repository is opt-in per sink.

[audit]
enabled = true
source_id = "ferroehr"
value_if_missing = "UNKNOWN"
suppress_login_events = true
fail_mode = "open"
resolve_subject = true
queue_capacity = 8192
purpose_header = "x-purpose-of-use"
permit_header = "x-data-permit"
purpose_codes = []
emergency_purpose_codes = []
KeyTypeDefaultDescription
enabledbooltrueMaster audit switch.
enterprise_site_idstringunsetThe AuditEnterpriseSiteID field.
source_idstringferroehrThe audit source id, also used for the destination participant.
value_if_missingstringUNKNOWNFill value for empty mandatory fields.
suppress_login_eventsbooltrueSkip successful-login records. Rejected accesses (401/403) are always recorded.
fail_modeenum{open,closed}openWhat an undeliverable audit record does. open logs, meters and lets the request succeed; closed rejects auditable operations with 503 (including when the local store has stopped accepting writes) so no PHI access goes un-audited.
resolve_subjectbooltrueEnrich the patient participant with a background lookup of the EHR’s subject. The lookup runs on the background drain, never on the request path; the IHE BALP patient patterns and the patient-centric audit search need the subject.
queue_capacityint8192Bounded audit queue capacity. Sized for write-path bursts: the drain persists in multi-row batches, so the queue only needs to ride out sink latency spikes.
server_hoststringunset ⇒ the value_if_missing fillThis node’s advertised network address, reported as the destination NetworkAccessPointID.
purpose_headerstringx-purpose-of-useThe request header a caller declares its purpose of use in, recorded on every access record. NEN 7513 asks on whose authority a record was read and EHDS Art. 9 asks why; neither is derivable from the request, so the caller declares it. IHE carries the equivalent in a SAML attribute rather than a header, so the header is FerroEHR’s own. An issuer with an [[auth.attributes]] table states the purposes in its token, and a header naming another purpose is refused (where the purpose comes from).
permit_headerstringx-data-permitThe request header a secondary-use caller declares the data permit it acts under in (EHDS Art. 68), recorded on every access record as permit. The value is the permit’s identifier, 1 to 128 characters of letters, digits and . _ : / # -; any other value is recorded as absent. No specification names a header for it, so the header is FerroEHR’s own. See Secondary use.
purpose_codeslist of string[]The purpose codes this deployment accepts. Empty records whatever the caller declares. A non-empty list records a declared code only when it is on the list, so an unagreed string does not sit in the trail reading like an established purpose.
emergency_purpose_codeslist of string[]The purpose codes that mark an access as an emergency access in the vital interest of the patient (EHDS Art. 11(5)). Each must also be on purpose_codes, or the server refuses to start. Empty marks nothing. The mark is recorded on the access record and shown to the patient through the access log; it lifts no restriction.
legal_basisstringunsetThe legal basis this deployment processes under, recorded on every access record. A deployment-level fact: the controller establishes the GDPR Art. 6/9 condition once. Unset records nothing rather than a guess.

Note

The local store renders a FHIR R4 AuditEvent from each record when it is read, and the ATX:FHIR Feed sends one, so both need the fhir build feature, on in the published binary and container images. A binary built with --no-default-features refuses at startup if audit.store.enabled is set or [audit.fhir_feed] is configured; the DICOM/syslog feed needs no FHIR and stays available.

Note

There is no [atna] section. Configuration is strict, so a file or environment variable still setting an [atna] key fails at boot with an unknown-key error; move the setting under [audit].

[audit.store]: the local Audit Record Repository

KeyTypeDefaultDescription
enabledbooltruePersist every record in the audit schema, served through the ITI-81 GET /fhir/r4/AuditEvent search.
retentioncalendar periodunset (keep forever)How long records are kept, an ISO 8601 period of whole years ("P3Y") or days ("P1830D"); unset keeps them forever. Applied hourly by the retention reaper. Years are compared exactly against the floors and ceilings, which are written in years, and reaped with calendar arithmetic. A value below the retention floor of a jurisdiction the active [privacy.identifier_scan] rules name is a boot error naming both bounds; see Audit trail. The name is EHDS Annex II’s.
sgb_v_309_controllerboolfalseSet only if the deploying organisation is, or acts for, one of the controllers SGB V § 307 names for a German telematics-infrastructure application. It caps the horizon at the three-year period of SGB V § 309 Abs. 1, after which Abs. 3 requires deletion without delay, so a declared controller cannot keep records forever.
verify_intervalduration"1h"The time between two scheduled verifications of the store’s hash chain; "0s" turns the schedule off. Each run verifies the records written since the newest link an earlier run found intact. A finding is logged at ERROR, counted in atna_audit_chain_findings and reported by the audit_chain indicator on GET /health/readiness. See Tamper evidence.
