#? id = ""

# The key each Basic user is bound by (`[authz.party_binding.basic_user]`).
#? [[authz.party_binding.basic_user]]
# The `[auth.basic.users]` user-id.
#? user = ""
# The `identifier_issuer` of the `[auth.party]` table the key belongs to.
#? key_issuer = ""
# The binding key the user's `PERSON` carries.
#? key = ""

# The person templates and attributes of the shared party mapping.
[authz.party_binding.person]

# `[authz.party_binding.person.template]`, one per template a professional's
# `PERSON` may use.
#? [[authz.party_binding.person.template]]
# An operational template in the definition store rooted at `PERSON`.
#? template_id = ""
# Whether SCIM and just-in-time creation create new persons with this template;
# exactly one table sets it.
#? default = false

# The binding key.
#? [authz.party_binding.person.template.key]
# The openEHR path.
#? path = ""
# The `DV_IDENTIFIER.type`.
#? type = ""

# The SCIM `userName`.
#? [authz.party_binding.person.template.user_name]
# The openEHR path.
#? path = ""
# The `DV_IDENTIFIER.type`.
#? type = ""

# The SCIM `externalId`.
#? [authz.party_binding.person.template.external_id]
# The openEHR path.
#? path = ""
# The `DV_IDENTIFIER.type`.
#? type = ""

# `[authz.party_binding.person.attribute]`, one per mapped value.
#? [[authz.party_binding.person.attribute]]
# A SCIM attribute path, with the RFC 7644 §3.4.2.2 `valuePath` filter form
# (`emails[type eq "work"].value`).
#? scim = ""
# An OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §5.1 claim.
#? oidc = ""
# Whether just-in-time creation writes the value.
#? jit = false
# Whether this is the name the committer reads; at most one table sets it.
#? name = false
# The path the value goes to, per template id.
#? path = {}

# The professional `ROLE` template.
#? [authz.party_binding.professional_role]
# An operational template rooted at `ROLE`.
#? template_id = ""

# The provisioned `GROUP` template.
#? [authz.party_binding.group]
# An operational template rooted at `GROUP`.
#? template_id = ""
# The path of the group's `displayName`, a `DV_TEXT` in `identities`.
#? display_name = ""

# The group's `externalId`.
#? [authz.party_binding.group.external_id]
# The openEHR path.
#? path = ""
# The `DV_IDENTIFIER.type`.
#? type = ""

# The membership `PARTY_RELATIONSHIP` archetype.
#? [authz.party_binding.membership]
# A `PARTY_RELATIONSHIP` archetype.
#? archetype_id = ""

# The representation `PARTY_RELATIONSHIP` archetype.
#? [authz.party_binding.representation]
# A `PARTY_RELATIONSHIP` archetype whose `source` is the representative and
# whose `target` is the subject.
#? archetype_id = ""
# Each relationship type code of the archetype, mapped to a code of the openEHR
# `subject_relationship` group.
#? relationship_codes = {}

# What FerroEHR does for each `persons` issuer beyond the lookup
# (`[authz.party_binding.issuer]`): just-in-time creation.
#? [[authz.party_binding.issuer]]
# The `persons` issuer the table holds for.
#? issuer = ""
# Whether a first login with no party creates a provisional `PERSON`.
#? jit = false
# Whether a guest the issuer's `[auth.party]` table admits is created too.
#? guests_jit = false
# The claim the `userName` is read from; the issuer profile's `person_key` when
# unset.
#? user_name_claim = ""
# The dotted claim path the identity provider is read from.
#? idp_claim = "idp"
# The identity providers whose logins are created.
#? admit_idp = []
# The groups, read from the `[auth.party]` table's `group_claim`, one of which
# a created login holds.
#? admit_groups = []
# The roles, read from `[auth] role_claims`, one of which a created login
# holds.
#? admit_roles = []
# The lowest `[authz.assurance]` level a created login carries.
#? admit_assurance = "low"

# The systems whose imported committers are trusted (`[authz.import]`).
[authz.import]
# The `creating_system_id` values whose wrapped committers may name a local
# party; never this node's own system id.
trusted_systems = []

# The system clients that commit (`[authz.system_client]`).
#? [[authz.system_client]]
# The `machines` or `persons` issuer of the client's tokens.
#? issuer = ""
# The client the token names.
#? client_id = ""
# The template ids the client may commit; none by default.
#? writes = []
# What the client commits: a relayed record of a human act, a device's
# registration, or both.
#? origins = []
# The issuers of the device identifiers a `device` client names.
#? device_identifier_issuers = []

# The healthcare provider the client acts for, recorded on every system access.
#? [authz.system_client.provider]
# The issuer of the identifier.
#? issuer = ""
# The identifier.
#? id = ""

# The facilities the client may commit for.
#? [[authz.system_client.facilities]]
# The issuer of the facility identifier.
#? issuer = ""
# The facility identifier; exclusive with `id_prefix`.
#? id = ""
# The prefix every admitted facility identifier starts with; exclusive with
# `id`.
#? id_prefix = ""

# The federation agreements (`[authz.federation]`).
[authz.federation]

# The agreements, one per issuer and accessor.
#? [[authz.federation.agreement]]
# The `federation` issuer of the external callers.
#? issuer = ""
# Who the agreement admits: named persons, or the organisation.
#? accessor = "person"
# The agreement's name.
#? name = ""
# The agreement's version.
#? version = ""
# The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 jurisdiction; a `profile = "nl"` issuer implies `NL`.
#? jurisdiction = ""
# The kind of exchange the agreement covers.
#? exchange = ""
# What the exchange is for; required of an NL agreement, which may not serve a
# keuring (Wabvpz Art. 15f(2)).
#? purpose = "care"
# The source of the consent the exchange is conditioned on, never its legal
# ground.
#? consent = "mitz"
# The most an external caller may read: `patient/` scopes only.
#? reads = []
# The template ids an external person may commit; none by default.
#? writes = []
# Whether an external person may discard a dispensation of the same point of
# care within `discard_window`.
#? discard = false
# The window of a discard, a whole number of hours (MyHealth@EU Requirements
# Catalogue 10.0.0, requirement 07.04, sets `"24h"`).
#? discard_window = "1d"
# The MyHealth@EU service a contact point's person agreement serves, which
# names the `*_NOT_FOUND` code of a request outside the TRC patient; required
# on a `contact_point` issuer and refused elsewhere.
#? ehdsi_service = "patient_summary"
# Whether a professional of the agreement may read an opted-out EHR where
# national law provides the EHDS Art. 10(2) vital-interest access.
#? opt_out_override = false
# For an organisation: whether no natural person views the data, or the
# requester logs the person.
#? access_class = "automated"
# For a `chained` access: how long the requester keeps its log, a calendar
# period (`"P5Y"`).
#? chained_log_retention = "P5Y"

# The legal ground of the processing.
#? [authz.federation.agreement.legal_ground]
# The point of GDPR Art. 6(1), `a` to `f`.
#? gdpr_6_1 = ""
# The point of GDPR Art. 9(2), `a` to `j`.
#? gdpr_9_2 = ""
# The national provision, such as `UAVG Art. 30(3)(a)`.
#? national = ""

# The admission rate per caller, above which a request is refused before any
# patient lookup; required.
#? [authz.federation.agreement.caller_rate]
# The requests per second a caller may send once its burst is spent.
#? requests_per_second = 0
# The requests a caller may send at once.
#? burst = 0

# The origins of data this deployment recognises, which a retention period and
# an access rule may name (`[authz.origin]`, EHDS Annex II 3.4).
#? [[authz.origin]]
# The id the origin's data carry: the
# `FEEDER_AUDIT.originating_system_audit.system_id` its feeds commit under, and
# the origin a direct commit by one of `Self::clients` is stamped with.
# Compared exactly.
#? id = ""
# The authenticated clients whose direct commits come from this origin: a Basic
# user name, or the `client_id` (failing that the `azp`) of an OAuth 2.0 access
# token (RFC 9068 §2.2). Each client belongs to one origin at most.
#? clients = []

# The openEHR REST API: the base path, the system identifier, the `OPTIONS`
# identity, the `OpenAPI` UI, CORS, the clinical body tier and the ADMIN and
# terminology groups.
[api]
# The ITS-REST base path all API routes hang off, from the root of the
# listener. `management.base_path` is set the same way; the two never overlap.
base_path = "/ferroehr/rest/openehr/v1"
# Who may read the Swagger UI and the `OpenAPI` documents at the REST root:
# `off` (not mounted), `admin_only`, `private` (any authenticated principal;
# the default) or `public`. The documents list the whole enabled operation
# surface, admin and message groups included, so `public` discloses it to
# anyone who can reach the port. The same vocabulary the management endpoints
# use; the name is the `OpenAPI` Specification's, the document the UI renders.
openapi_ui = "private"
# This CDR's own openEHR **system identifier** — the identity the deployment
# stamps into the data it authors (`FERROEHR__API__SYSTEM_ID`).
system_id = "ferroehr.local"
# The largest body the ordinary clinical surface accepts, below the listener's
# `server.body_limit`.
#? body_limit = "512KiB"
# Whether the ADMIN API group is served.
admin = false
# Whether the terminology extension API is mounted. Off by default — the
# routes answer `404` unless enabled. The terminology server the CDR asks is
# `[terminology]`.
terminology = false

# The CORS protocol answers of the API (Fetch Standard §3.2). Absent, no CORS
# header is sent, so a browser on another origin cannot read a response.
#? [api.cors]
# `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`: the origins a browser may read responses for,
# each a serialized origin such as `https://app.example`, or `["*"]` for any
# origin (dev only).
#? allow_origins = []
# `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`: the methods a preflight admits; empty admits
# the method the preflight asks for.
#? allow_methods = []
# `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`: the request headers a preflight admits; empty
# admits the headers the preflight asks for.
#? allow_headers = []
# `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`: the response headers a script may read
# beyond the CORS-safelisted ones.
#? expose_headers = []
# `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`: whether a credentialed request's response
# may be read. Refused beside `allow_origins = ["*"]`, which the Fetch Standard
# forbids together.
#? allow_credentials = false
# `Access-Control-Max-Age`: how long a preflight answer may be cached; unset
# sends no header.
#? max_age = "500ms"

# The `OPTIONS /` System-Options manifest identity (`[api.options]`). Sourced
# from config so the public identity is not a string literal in the handler;
# the live endpoint list is supplied separately by `ferroehr_rest::router`.
# This is the *display* identity of the manifest — the data-authoring
# identity is `Self::system_id`.
[api.options]
# `Options.solution` — the product name.
solution = "FerroEHR"
# `Options.vendor` — the organisation providing the solution (ITS-REST
# `specifications/schemas/others/Options.yaml`, a plain string); defaults to
# the manufacturer's name (`crate::manufacturer::MANUFACTURER`).
vendor = "Cadasto B.V."

# The shared `PostgreSQL` DSN, pool tuning, migrations and one table per
# storage domain.
[database]
# `PostgreSQL` connection DSN (`postgres://user:pass@host:port/db`).
# Credentials are redacted from every rendering (`SecretUrl`).
#? url = ""
# Path to a file holding the DSN, read at boot in place of `Self::url`.
#? url_file = ""
# DSN that schema preparation (`prepare`) authenticates as; unset (the default)
# reuses `Self::url`.
#? migrate_url = ""
# Path to a file holding `Self::migrate_url`, read at boot in place of it —
# the mounted-secret route, as `Self::url_file` is for the clinical DSN.
# Setting both is a boot error.
#? migrate_url_file = ""
# Upper bound of the connection pool.
max_connections = 20
# Connections the pool keeps open when idle (avoids cold reopen + `SET
# search_path` churn under variable load).
min_connections = 2
# How long to wait for a free connection before failing.
acquire_timeout = "30s"
# `statement_timeout` applied to every pooled connection; `"0s"` leaves the
# server default (usually unlimited).
statement_timeout = "1min"
# Whether the server applies its embedded migrations at boot (`MigrationMode`).
migrations = "apply"

# The clinical record's own DSN and the credential that prepares its database.
[database.clinical]
# This domain's `PostgreSQL` DSN. Unset reuses `[database] url`.
#? url = ""
# Path to a file holding `Self::url`, read at boot in place of it — the route
# for a deployment that mounts its database credential as a file rather than
# passing it as an environment value, which is readable through
# `/proc/<pid>/environ` and inherited by every child process. Setting both is a
# boot error.
#? url_file = ""
# The credential that prepares the database this domain lives in when that is
# not the database `[database] migrate_url` reaches.
#? migrate_url = ""
# Path to a file holding `Self::migrate_url`, read at boot in place of it.
# Setting both is a boot error.
#? migrate_url_file = ""

# The identities' own DSN and the credential that prepares their database.
[database.party]
# This domain's `PostgreSQL` DSN. Unset reuses `[database] url`.
#? url = ""
# Path to a file holding `Self::url`, read at boot in place of it — the route
# for a deployment that mounts its database credential as a file rather than
# passing it as an environment value, which is readable through
# `/proc/<pid>/environ` and inherited by every child process. Setting both is a
# boot error.
#? url_file = ""
# The credential that prepares the database this domain lives in when that is
# not the database `[database] migrate_url` reaches.
#? migrate_url = ""
# Path to a file holding `Self::migrate_url`, read at boot in place of it.
# Setting both is a boot error.
#? migrate_url_file = ""

# The audit repository's own DSN and the credential that prepares its database.
[database.audit]
# This domain's `PostgreSQL` DSN. Unset reuses `[database] url`.
#? url = ""
# Path to a file holding `Self::url`, read at boot in place of it — the route
# for a deployment that mounts its database credential as a file rather than
# passing it as an environment value, which is readable through
# `/proc/<pid>/environ` and inherited by every child process. Setting both is a
# boot error.
#? url_file = ""
# The credential that prepares the database this domain lives in when that is
# not the database `[database] migrate_url` reaches.
#? migrate_url = ""
# Path to a file holding `Self::migrate_url`, read at boot in place of it.
# Setting both is a boot error.
#? migrate_url_file = ""

# The management/observability surface.
[management]
# Master switch. When `false`, no management routes are mounted at all.
enabled = false
# The base path the management endpoints hang off.
base_path = "/management"
# When set, the management surface is served from its **own** listener on this
# socket address (a separate axum server task in the binary) instead of the
# main API listener — so production can keep it off the public listener
# entirely. The same form as `server.listen`.
#? listen = ""
# Span-timing capture: every span's folded stacks are written to this file, for
# `inferno-flamegraph` to render offline. Unset, nothing is captured.
#? flame_file = ""

# Per-endpoint access levels — the SINGLE authority for this surface.
[management.endpoints]
# `/management/info`.
info = "off"
# `/management/metrics` (+ `/{name}`) — the JSON registry view.
metrics = "off"
# `/management/prometheus` — the text exposition scraped by Prometheus.
prometheus = "off"
# `/management/env` — the redacted effective configuration.
env = "off"
# `/management/loggers` — the runtime `EnvFilter` control.
loggers = "off"
# `/management/flamegraph` — the on-demand CPU flamegraph (pprof sampling).
flamegraph = "off"
# `/management/health` — every readiness indicator with its detail.
health = "off"
# `/management/status` — the status document with the licence, the deployment
# posture and the support period.
status = "off"

# Limits for the on-demand CPU profiler (`endpoints.flamegraph`).
[management.profiling]
# The longest sample window a single request may ask for, in whole seconds.
max_duration = "30s"
# The highest sampling frequency a request may ask for, in Hz.
max_frequency = 999

# The IHE ATNA audit trail / System Log (local Audit Record Repository + the
# syslog and FHIR-feed forwarding sinks).
[audit]
# Master switch (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__ENABLED`). **On by default** — every
# deployment gets a queryable audit trail with zero external dependencies (the
# sinks decide where records go).
enabled = true
# Enterprise/site id → `AuditEnterpriseSiteID`
# (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__ENTERPRISE_SITE_ID`).
#? enterprise_site_id = ""
# Audit source id → `AuditSourceID` and the destination participant
# (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__SOURCE_ID`).
source_id = "ferroehr"
# Fill value for empty mandatory fields (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__VALUE_IF_MISSING`).
value_if_missing = "UNKNOWN"
# Skip successful-login records (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__SUPPRESS_LOGIN_EVENTS`).
# Rejected accesses (401/403) are always recorded.
suppress_login_events = true
# Failure mode (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__FAIL_MODE`): `open` | `closed`.
fail_mode = "open"
# Enrich the patient participant via a background indexed lookup of
# `ehr.subject_id` (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__RESOLVE_SUBJECT`). On by default — the
# IHE BALP `Patient*` patterns and the patient-centric audit search need the
# subject; the lookup runs only on the background drain.
resolve_subject = true
# Bounded audit queue capacity (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__QUEUE_CAPACITY`). Sized for
# write-path bursts: the drain persists in multi-row batches, so the queue only
# needs to ride out sink latency spikes, but a loaded write path can enqueue
# thousands per second.
queue_capacity = 8192
# This node's advertised network address → the destination
# network-access-point (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__SERVER_HOST`); the `value_if_missing`
# fill when unset.
#? server_host = ""
# The request header carrying the caller's declared purpose of use
# (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__PURPOSE_HEADER`), recorded on every access record.
purpose_header = "x-purpose-of-use"
# The request header carrying the data permit the caller acts under
# (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__PERMIT_HEADER`), recorded on every access record.
permit_header = "x-data-permit"
# The purpose codes this deployment accepts (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__PURPOSE_CODES`).
purpose_codes = []
# The declared purpose codes that mark an access as an emergency access
# (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__EMERGENCY_PURPOSE_CODES`). Empty (the default) marks
# nothing.
emergency_purpose_codes = []
# The legal basis this deployment processes under
# (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__LEGAL_BASIS`), recorded on every access record.
#? legal_basis = ""

# The template and archetype map every access is classified through by EHDS
# priority category (Annex II 3.2(c)). Empty by default, so the map FerroEHR
# ships applies; an unmapped access is recorded `unclassified`.
[audit.categories]
# Whether the map FerroEHR ships applies while this section declares no
# template and no archetype (`shipped_map`, on by default). Off with nothing
# declared, no map applies and every access is recorded `unclassified`, which
# `deployment.profile = "production"` refuses as the `no_category_map` gap.
shipped_map = true
# The national categories (Art. 14(1) third subparagraph), each
# `<system>|<code>`.
national = []
# Template id → categories (`[audit.categories.templates]`), consulted first.
templates = {}
# Archetype id → categories (`[audit.categories.archetypes]`), consulted for
# an object whose template the map does not name.
archetypes = {}

# The local Audit Record Repository.
[audit.store]
# Persist every record locally (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__STORE__ENABLED`). **On by
# default** (owner posture: compliance out of the box).
enabled = true
# How long records are kept, a calendar period (`"P5Y"`, `"P1830D"`); unset
# keeps them forever (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__STORE__RETENTION`). Applied hourly by
# the retention reaper.
#? retention = "P5Y"
# Whether this deployment is one of the controllers SGB V § 307 names for a
# German telematics-infrastructure application
# (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__STORE__SGB_V_309_CONTROLLER`). **Off by default.**
sgb_v_309_controller = false
# The time between two scheduled verifications of the store's hash chain
# (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__STORE__VERIFY_INTERVAL`); `"0s"` turns the schedule off.
# Default one hour.
verify_interval = "1h"
# The time between two scheduled full passes over the hash chain
# (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__STORE__FULL_VERIFY_INTERVAL`), which also recompute the
# records before the checkpoint; `"0s"` leaves the full pass to `SELECT * FROM
# audit.verify_audit_chain()` on demand. Default one week. A run that found
# damage is always followed by a full pass.
full_verify_interval = "7d"

# The classic DICOM-over-syslog feed; absent, off.
#? [audit.syslog]
# The Audit Record Repository, `tls://host:port`
# (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__SYSLOG__URL`): RFC 5425 TLS, on the §4.1 port 6514 by
# default.
#? url = "tls://localhost:6514"
# The directory of the `ihe-atna` spool every record is stored in before it is
# sent (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__SYSLOG__SPOOL_DIR`), owner-only; unset, the spool is
# held in memory and a restart loses what it holds.
#? spool_dir = ""
# The most records the spool holds
# (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__SYSLOG__SPOOL_MAX_EVENTS`).
#? spool_max_events = 100000
# The most the spool holds in size (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__SYSLOG__SPOOL_MAX_SIZE`).
#? spool_max_size = "256MiB"

# The TLS material of the connection to the ARR (`[audit.syslog.tls]`): the
# family's outbound TLS keys, the client identity for mutual TLS and the trust
# roots beside the platform's.
#? [audit.syslog.tls]
# The client certificate chain and its private key, in one PEM.
#? client_identity = ""
# A file holding `client_identity`.
#? client_identity_file = ""
# A PEM bundle of trust roots beside the platform's.
#? trust_roots_file = ""
# The oldest TLS version the client speaks: `"1.3"` unless lowered to `"1.2"`,
# as for the listener.
#? min_version = "1.3"

# The wait between two delivery attempts.
#? [audit.syslog.retry]
# The longest wait between two delivery attempts after a failure.
#? max_backoff = "1min"

# The RESTful-ATNA FHIR `AuditEvent` feed; absent, off.
#? [audit.fhir_feed]
# How long the forwarder waits for a new record before it reads the store again
# (`FERROEHR__AUDIT__FHIR_FEED__POLL_INTERVAL`); at least 100 ms is waited.
#? poll_interval = "2s"

# `[audit.fhir_feed.endpoint]`, the family's outbound endpoint: the ARR's FHIR
# base URL (`url`; the `AuditEvent` endpoint is `{url}/AuditEvent`), the
# timeout of one `POST`, the `retry` of a delivery, the TLS and the credential,
# such as the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant of the IHE IUA authorized
# client. Credentials in the URL are masked in every rendering.
#? [audit.fhir_feed.endpoint]
# The service's URL (RFC 3986); required. It renders with its userinfo and its
# query masked, in `Debug` and when serialized.
#? url = ""
# How long one whole call may take; never zero.
#? timeout = "10s"
# How long opening the connection may take; unset, only `timeout` bounds it.
#? connect_timeout = "500ms"

# How a failed call is tried again.
#? [audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.retry]
# How many times one call is tried in all; 1 tries once.
#? max_attempts = 3
# The wait before the second try.
#? initial_backoff = "200ms"
# The longest wait between two tries.
#? max_backoff = "1min"

# The TLS of the connection, built by the product's reader of TLS material.
#? [audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.tls]
# The client certificate chain and its private key, in one PEM.
#? client_identity = ""
# A file holding `client_identity`.
#? client_identity_file = ""
# A PEM bundle of trust roots beside the platform's.
#? trust_roots_file = ""
# The oldest TLS version the client speaks: `"1.3"` unless lowered to `"1.2"`,
# as for the listener.
#? min_version = "1.3"

# The credential the calls carry: HTTP Basic or the client credentials grant.
#? [audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.credentials]
# The Basic user-id.
#? user = ""
# The Basic password, rendered redacted.
#? password = ""
# The file holding the Basic password.
#? password_file = ""

# The client credentials grant.
#? [audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.credentials.oauth]
# The issuer whose metadata names the token endpoint; exclusive with
# `token_endpoint`. It renders with any userinfo masked, as `SecretUrl` renders
# itself.
#? issuer = ""
# The token endpoint itself; exclusive with `issuer`. It renders with its
# userinfo and its query masked.
#? token_endpoint = ""
# The client identifier.
#? client_id = ""
# How the client authenticates.
#? client_auth = "client_secret_basic"
# The client secret, rendered redacted.
#? client_secret = ""
# The file holding the client secret.
#? client_secret_file = ""
# The PEM file holding the private key of the client assertion under
# `private_key_jwt`, and of the actor assertion of an onward exchange
# (`credentials.onward.actor_assertion`) whatever the client authentication.
#? private_key_file = ""
# The `kid` the assertion names; the RFC 7638 thumbprint when empty.
#? kid = ""
# The algorithm the assertion is signed with; when unset, by key type, an EC
# key by its curve (P-256 ES256, P-384 ES384).
#? assertion_alg = ""
# The `scope` request parameter; empty for none.
#? scope = ""
# The RFC 8707 resource indicator; empty for none.
#? resource = ""
# The `audience` request parameter; empty for none.
#? audience = ""
# How long before the token expires a new one is fetched.
#? refresh_margin = "30s"
# How long one call to the authorization server may take.
#? timeout = "10s"
# The `aud` of a `private_key_jwt` assertion: `token_endpoint` (the default) or
# `issuer`, which needs `issuer` set.
#? assertion_audience = "token_endpoint"
# The PEM file of the `DPoP` key the tokens are bound to (RFC 9449).
#? dpop_key_file = ""
# Whether the tokens are bound to the client certificate (RFC 8705 §3).
#? certificate_bound = false
# The security profile: `oauth2` (the default) or `fapi2`.
#? security_profile = "oauth2"
# The hosts a FAPI 2.0 mutual-TLS alias may be on (RFC 8705 §5).
#? mtls_alias_hosts = []
# The PEM file of the previous assertion key, published, never signing.
#? previous_private_key_file = ""
# How long the previous key stays published; `0s` for as long as it is set.
#? previous_key_overlap = "0s"
# The PEM file of the next assertion key, published and never signing.
#? next_private_key_file = ""
# The RFC 9396 `authorization_details` JSON text; empty for none.
#? authorization_details = ""

# The TLS of the token endpoint connection: trust roots beside the platform's,
# the client identity presented over mutual TLS (RFC 8705 §2) and the minimum
# version. The crate reads none of it: a table that names material resolves
# through the product's `TlsBuilder`.
#? [audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.credentials.oauth.tls]
# The client certificate chain and its private key, in one PEM.
#? client_identity = ""
# A file holding `client_identity`.
#? client_identity_file = ""
# A PEM bundle of trust roots beside the platform's.
#? trust_roots_file = ""
# The oldest TLS version the client speaks: `"1.3"` unless lowered to `"1.2"`,
# as for the listener.
#? min_version = "1.3"

# The onward target the lane reaches on a caller's behalf, authenticating with
# `oauth`.
#? [audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.credentials.onward]
# The identifier of the issuer of the onward tokens, whose metadata names its
# token endpoint unless `token_endpoint` is set. It renders with any userinfo
# masked, as `SecretUrl` renders itself.
#? issuer = ""
# Whose tokens the issuer signs: `persons` (a delegated exchange), `patients`
# (a patient's own token) or `federation`; required, with no default.
#? kind = "persons"
# The preset the issuer's profile starts from.
#? profile = "rfc9068"
# The token endpoint itself; empty to discover it from `issuer`. It renders
# with its userinfo and its query masked.
#? token_endpoint = ""
# The client id at this issuer; empty for the lane's own.
#? client_id = ""
# The audiences an onward token may name, at least one.
#? audiences = []
# The `resource` or `audience` values the request names, as the profile's
# `onward_indicator` says.
#? indicators = []
# The `scope` the request names; empty for none.
#? scope = ""
# The claim a chained federation route carries from the subject token to the
# onward token; empty for none.
#? correlation_claim = ""
# Whether the lane holds the tokens it obtains until they near their `exp`.
# `false` exchanges a token at the issuer on every call, a setting for a
# performance measurement's self-test, never for production. `true` by default.
#? cache = true
# Whether every token exchange sent without an actor token names the lane's
# client as its actor with an assertion signed by the current key of its
# `oauth` table's key ring (RFC 8693 §2.1; `Onward::with_actor_assertion`).
# `false` by default.
#? actor_assertion = false

#? value = ""

#? subjects = []

#? sub_is_client = false

#? differs_from_iss = ""

#? [[audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.credentials.onward.keys.delegates]]

#? issuer = ""

#? contact_point = false
# The default sources the table starts from.
#? mapping = "iua"
# The sources of each field, over the mapping's.
#? fields = {}
# The country codes a professional may carry.
#? countries = []
# The issuing authorities a professional or provider may name.
#? issuing_authorities = []
# The prefixes a healthcare provider identifier must start with.
#? provider_identifier_prefixes = []
# Whether the issuer attests the `authorization_details` it puts in a token,
# which RFC 9396 §12 has "sent through the user agent".
#? attests_authorization_details = false

#? authorization_details_type = ""

#? organisation_types = []

#? presentations_claim = ""

#? exchanges_from = []

# The data-minimisation policy: the subject namespaces, the identifier scan and
# protection, the cohort query and the access delay.
[privacy]
# The namespaces an `EHR_STATUS.subject.external_ref` may name
# (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__SUBJECT_NAMESPACES`, comma-separated in the environment)
# — the pseudonymisation domains this deployment issues subject pseudonyms
# in.
subject_namespaces = []
# Accept `PARTY_IDENTIFIED` / `PARTY_RELATED` carrying `name` or `identifiers`
# in clinical content (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__ALLOW_IDENTIFIED_PARTIES_IN_EHR`).
allow_identified_parties_in_ehr = false

# The identifier scanner.
[privacy.identifier_scan]
# `strict` (refuse) or `warn` (accept and record)
# (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__IDENTIFIER_SCAN__MODE`).
mode = "strict"
# The national personal-identifier rules this deployment scans for, by rule key
# (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__IDENTIFIER_SCAN__RULES`, comma-separated in the
# environment). An unknown key is a boot error naming it.
rules = ["ch-ahvn13", "ch-epd-pid", "de-kvnr", "fi-hetu", "gb-nhs-number", "nl-bsn", "no-fodselsnummer", "se-personnummer"]
# Extra identifier patterns this deployment refuses, as Rust regular
# expressions (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__IDENTIFIER_SCAN__PATTERNS`, comma-separated
# in the environment).
patterns = []

# The national-identifier protection of the demographic domain; absent, off.
#? [privacy.identifier_protection]
# The scheme codes to protect
# (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__IDENTIFIER_PROTECTION__SCHEMES`).
#? schemes = ["nl-bsn"]
# The root key, 64 hex characters
# (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__IDENTIFIER_PROTECTION__KEY`), or its `key_file` sibling.
#? key = ""
# A file holding the root key, read at boot
# (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__IDENTIFIER_PROTECTION__KEY_FILE`).
#? key_file = ""

# The cross-domain cohort-query allow-list and limits.
[privacy.cohort]
# The distinct-EHR floor a result set must reach to be served
# (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__COHORT__SMALL_CELL_THRESHOLD`); `0` disables
# suppression.
small_cell_threshold = 5
# The largest cohort a predicate may select
# (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__COHORT__MAX_COHORT_SIZE`).
max_cohort_size = 100000
# Whether a cohort may name its subjects by identifier
# (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__COHORT__SUBJECTS`), each resolved through the installed
# EHR index provider. The one cohort form an IHE patient identity source
# serves, so it turns the surface on without a bound predicate.
subjects = false

# The bound predicates, keyed by the name a caller uses
# (`[privacy.cohort.predicates]`). Empty — the default — leaves the
# predicate half of the surface off.
# [privacy.cohort.predicates.<name>]
# The archetype HRID of the nearest archetyped ancestor of the ELEMENT
# (`openEHR-DEMOGRAPHIC-ADDRESS.address.v1`), matched case-insensitively
# against the stored, case-folded column (BASE `base_types`
# `master05-identification_package.adoc` §"Composite Identifiers and Case").
# archetype = ""
# The ELEMENT's `archetype_node_id` at-code (`at0012`).
# node = ""
# How the caller's value is matched against the leaf.
# kind = "text"

# The EHDS Art. 3(3) delay of the person's own access; absent, off.
#? [privacy.access_delay]
# The categories whose new compositions are held at creation, named as
# `[audit.categories]` names one: a priority category of Art. 14(1) by its code
# (`Laboratory-Reports`, `Medical-Imaging`, …) or as `<system>|<code>`, or a
# national category the map declares
# (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__ACCESS_DELAY__CATEGORIES`, comma-separated). Empty holds
# nothing at creation, and a professional still holds an object by hand.
#? categories = []
# How long a hold lasts at most, a whole number of hours from `"1h"` to
# `MAX_HOURS` hours (`FERROEHR__PRIVACY__ACCESS_DELAY__MAX_DELAY`): the length
# of a hold placed at creation and the latest end a professional may give one.
# Required.
#? max_delay = "500ms"

# The record itself: the subject index, versioning, signing, the query engine,
# the change feed and multimedia.
[record]
# Who holds the subject-to-EHR cross-reference, the IHE patient identity source
# of `[pixm]` (`pixm`) or the in-instance map (`local`). No default: an unset
# index refuses the start.
#? subject_index = "pixm"

# The answer to an identical re-send.
[record.versioning]
# `idempotent_resend` (default `false`): when `true`, an update whose content
# equals the current version's commits nothing and answers with the existing
# version's `ETag` and `Location`, leaving one `resend` record on the access
# log. No `commit_audit` and no CONTRIBUTION then record the act (RM common
# master06 §Committal and Audits), which is why the default records every
# commit. The name is RFC 9110 §9.2.2's: a re-send then has the effect of one
# request.
idempotent_resend = false

# VERSION signing.
[record.signing]
# Server-side signing of committed versions. Defaults **on** so the STANDARD
# "Signing" capability is demonstrably met.
enabled = true
# Signing mode: `digest` | `pgp`.
mode = "digest"
# Armored RFC 4880 secret key; **required for `pgp` mode** (validated at boot,
# fail-closed).
#? key_file = ""
# Key passphrase, kept in `ferrohealth_secret::secret::Secret` and redacted
# from any config snapshot.
#? key_passphrase = ""
# File-based indirection for `Self::key_passphrase` (K8s/Docker secrets).
# Exactly one of the pair may be set; the loader reads and trims the file.
#? key_passphrase_file = ""
# Armored RFC 4880 **public** keys retired from signing but retained for
# verification, so versions signed before a key rotation keep verifying.
retired_key_files = []
# Read-time verification policy: `off` | `warn` | `strict`. **Unset** (the
# default) resolves via `Self::effective_verify_on_read` to `strict` when
# signing is enabled — the explicit "sign but never check" state is reachable
# only by deliberately setting `off`.
#? verify_on_read = "off"

# AQL execution knobs.
[record.query]
# Max distinct cached query plans; `0` disables the plan cache (every lookup
# misses and the full parse→lower path runs).
plan_cache_capacity = 256
# Per-query DB execution budget; `"0s"` disables it. Overrun reports `408`
# (ITS-REST `Requests_and_responses` §HTTP status codes).
timeout = "30s"
# The largest page of rows one query execution serves; `0` means unbounded.
max_result_rows = 10000

# The commit-event outbox readers and their retention.
[record.change_feed]
# The readers of the outbox feed, each a name matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`
# (`ferrobridge`, for one). Boot registers each one and marks every reader the
# list no longer names inactive. Empty by default: no commit writes an outbox
# row.
readers = []
# How long a row is kept once every active reader has acknowledged it, counted
# from its commit instant.
retention = "7d"
# How often the retention prune runs.
prune_interval = "1h"

# `DV_MULTIMEDIA` externalization to object storage. It keeps `enabled`,
# because its store applies while it is off: blobs already offloaded are read
# back from `url`.
[record.multimedia]
# Master switch. `false` (default) = today's inline behaviour, byte for byte;
# no object store is built or contacted.
enabled = false
# A decoded `DV_MULTIMEDIA.data` strictly larger than this is offloaded to the
# object store; at or below it stays inline. Default `"256KiB"`.
threshold = "256KiB"
# S3-compatible endpoint URL (e.g. a SeaweedFS S3 gateway in dev/test, or an
# AWS/MinIO endpoint in prod). `None` uses the object_store default AWS
# endpoint resolution. Any `userinfo` in it is masked in every rendering. An
# `http://` URL is plain HTTP, which a dev SeaweedFS speaks; a `production`
# deployment names it as a gap.
#? url = ""
# Target bucket for content-addressed blobs.
bucket = "openehr-multimedia"
# AWS region (S3 requires one even for non-AWS endpoints).
region = "us-east-1"
# Access key id. `None` (with `secret_access_key` also `None`) runs the client
# unsigned/anonymous — the mode a keyless dev SeaweedFS accepts.
#? access_key_id = ""
# Secret access key (paired with `access_key_id`); never rendered.
#? secret_access_key = ""
# File-based indirection for `Self::secret_access_key` (K8s/Docker secrets).
# Exactly one of the pair may be set; the loader reads and trims the file.
#? secret_access_key_file = ""

# The outbound FHIR terminology server; absent, none is asked.
#? [terminology]
# On a binding the server cannot resolve: `accept` (the default) or `refuse`. A
# resolved non-member is refused under either setting.
#? on_error = "accept"

# `[terminology.endpoint]`, the family's outbound endpoint: the FHIR R4B base
# URL (`url`, such as `http://ferroterm:8080/r4b`, required), the timeouts, the

# masked in every rendering.

# The service's URL (RFC 3986); required. It renders with its userinfo and its

# How long one whole call may take; never zero.
#? timeout = "10s"

#? connect_timeout = "500ms"

# The wait before the second try.

Party binding: bootstrap and migration

FerroEHR binds every person who logs in to a demographic PERSON, and a login with no PERSON is refused (403, refused-unbound). This page takes a new deployment from an empty database to its first bound login, and takes an existing deployment, whose people were attributed by login alone, to binding. The configuration it names is in Authentication & access, and the two commands are in CLI & production checklist. Every incompatible change of the release, with its upgrade step, is on Breaking changes of party binding.

No openEHR specification governs a deployment’s migration or its credential store: this is FerroEHR’s own design.

Who is a person

Every [[auth.basic.users]] entry is a person. It maps to the PERSON that carries its binding key, with [[authz.party_binding.basic_user]]:

[[authz.party_binding.basic_user]]
user = "clinician"
key_issuer = "urn:example:staff-login"   # the identifier_issuer of an [[auth.party]] table
key = "clinician"                        # the binding key the PERSON carries

A Basic user with no mapping refuses the start, naming the user. A machine, read-only included, authenticates with OAuth 2.0 client credentials under a declared [[authz.system_client]]. A Basic credential carries no assurance level, so with [authz.assurance] minimum set it is refused on patient data, and the server logs a warn naming every mapped Basic user while no minimum is set.

Bootstrapping a new deployment

With Basic users persons only, a new deployment has no machine login to start from, so it starts in this order:

  1. Declare the identity provider’s SCIM client. It is an OAuth 2.0 client-credentials client (RFC 6749 §4.4) of the deployment’s authorization server with the provisioning scope: an [[auth.issuer]] of kind machines that issues its tokens, and a [[auth.scim.client]] naming that issuer, the client, the scope and the binding_issuer its Users’ keys are written under.
  2. Provision the first person through /scim/v2/. The identity provider, or you through that client, sends POST /scim/v2/Users (RFC 7644 §3.3). FerroEHR creates the PERSON and its professional ROLE, and issues the PERSON’s id itself (RFC 7643 §3.1: the id “is always issued by the service provider”).
  3. Only then map a Basic user, by that person’s binding key. A Basic user mapped before its PERSON exists is refused at its first request.

The first administrator is a provisioned person whose token carries the administrator role from an issuer [authz.rbac] role_issuers lists.

The Docker Compose quickstart follows this path from an empty database: its ferroehr-provision one-shot takes a token for the quickstart-scim client and provisions the user ferroehr through /scim/v2/ once the server is healthy, and ferroehr is mapped by its key. The hosted sandbox does the same with its ferroehr-provision service after every nightly reset, and its reseed waits for the login to bind before it commits the demo data.

Migrating an existing deployment

An existing deployment attributes its people by login alone. It moves to binding in four steps, each with its check. Add the persons issuers last: from then on, every login with no PERSON is refused.

1. Prepare the existing persons

Bring every existing PERSON, for example those migrated from an earlier system, to a template of the party mapping, with the login identifier at the binding-key selector and the identity provider’s userName at its selector. Leave externalId to the identity provider, which issues it (RFC 7643 §3.1). A prepared PERSON performs no professional ROLE yet, so it does not bind.

Adopt them. ferroehr party-binding adopt gives each listed PERSON a professional ROLE of the mapping’s role template, with the PERSON as performer, and a new PERSON version listing it in roles, in one demographic CONTRIBUTION committed by the administrator you name, and writes one access record per adopted PERSON:

ferroehr party-binding adopt --admin <ADMIN_PARTY_ID> \
  --migration "<committer name of the migration>" <PARTY_ID>...

It refuses, naming them, every PERSON whose binding key was introduced by a committer the provenance rule does not accept (step 3), so a key a demographic writer planted before the upgrade is never adopted silently. Adopt before the first SCIM run: without the ROLE, the provider’s userName eq query finds no User and creates a duplicate.

At its next start, the server fills the binding side table from the party versions and refuses to start on any duplicate key, naming the parties.

2. Upgrade, then provision through SCIM

Start the upgraded deployment with only the SCIM client’s issuer configured; the persons issuers come in step 4, so no clinician meets a refusal while provisioning runs (for Microsoft Entra ID, the initial provisioning cycle). The provider’s filter=userName eq "..." queries find the existing persons whose keys are equal, so it updates them, writing their externalId, and creates only the professionals who have no PERSON yet. A bulk load through SCIM is the one sanctioned route.

3. Run the pre-flight

ferroehr party-binding check --admin <ADMIN_PARTY_ID> \
  --migration "<committer name of the migration>" \
  --expected assigned-users.txt

ferroehr party-binding check reads the party versions and writes nothing, so it runs before any boot fill. Per key issuer it reports the persons that carry a key, duplicates, inactive and abandoned persons, the provisional persons older than provisional_report_after, the key-bearing persons that perform no professional ROLE (which adopt has not reached), and every mapped Basic user with the PERSON it binds.

For each key it reports the committer of the version that introduced the key, and fails unless that committer was a [[auth.scim.client]], an administrator you name, a migration you declare, or just-in-time creation on an issuer with jit = true. A stored version records no role its committer held, so you name the administrators (--admin, --admin-key), and the report repeats them.

With --expected, it reads the identity provider’s list of assigned users (their login identifiers, exported from the provider, one per line) and lists every one with no PERSON. The command exits non-zero on a duplicate, a missing person or a key that fails the provenance rule.

4. Add the persons issuers

Add each persons issuer with its [[auth.party]] table. Every login with no PERSON is refused from then on; the warn lines and the binding_refusals metric show any the pre-flight missed.

Versions committed before binding

Versions are immutable, and nothing rewrites an AUDIT_DETAILS (RM Common master06-change_control_package.adoc §Committal and Audits), so every version committed before the upgrade keeps the committer it was committed with. Only versions committed after it name the bound PERSON.

Go-live prerequisites in other products

A deployment whose FerroBRIDGE facade or FerroFED gateway writes to FerroEHR adds its persons issuers only after the bridge and the gateway reach it under the caller; until then their writes are refused by the committer rule.

ProductWhat it needsRelease
FerroBRIDGEWrites to the CDR under the facade caller’s exchanged token (FerroHEALTH/FerroBRIDGE#1582)FerroBRIDGE v0.0.23
FerroFEDThe gateway reaches the CDR under the caller (FerroHEALTH/FerroFED#1615)none as of FerroFED v0.0.19; the issue’s FerroFED milestone is v0.0.20

No FerroFED release up to v0.0.19 reaches the CDR under the caller, so a deployment with a FerroFED gateway adds its persons issuers only once a FerroFED release carries that change (FerroHEALTH/FerroFED#1615).

Breaking changes of party binding

The release that binds every person to a demographic PERSON changes the configuration and the wire in ways an existing deployment must act on. Each change below has the upgrade step it needs and its own entry under Changed or Removed in the changelog. The order to apply them in is on Party binding: bootstrap and migration.

Configuration

  • The family pins move together. ferrohealth-smart 0.9, with ferrohealth-authz, ferrohealth-session, ihe-atna, ehds-logging, ihe-iti, ferrohealth-config, ferrohealth-server and ferrohealth-ui. Upgrade: nothing to set; the configuration changes below follow from the ferrohealth-smart 0.9 shape.
  • Every issuer is an [[auth.issuer]] table with a required kind (persons, patients, machines or federation) and a profile, and holds every setting of its tokens itself. Upgrade: write each issuer as its own table, move the section-level settings (audience, algorithms, clock_skew_seconds, the jwks_* keys, timeout_ms, mode, role_claims, [auth.introspection]) onto it, give it its kind, and put patients and professionals at separate issuers.
  • token_profile, the section-level issuer settings and the claim key of [[auth.party]] are deleted. A configuration that still names them refuses the start, naming what replaces it. Upgrade: replace token_profile = "jwt" with token_types = ["JWT"] and the required_claims the issuer’s tokens carry, drop token_profile = "rfc9068", and let the issuer profile’s person_key name the key claim.
  • acting_for_claim and client_tokens are removed with [authz.professional]. The issuer’s kind and profile classify the caller. Upgrade: remove the table and list a client that acts for a person in its issuer’s delegates.
  • Basic users are persons only. Every [[auth.basic.users]] entry maps to a PERSON by its binding key in [[authz.party_binding.basic_user]], an unmapped one refuses the start naming the user, and every machine, read-only included, uses OAuth 2.0 client credentials under a declared [[authz.system_client]]. Upgrade: provision each person a Basic user stands for through SCIM, map the user by that person’s key, and move every machine to client credentials.
  • Every committing system client needs its declaration, and the facility rule only checks. A system caller commits into an EHR only as a client an [[authz.system_client]] table declares, each COMPOSITION of a template its writes lists and naming a facility its facilities lists; the server never writes the facility for it. Upgrade: declare every client that commits, with its writes, facilities and origins, and give its compositions the facility identifier.
  • Import needs a role. Importing an EHR Extract needs [authz.rbac] import_role or a system/ caller. Upgrade: set import_role and give it to the accounts that import.

Binding and the committer

  • Unbound, inactive, abandoned and deprovisioned persons are refused. A persons login whose key no PERSON carries is refused with 403 (refused-unbound), and so is one whose PERSON is 800|inactive|, 801|abandoned| or deleted. Upgrade: provision every professional before you add a persons issuer, through the four steps.
  • The professional ROLE is what makes a PERSON bindable. A PERSON binds only while it performs a ROLE of the mapping’s role template naming it as performer. Upgrade: give each existing person its ROLE with ferroehr party-binding adopt before the first SCIM run.
  • The committer is the server’s. A bound caller commits under the committer the server writes, and a stated committer must equal it or be the placeholder {"_type": "PARTY_IDENTIFIED", "identifiers": [{"_type": "DV_IDENTIFIER", "issuer": "<iss>", "id": "<sub>"}]}, which names the authenticated caller; any other is refused with 403. Upgrade: stop sending a committer, or send the placeholder.
  • Every person’s committer carries the provider identifier, type healthcare-provider, beside the login identifier and the external_ref to the PERSON, and a representative commits as a PARTY_RELATED naming their own PERSON and the coded relationship. Upgrade: read the provider and the representative from these committers.
  • A patient’s committer is PARTY_SELF without external_ref. Upgrade: find a person’s own entries by the committer’s PARTY_SELF type, not by a former external_ref.
  • System callers and patient context are strict. A system caller holds system/ scopes only, and a token carrying a user/ or patient/ scope is refused with 403; a patient-context token commits no demographic version. Upgrade: give each system client system/ scopes alone.
  • The parties binding relies on are protected. A key-bearing PERSON, its professional ROLE, a representation relationship and a provisioned GROUP are written through the demographic API by an administrator only, and a present binding key changes only through POST /admin/party/binding-key. Upgrade: write these parties as an administrator.

Versions committed before the upgrade keep their committer: versions are immutable, and nothing rewrites an AUDIT_DETAILS (RM Common master06-change_control_package.adoc §Committal and Audits).

Security

A clinical data repository holds PHI, so its access controls and audit trail are part of the product. This chapter covers the four security surfaces you configure when you deploy FerroEHR: authentication (who is calling), authorization (what they may do), the pseudonymisation boundary (which role reads which domain), and the ATNA audit trail (recording what happened). Each is independently configurable, and each is described here in terms of the environment variables you actually set.

This chapter tells you how to configure each control. Its companions tell you the rest: the Threat model states what remains true after each control has done its job: the trust boundaries, the residual risk at each, and what this software explicitly does not defend against; and Verifying releases covers the artifacts themselves: how to establish that the binary, image, or chart you downloaded came from this project’s own build. Read the threat model before you decide a control is sufficient for your deployment.

  • Authentication
    • Assurance level and the natural person on patient data

  • Authorization

    • ABAC (attribute-based, fine-grained)
  • Response security headers

  • Secrets: mount files, never bake values
