[terminology], [pixm], [audit.fhir_feed] and [authz.abac.remote] read where they call and how from one [<x>.endpoint] table, the same keys for every outbound integration of every FerroHEALTH product: url, timeout, connect_timeout, retry (max_attempts, initial_backoff, max_backoff), tls (trust_roots_file, client_identity_file, min_version) and credentials (HTTP Basic user with password or password_file, or the client credentials grant [...credentials.oauth]). terminology.url, timeout and [terminology.oauth] are terminology.endpoint.url, timeout and [terminology.endpoint.credentials.oauth]; pixm.url, timeout, [pixm.tls] and [pixm.oauth] are pixm.endpoint.url, timeout, [pixm.endpoint.tls] and [pixm.endpoint.credentials.oauth]; audit.fhir_feed.url, [audit.fhir_feed.retry] and [audit.fhir_feed.oauth] are audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.url, [audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.retry] and [audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.credentials.oauth]; authz.abac.remote.url, connect_timeout, timeout and [authz.abac.remote.oauth] are authz.abac.remote.endpoint.url, connect_timeout, timeout and [authz.abac.remote.endpoint.credentials.oauth]. The v5.6 keys are refused naming their new home. Every client now honours retry: the terminology, PIXm and remote policy clients try a call that got no answer or a 5xx up to max_attempts times (three by default; each tried once before), so set max_attempts = 1 to keep one attempt, and the FHIR feed’s delivery rounds take max_attempts tries each, from initial_backoff, before the round waits max_backoff; the feed still never gives a record up. The environment follows the tree (FERROEHR__TERMINOLOGY__ENDPOINT__URL, FERROEHR__AUDIT__FHIR_FEED__ENDPOINT__URL), and so do the Helm chart’s values and its client secret routing, in the chart’s 25 line (#5331).

  • The FerroEHR PostgreSQL image is built on the 2026-11-09 respin of postgres:18.6 (sha256:e3d24f69…), a same-version respin with rebuilt base packages. A full scan of the rebuilt image on amd64 and arm64 finds the same findings as the image of the previous base, each judged in security/vex/postgres-os.openvex.json, and a gate scan finds no fixable HIGH or CRITICAL finding (#5332).

  • The development and Keycloak example compose files run Keycloak 26.8.2 (quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.8.2@sha256:723b1d6e…). Of the 26.8.2 upgrading notes, the shipped realm meets the ones that touch it: the Admin REST API’s new audience check passes for the master realm’s admin-cli token the browser-test harness uses, and the realm uses no token exchange, identity broker, SAML client, CIBA or dynamic client registration. The ferroehr-service client-credentials token carries the same audience and scopes as under 26.8.1 (#5333).

Removed

  • [authz.professional] (claim, client_tokens, acting_for_claim) and its 403 for a token that names no natural person. The issuer’s kind and profile classify the caller, and the access record’s acting mode and professional come from that classification: a person’s own token is the person, and a delegated token is the client acting for the person it names. Upgrade step: remove the table, which refuses the start, and list a client that acts for a person in its issuer’s delegates (#5003).

  • The named refusal of authz.rbac.user_role, which v5.6 introduced, is gone under the one-release rule for removal aids: the key is now refused as an unknown key when the configuration loads (#5259).

Fixed

  • A 553|incomplete| commit no longer refuses an empty mandatory archetype slot: RM common master06 §Incomplete Content sets every occurrences lower limit to zero, a slot’s included, while too many fillers are still refused. The OPT 1.4 writer now closes a mandatory slot once the fillers placed in it carry its lower bound, as ADL 2 §Slot Filling and Redefinition allows, and still refuses to close one they leave unmet (#5042).

  • The example of a party template whose identity the template marks optional is a party of its class carrying one identity at every detail level, where the required level answered 500: RM demographic PARTY.identities admits no party without one. A party template that constrains no identity at all answers 400 Bad Request naming its class (#5057).

  • An AQL VERSION standard predicate on commit_audit/time_committed applies its operator: VERSION v[commit_audit/time_committed/value > $t] returns every version committed after $t, where it returned the trunk version current at $t whatever the operator (QUERY 1.1.0 master03 §Standard predicate). A number, boolean or NULL literal as the bound, a string bound no ISO 8601 form reads, and a time_committed path other than the whole value or /value are refused with 400 (#5062).

  • AQL refuses a number, boolean or null parameter or literal compared with a date/time path, in WHERE and in a VERSION predicate, with the same 400 a non-ISO 8601 string gets; such a bound used to become NULL and match nothing (#5064).

  • The served OpenAPI document now lists, on both template example operations, the 400 answered for a party template that constrains no PARTY_IDENTITY (#5066).

  • The compose quickstart, the hosted sandbox and the Helm chart run FerroPIX 0.0.18 (ghcr.io/ferrohealth/ferropix:0.0.18@sha256:6fb622b5b9ade34c8a4053112c8f166ff495d8b32bf99f35529d01e512b7cc42), with the FerroPIX chart 0.3.10 built for it. The 0.0.16 they pinned had an outbox sender that never slept while its outbox was empty, so an idle install kept about 1.2 CPU cores busy between FerroPIX and its PostgreSQL at about 8,000 transactions a second (FerroHEALTH/FerroPIX#490). 0.0.18 also makes FerroPIX’s [auth] scopeless_subjects and role_claims hold per issuer, which changes nothing for a FerroPIX that trusts one issuer, as every configuration FerroEHR ships does. The chart moves to 21.0.5 (#5073).

  • An OPT2 built from a template that specialises a published archetype now carries that archetype, by its full id, as parent_archetype_id, as the OPERATIONAL_TEMPLATE invariant is_specialised requires (AOM2 §3.6.6), so a reader of the OPT finds the archetype its root specialises. The ADL form of an OPT still prints no specialize section (OPT2 §Artefact Structure), so the parent travels in the canonical JSON form (#5075).

  • A refused-key-claim-missing access record names the key claim the issuer’s binding reads (its person_key) in binding_detail.claim, so an operator sees which claim the token lacked. It records the name only, never a claim value (#5139).

  • A 403 for a caller kind is recorded with its own binding code: refused-system-personal-scope for a system caller holding a user/ or patient/ scope, refused-no-agreement for an external caller whose issuer has no agreement for its accessor kind, and refused-scope-beyond-agreement for an external caller holding a scope its agreement does not read. Audit migration 0024 widens the binding constraint; the problem text of each refusal is unchanged (#5140).

  • openehr-sdt builds no /context node, and no start_time or setting leaf, in the Web Template of an OPT 1.4 whose COMPOSITION prohibits context (existence 0..0, or an EVENT_CONTEXT of occurrences 0..0), and the template example of such a template carries no context. A template that leaves context open or optional keeps the node as before (#5147).

  • openehr-sdt gives the /context node it synthesizes in a Web Template the min of the template’s existence on COMPOSITION.context, and 0 where the template leaves context unconstrained, since the RM makes context optional (0..1). A client following the Web Template no longer treats the context as mandatory when the template does not require it, and the required template example of such a template carries no context (#5154).

  • An ADL2 template that deletes an attribute (existence matches {0}), for example COMPOSITION.context, keeps the prohibition after it compiles to its operational template: openehr-adl’s create_opt now returns a RawOpt that names each removed attribute beside the OPT, and build_web_template_v2_4 takes that list. A template that deletes context gets no /context node, and a commit that carries one is refused, as it is for an OPT 1.4 template that prohibits context. An OPT2 uploaded already compiled carries no such list and reads a deleted attribute at its reference-model existence. Breaking for crate users: create_opt returns RawOpt and build_web_template_v2_4 takes the prohibited attributes (#5154).

  • A composition commit whose template_id names a stored ADL2 archetype rather than a template is refused with 422 as an unknown operational template; it failed at the insert with a server error before (#5177).

  • openehr-rm types REFERENCE_RANGE.range as DV_INTERVAL<T>: ReferenceRange is now generic over its limit type (ReferenceRange<DvQuantity> on a DV_QUANTITY, ReferenceRange<DvOrdered> on the other ordered types), its is_in_range and Range_is_simple work at that type, and the static RM model gives REFERENCE_RANGE.range and IMPORTED_VERSION.item their argument. Each model::RmAttribute and model::RmTypeRef now keeps the formal parameter it is written as (formal, Some("T") for DV_INTERVAL.lower) beside the resolved bound. The RM class table declares REFERENCE_RANGE<T> and leaves T unused; the generator restores it from a cited table and refuses a schema that no longer matches (#5196) (#5188).

  • An access record names the client the token’s issuer profile reads from client_claims (azp under the entra and keycloak profiles), the one the caller was admitted as. A token carrying a different client_id claim beside it was recorded under that claim. The [origins] register and the SCIM client lookup read the same client (#5194).

  • An Interval or DV_INTERVAL read from canonical JSON or XML that omits a boundedness or inclusion flag now takes it from its bound. An absent bound reads as unbounded and not included, and a present bound as bounded and included. A flag the wire states is kept as written. Before, an omitted flag always read as bounded and included, so an interval with only an upper came out with a bounded, included lower side that had no value. ITS-JSON requires all four flags, and BASE ties none of them to its bound, so reading the omission is our own design (#5203).

  • The viewer’s New contribution commits as the signed-in login. Each audit carries the placeholder naming that login, and the server records the committer it derives from the login. The free-text committer field is gone. For a login bound to a demographic PERSON, a stated name that differs from the PERSON’s name was refused with 403 (#5222).

  • The management surface answers a caller the login binding refuses with 403 and its binding code, such as refused-unbound, as every other route does, in place of 401: the credential authenticated, so new credentials cannot help (RFC 9110 §15.5.4). An absent or invalid credential still answers 401 with its challenge (#5250).

  • The party binding posture in ferroehr report and the boot log masks the user name and password of an issuer URL, as every other rendering of the configuration does (#5259).

  • GET /definition/query/{namespace}:: lists every stored query in the namespace again, where it answered 400 since the typed stored-query name: ITS-REST 1.1.0 definition_query_list reads its name as a pattern in which an empty part is a wildcard, so ::{name} also lists the names that start with it in any namespace. openehr-its gains rest::stored_query::QueryNamePattern, the type the generated DefinitionQueryListParams carries. The store and the single-query reads still refuse an empty name or namespace (#5268).

  • The identifier scan ([privacy.identifier_scan]) reads the name of the ELEMENT that holds a DV_IDENTIFIER when the identifier’s type is absent or names neither a person nor an item, with the same word rules. An untyped laboratory order number in the Receiver order identifier or Requester order identifier element of laboratory_test_result.v1 that passes the NHS Number check by chance is now stored under the default rule set. A person word still wins, so an untyped value in an element named NHS number or Patient identifier stays scanned, and a type that names a kind takes precedence over the element name (#5291).

  • The Helm chart’s description and README name config.deployment.profile, the key the chart refuses to render without since 5.7.0, and the README’s install command sets it; the command it showed set the old config.deployment_profile and did not render (chart 25.0.1) (#5341).

Security

Shipped with functional changes because: the advisory reaches only a deployment that trusts several issuers, which no configuration FerroEHR ships does, and its fix changes what such a configuration must state at boot, so it lands on main beside the AQL version attestations already merged for this release; a security-only patch of the last release remains open to the release cut.

  • A Basic user never carries a system/ scope, through ferrohealth-smart 0.9.1 (GHSA-jhg2-jwjp-hq74, CWE-269, CWE-863). A system/ scope granted to a Basic user gave that person every resource of a type, a backend service’s reach. Such a user now refuses the start, naming the user and the scope. Upgrade step: give each Basic user the user/ scopes a person holds, and move each machine on Basic to a client of the authorization server under the client credentials grant (#5003).

  • [auth] scopeless_subjects and role_claims hold per issuer, through ferrohealth-smart 0.8.9 (GHSA-pfgx-xq28-2629, CWE-863, CWE-639). Before it, beside several [[auth.issuer]] tables both lists applied to every trusted issuer’s tokens: a token from any of them whose sub was listed met every SMART on openEHR requirement without a scope, and any of them could assert every role the RBAC checks, ADMIN included. An entry is now written <issuer>#<value> and holds for that issuer alone; beside several issuers a bare entry, or one naming an issuer the section does not trust, refuses the boot. Upgrade step for a deployment with several issuers: write each scopeless_subjects entry as <issuer>#<sub>, and write each role_claims path as <issuer>#<path> for the issuers whose roles count (or set role_claims = [] to read none), since the default role_claims is bare and refused. A deployment with one issuer changes nothing (#5047).

  • The ferroehr-postgres image carries zlib1g 1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+deb13u1 from trixie-security, which fixes CVE-2026-76844 and CVE-2026-85091 (HIGH, heap overflows in zlib’s gzip writer) and CVE-2026-27171 (MEDIUM, an infinite loop in crc32_combine64). The image of 5.6.3 and earlier releases carries 1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+b1, judged affected with the upgrade as its action (security/vex/postgres-os.openvex.json). The ferroehr and ferroehr-viewer images keep the distroless base’s zlib, which neither program loads (security/vex/ferroehr-os.openvex.json) (#5137).

  • The ferroehr and ferroehr-viewer images move to the gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian13:nonroot build of 2026-11-08 (sha256:cc66d222…), whose zlib1g 1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+deb13u1 fixes CVE-2026-76844 and CVE-2026-85091 (HIGH, heap overflows in zlib’s gzip writer) and CVE-2026-27171 (MEDIUM, an infinite loop in crc32_combine64). Neither program loads zlib. The images of 5.6.3 and earlier releases carry 1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+b1, judged affected with the upgrade as its action, as the ferroehr-postgres image of those releases is (security/vex/ferroehr-os.openvex.json) (#5152, #5329).

  • CVE-2026-112321, CVE-2026-112322 and CVE-2026-112323 (memory and CPU exhaustion in kadmind through the AUTH_GSSAPI handler) and CVE-2026-119079 (CPU exhaustion in the KDC decoding an AS-REQ or TGS-REQ) in MIT Kerberos 5 have no Debian fix for trixie and are judged not_affected in ferroehr-postgres. The image carries neither kadmind, a KDC nor libgssrpc, and the PostgreSQL server never decodes either request; the configuration FerroEHR ships enables no GSS-API authentication (security/vex/postgres-os.openvex.json) (#5344).

5.7.0-rc1 - 2026-11-10

5.7.0-rc1 is the first release candidate of 5.7.0, published for testing. 5.6.3 stays the stable release: this pre-release moves neither the latest image tags, the book under /docs/latest/ nor the hosted sandbox, it publishes no crates, and it receives no fixes; the next release candidate or 5.7.0 itself replaces it. Before you try it: the configuration is one table per concern with typed durations and sizes, so run ferroehr config check on your file first, which names every key a release before 5.7.0 read with its replacement, all at once; every person is bound to a demographic PERSON, so each persons issuer needs its [[auth.party]] table and each Basic user its [[authz.party_binding.basic_user]] mapping, with the steps on the book’s bootstrap and migration page; and a deployment whose FerroBRIDGE facade or FerroFED gateway writes to FerroEHR adds its persons issuers only after FerroBRIDGE v0.0.23 and FerroFED v0.0.17 reach it. Party migrations 0027 to 0032, clinical migration 0035 and audit migrations 0023 to 0025 add the binding, SCIM, DPoP replay and refusal tables, columns and codes. Helm chart 25.0.1-rc1 carries appVersion 5.7.0-rc1. Security carries two advisories, GHSA-jhg2-jwjp-hq74 and GHSA-pfgx-xq28-2629, the zlib fixes of CVE-2026-76844, CVE-2026-85091 and CVE-2026-27171 in the three images, and the not_affected judgements of four krb5 CVEs in the PostgreSQL image.

Added

  • AQL reads the attestations of a version: v/attestations and any ATTESTATION attribute below it (is_pending, reason, proof, items, committer, time_committed) under FROM EHR e CONTAINS VERSION v CONTAINS COMPOSITION c, with predicates on attestations and EXISTS, and v/commit_audit/is_pending and v/commit_audit/reason on a commit audit that is an ATTESTATION. SELECT v/attestations returns the list, and a comparison below attestations holds when any attestation matches. The FerroEHR extension function LAST(v/attestations/<path>) reads the most recent attestation, so WHERE LAST(v/attestations/is_pending) = true lists the versions awaiting signature, including one marked pending again after it was signed (#4989).

  • The party binding’s configuration, each table with its boot refusals: [authz.party_binding] (provider as one table or one table per tenant, namespace, basic_user), [authz.import] trusted_systems, [[authz.system_client]] (the provider, facilities, templates and origins of each client-credentials client that commits) and [[authz.federation.agreement]] (what a federation issuer’s external persons or organisation may do, on which legal ground), with [authz.rbac] role_issuers and import_role. A template an agreement or a system client writes that the store does not hold refuses the start. The boot line and GET /management/info list the issuers with their kind and identifier issuer, the provider, and every agreement with its accessor and legal ground, and an agreement that admits an organisation without a named person is logged at warn (#5003).

  • [auth.idp.entra], the Microsoft Graph access of the idp-entra adapter of ferrohealth-smart, which resolves the groups of an Entra ID groups overage for an issuer whose profile sets adapter = "idp-entra" (#5003).

  • [auth.dpop] and [[auth.issuer]] sender_constraint: tokens bound to a DPoP key (RFC 9449) or a mutual-TLS client certificate (RFC 8705), checked on every request. A DPoP proof is recorded by the replica that accepted it, so the Helm chart refuses a sender-constrained issuer on more than one replica (#5003).

  • The login binding reads the local party source on every request, with no cache: the new party migration 0027_binding_side_table adds the indexed binding_identifier, binding_membership and binding_representation relations, written in each party commit’s transaction from the PERSONs of the mapped templates that perform a professional ROLE or represent another person, their GROUP memberships and their representation relationships, and rebuilt from the party versions alone. A login matching two parties, an inactive, abandoned or deleted party, a token without the key claim, a party without the needed marker and unreadable groups are refused with 403 and their binding code; a party store or identity provider that cannot answer is answered 503 (#5004).

  • ferroehr definitions load <path>... stores OPT 1.4 (.opt) and ADL 2 (.adls) definitions before serve, through the validation and versioning of the REST upload. A file already stored with the same text is left alone and other text under a stored id is refused, so a deployment runs it at every start to give its party mapping the templates it needs at boot. deploy/definitions/professional/ holds a professional PERSON and ROLE pair adapted from openEHR CKM archetypes for the development lanes and the quickstart (#5006).

  • The compose quickstart binds its user to a professional PERSON: the ferroehr-definitions one-shot loads the PERSON and ROLE templates the party mapping names before the server starts, and ferroehr-provision creates the user through /scim/v2/Users with a token of the development issuer, then reports healthy, so docker compose up --wait returns once the login is bound. The Helm chart (23.3.0) takes definitions.files, which an init container stores with ferroehr definitions load before the server container starts. The conformance, browser and Kubernetes lanes load the same templates and provision every login they use through SCIM, with the committed test client of docs/conformance/party/scim/ (#5006).

  • ferroehr party-binding adopt <PARTY_ID>... gives each prepared PERSON of an existing deployment a professional ROLE of the mapping’s role template, with the PERSON as performer, and a new PERSON version listing it in roles, all in one demographic CONTRIBUTION committed by the first administrator named with --admin or --admin-key, and writes one access record per adopted PERSON through the configured audit trail. It refuses the whole adoption, naming them, while any listed PERSON’s key was introduced by a committer that is no [[scim.client]], named administrator or --migration, so a key planted before the upgrade is never adopted. A PERSON that already performs the ROLE is reported and left alone. The report is JSON on stdout (#5009).

  • ferroehr party-binding check is the read-only pre-flight of a migration to party binding, and the one report of the provisional persons just-in-time creation left incomplete. It reads the party versions alone, so it runs before any boot fill, and writes nothing. Per key issuer it reports the PERSONs that carry a binding key, every selector value two PERSONs carry, the inactive and abandoned ones, the provisional ones older than provisional_report_days, the key-bearing ones that perform no professional ROLE, and every mapped Basic user with the PERSON it binds. For each key it names the committer of the version that introduced it, and fails unless that committer is a [[scim.client]], an administrator named with --admin or --admin-key, a migration declared with --migration, or just-in-time creation on an issuer with jit = true. --expected <file> lists every login of the identity provider with no PERSON. The report is JSON on stdout, and the command exits non-zero on a duplicate, a missing person or a key that fails the provenance rule (#5009).

  • At boot, FerroEHR logs a warn naming every Basic user mapped in [[authz.party_binding.basic_user]] while [authz.assurance] minimum is unset: a Basic credential carries no assurance level, so such a person is never refused on patient data (#5009).

  • The one PERSON mapping SCIM provisioning, just-in-time creation and the login binding share: [[authz.party_binding.person.template]] with the binding key, userName and externalId selectors of each template, [[authz.party_binding.person.attribute]] with the SCIM attribute, the OpenID Connect claim and the path of each mapped value, and [authz.party_binding.professional_role], [authz.party_binding.group], [authz.party_binding.membership] and [authz.party_binding.representation]. Boot refuses a mapping that breaks one of its rules, naming the key, including a template that is absent, rooted at another class or lacks a mapped path, and deleting a template the mapping names is refused with 409 (#5013).

  • The new party migration 0028_binding_selectors holds each binding key, userName (compared after RFC 8265 width mapping, lower case and NFC), externalId and group displayName to one live party, so a commit giving one a second party is refused with 409. The first boot fills the side table under the mapping’s digest, a replica with another mapping refuses to start, and ferroehr party-binding refill rebuilds it after a mapping change, refusing while a replica runs and naming the parties when a value is carried twice (#5013).

  • POST /admin/party/binding-key re-keys a PERSON’s binding key: it refuses the administrator’s own login and a key already bound, retires the old key in the same commit and writes one access record carrying both (#5013).

  • [scim] mounts the SCIM 2.0 service provider at /scim/v2/ (off by default): [[scim.client]] declares each provisioning client by issuer, client_id, scope and binding_issuer, and public_base_url names the origin its documents hang off. /scim/v2/ServiceProviderConfig answers without a token; /ResourceTypes and /Schemas answer a declared client acting for nobody that holds its scope, within [server.caller_rate]. Every refusal is an RFC 7644 Error message. The start is refused for a client of a non-machines issuer, one declared twice, two clients sharing a binding_issuer, or a binding_issuer no [[auth.party]] table carries (#5014).

  • The SCIM endpoint answers the Microsoft Entra ID provisioning client as Microsoft’s “Develop a SCIM endpoint” guide documents it: a value-filtered attribute such as emails[type eq "work"].value serves its type and declares primary read-only, so the primary Entra sends is ignored (RFC 7644 §3.3); a PATCH of userName renames the User; and the Test Connection probes are answered with an empty ListResponse and 404. ferroehr config check refuses a [scim] the person mapping cannot serve, as serve does. The Helm chart exposes config.scim and routes /scim/v2 on every Ingress host when it is enabled, and the book walks an operator through provisioning from Entra ID, with the Workload Identity Federation checks the authorization server makes (#5014).

  • /scim/v2/Users/{id} takes PUT, PATCH and DELETE: a write commits the next version of the professional’s PERSON, clearing a mapped attribute a PUT leaves out, keeping the binding key and externalId, and moving the lifecycle state by active (complete or incomplete to inactive or abandoned and back, an abandoned User completed in two versions, an attribute change to an inactive User refused until it is reactivated). DELETE logically deletes the PERSON and its professional ROLE in one CONTRIBUTION and leaves the binding key as a tombstone. An If-Match naming another version is 412, and ServiceProviderConfig declares PATCH. [scim] max_deactivations and deactivation_window_minutes bound the deactivations and deletions of one client, counted in the database so replicas share the bound, with 429 past it (#5014).

  • /scim/v2/Users serves a client’s Users: POST creates the professional’s PERSON and its professional ROLE in one demographic CONTRIBUTION, complete when the template holds in full and incomplete otherwise, GET /Users/{id} answers with the version’s entity tag and 304 to a matching If-None-Match, and GET /Users answers a ListResponse filtered by eq and and over userName, externalId and id, with any other filter 400 invalidFilter. A client sees only the Users whose binding key its binding_issuer issues, every SCIM request is an access record of the client naming the PERSON, and ServiceProviderConfig declares entity tags. The start is refused when [scim] is on and the party mapping has no default person template with a user_name selector or no professional role (#5014).

  • /scim/v2/Groups serves SCIM Groups as demographic GROUPs of [authz.party_binding.group], each member holding an inline PARTY_RELATIONSHIP of [authz.party_binding.membership] from its PERSON to the GROUP, with no ROLE minted: create, read, eq/and filters on displayName, externalId and id, excludedAttributes=members, PATCH (answered 204), PUT and DELETE, with the entity tags of Users. A Group belongs to the client that created it, its members are that client’s Users, its displayName is unique, and its externalId sits under the client’s group_identifier_issuer. A remove of members with a value list removes only those members, an Entra compatibility deviation from RFC 7644 §3.5.2.2. Deleting a User removes its memberships in the same CONTRIBUTION. [scim] max_group_members (default 5000) caps a Group (#5015).

  • Just-in-time creation of a provisional PERSON at a first login, off by default and enabled per persons issuer in a new [[authz.party_binding.issuer]] table (jit, guests_jit, user_name_claim, idp_claim, admit_idp, admit_groups, admit_roles, admit_assurance). A login of a person or a delegated caller that matches no party and meets every declared admission condition commits one 553|incomplete| PERSON holding the binding key, the userName and the name claims of the access token, with its professional ROLE, as a creation by the person, and is served bound to it; any other mapped attribute is written only where its mapping sets jit = true, and externalId never. Concurrent first requests commit one PERSON, a deprovisioned or inactive login is never recreated, a taken userName refuses the login, and a SCIM client of the key’s issuer completes the PERSON. Boot refuses jit without an admission condition or a mapping that can write it. ferroehr party-binding check lists the provisional persons older than [authz.party_binding] provisional_report_days (default 30) (#5016).

  • A party of a mapped template is validated against that template on every demographic write: a PERSON or GROUP whose archetype_details.template_id names a template of the shared party mapping, and a PARTY_RELATIONSHIP of its membership archetype. A 532|complete| version must meet every constraint, and a 553|incomplete| one may miss mandatory nodes but nothing it carries may be wrong (RM common master06 §Incomplete Content); the refusal is a 422 naming each failing path. Every other party keeps the reference-model checks alone, so parties created through the Demographic API under other templates are accepted as before (#5042).

  • The FHIR AuditEvent, the DICOM audit message and the ITI-20 syslog feed carry the binding fields of the access record: the binding outcome, the party and its groups, the provider acted for, the facilities of a system commit, the representation with its relationship, the actor chain, the external accessor’s asserted fields and the agreement with its legal ground, consent and access class, and a chained request’s correlation id. ehds-logging 0.5.1 writes them as the ehds-accessor and ehds-relayed entities, in the DICOM message as participant objects of type Other. The FHIR record also writes the external and system acting modes. FerroEHR moves to ehds-logging and ihe-atna 0.5.1 and ihe-iti 0.0.77 (#5043).

  • A bound representative reaches only the EHR whose EHR_STATUS names the subject it represents. Every composition, EHR_STATUS, directory, contribution and query request is held to that EHR whatever the token’s scopes cover, and a query must name it with ehr_id. A representative whose token names a subject its party has no live representation relationship to, or whose issuer no [[auth.party]] table binds, is refused with 403 and refused-representation-unrecorded (#5086).

  • The Helm chart (23.1.0) accepts bridge.cdr.oauth.tokenEndpoint for an authorization server whose metadata FerroBRIDGE cannot read at bridge.cdr.oauth.issuer. FerroBRIDGE then requests its client credentials token from that endpoint, and issuer still names the machines issuer the CDR trusts (#5093).

  • A MyHealth@EU contact point’s caller (a contact_point = true federation issuer) reaches patient data only for the patient of its treatment relationship confirmation. The token’s ehdsi.patient.id (system|value) is resolved to its EHR through the EHR index, and every patient-data request must name that EHR. A token without it is refused with 403 and ERROR_SEC_DATA_INTEGRITY_NOT_ENSURED, recorded as refused-trc-missing. Another patient’s EHR, an unknown EHR and a request naming no EHR all answer one 404 of the new problem type trc-patient-mismatch, carrying the agreement service’s *_NOT_FOUND code and recorded as a refused-trc-patient-mismatch security event (eHDSI XCA Profile 8.0.1 §4.2.1, §4.2.2). A contact point’s person agreement now names its ehdsi_service; upgrade step: set it, and list the issuer in [smart] patient_issuers (#5102).

  • An external person under an agreement with discard discards a dispensation of a listed template, as a logical delete, within discard_window_hours and from the same point of care: the dispensation’s health_care_facility carries the token’s provider identifier and its eHDSI organization-id. A token carrying permissions records and discards a dispensation only with PPD-046 (eHDSI SAML Profile 10.0.0 §2.5) (#5102).

  • A read under a federation agreement with a consent condition is served when the token carries the consent decision reference for its patient (Wabvpz Art. 1(j) and Art. 15a(1)), in the claim or authorization_details member the issuer’s [[auth.federation]] table maps to consent.reference, and refused with 403 without it. The reference is one string, the token’s patient/ grant holds it to the launch-context patient, and the access record carries it with the other external fields. ferrohealth-smart moves to 0.9.3, which reads the field (#5106).

  • Every access record of an authenticated request carries the outcome of the party binding (binding: bound, provisional, external, organisation, system, self or a refused-* code) with the fields it needs: the bound party, its groups, the provider, the guest mark, a representative’s representation, a delegated token’s actor chain, a verified external accessor’s fields and agreement, and the facilities a system caller’s compositions named. acting_mode gains delegated, external and system. The audit migration 0023_binding_outcome.sql adds the columns and restores a per-row digest version: records written before stay version 1 and keep verifying, new records are version 2, and a version-1 record after a version-2 one is refused (#5118).

  • Every refused request is an access record through the gated path, and a refusal of the login binding or of a caller kind carries its refused-* binding code and the party it names. Refusals of tokens that failed verification are budgeted by source network and those of verified callers by issuer and subject, so neither crowds out the other; past a caller’s limit its refusals become one summary record with the count and the EHR ids they named, and past a budget one summary record per issuer and outcome is written. Security-event refusals are recorded for every answered request, and a refusal record the system log cannot take is counted in atna_audit_refusals_unwritten. The limits, windows and budgets are kept per replica (#5119).

  • A chained organisation request under a federation agreement is served only when its token carries the requester’s correlation id in the claim or attested authorization_details member the issuer’s [[auth.federation]] table maps to correlation_id. Without it the request is refused with 403 and recorded under the binding code refused-correlation-missing (audit migration 0025); a request header never stands in for it. The organisation access record’s agreement carries the id and its source beside the legal ground and the access class. A chained agreement whose issuer maps no correlation_id, or maps it from a constant, refuses the start (#5120).

  • On the MyHealth@EU contact-point route, the committer of an external person names the professional by the HP Identity Assertion’s NameID: DV_IDENTIFIER{issuer = the assertion's issuer, id = the NameID, type = "hp_identifier:<NameID format>"}, beside the voucher’s oauth2 identifier (eHDSI SAML Profile 10.0.0 §2.1), and a dispensation’s discard is a logical delete under the same committer. A contact point’s COMPOSITION must carry the HCPO’s organization-id in EVENT_CONTEXT.health_care_facility.identifiers, under the issuer urn:oasis:names:tc:xspa:1.0:subject:organization-id, beside the provider’s identifier, or it is refused with 422. ferrohealth-smart moves to 0.9.4, which reads ehdsi.assertion.name_id_format and refuses a contact-point token without one of the three formats as ERROR_HPI_INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION; upgrade step: a contact point’s authorization server writes the NameID format into its tokens (#5144).

  • A federation caller above its agreement’s caller_rate, a MyHealth@EU contact point’s included, is answered 429 with Retry-After right after authentication and before any patient lookup, keyed on the token’s subject per replica, and every such refusal is counted into the caller’s summary record (#5149).

  • A deleted SCIM User’s contacts are erased from every version of its PERSON, keeping the name, the binding key and the identifiers for the record-keeping duties that need them. [scim] contact_erasure_minutes (default 0, at most 43200) sets when: 0 erases them in the DELETE itself, a period leaves them to a sweep that runs every minute. Each erased version’s node rows are derived again from the new body, its server signature is removed, and the erasure is an access record naming party:<id>#contacts. Party migration 0030 adds the scim_contact_erasure table (#5178).

  • openehr-rm types generic RM type names and paths: typing::RmType parses and prints names such as DV_INTERVAL<DV_QUANTITY>, typing::attribute_type gives an attribute of an instantiated class with the actual argument in place of the formal parameter, and typing::path_type types every step of an RmPath with its container. Each model::RmAttribute and model::RmTypeRef keeps the formal parameter it is written as (formal) beside the resolved bound. paths::write::item_at_path_mut and paths::write::set_at_path write at a path into a canonical instance, positional predicates included, creating the members the path names and changing nothing when a write is refused (#5187).

  • openehr-sdt: flat::navigate::Navigator gives every instance of a Web Template path in a composition, with each step’s occurrence, container index, positional path and JSON pointer, reaching a renamed instance where the template’s name is redundant and an OPT2 archetype root through the complete identifier the template recorded. flat::navigate::relative compares two paths step by step. flat::attribute_keys gives the FLAT key of an RM attribute of a structural class (the master05-rm_mapping.adoc tables, checked against them). A WebTemplateNode carries facts (the embedded template id of an OPT 1.4 archetype root and the terms its archetype defines) and every coded option its terminology, so no consumer walks the operational template (#5189).

  • openehr-base gives identifier and time parts as written: ObjectVersionId::object_id_str and ObjectVersionId::versioned_object_id keep the case of the object_id part, Iso8601Time::fraction_digits and Iso8601DateTime::fraction_digits return the digits of the fractional second as text, and Iso8601Duration::parts returns each component’s designator and number verbatim (DurationDesignator, DurationPart), with Iso8601Duration::fraction_digits for the seconds (#5190).

  • openehr-its reads the ITS-REST ETag as a typed entity tag: rest::etag::EntityTag parses and writes the RFC 9110 form, weak or strong, with the weak and strong comparisons. It types the tag as an ObjectVersionId or a HierObjectId. Every generated response-headers struct that carries an ETag gains entity_tag() beside the raw etag field (#5191).

  • openehr-term names the null_flavours and setting groups: codes::NullFlavour and codes::Setting give each concept’s code and English rubric and read a code back, held equal to the bundled terminology by tests. Every typed group’s ALL is now a slice (#5192).

  • openehr-am: HridRef reads an archetype reference with the version precision it was written at (VersionPrecision: major, minor or full, BASE Artefact Identification §Referencing), gives the version as written and matches an ArchetypeHrid by the specification’s rule, the namespace never a wildcard. ArchetypeHrid::local_semantic_id gives the namespace-free interface form a Web Template nodeId carries, which the v2_4 Web Template builder now uses (#5193).

  • openehr-its: rest::stored_query types a stored query’s qualified name (QualifiedQueryName, [{namespace}::]{query-name}, with check_registrable refusing the reserved aql), its version (QueryVersion, major.minor.patch in numeric order) and the version pattern a request addresses (VersionPattern, exact, {major} or {major}.{minor}, selecting the highest match), per ITS-REST 1.1.0. The generated stored-query operations and the StoredQuery and RESULT_SET documents carry them, so a name or version outside the grammar is a 400 where the request is decoded (#5207).

  • openehr_rm::Generation::earliest_for_composition answers the oldest RM generation whose canonical-JSON decode accepts a composition, so a builder can name ARCHETYPED.rm_version without naming a generation module; a value no generation decodes is a typed NoGenerationDecodes error carrying every generation’s refusal (#5242).

Changed

  • The published server, viewer and PostgreSQL images take their org.opencontainers.image.base.name and base.digest labels and annotations from the runtime stage’s digest-pinned FROM line at build time, so a base-image bump changes that one line. An image built directly from a Dockerfile no longer carries these two labels (#4953).

  • [auth] takes the ferrohealth-smart 0.9 shape. Every trusted issuer is an [[auth.issuer]] table with a required kind (persons, patients, machines or federation) and a profile (rfc9068 by default, or entra, keycloak, okta, nl), and holds every setting of its tokens itself. A configuration in the old shape refuses the start, naming what replaces it. Upgrade steps: write a flat issuer = "…" as an [[auth.issuer]] table; move audience, algorithms, clock_skew_seconds, jwks_max_age_seconds, jwks_refresh_interval_seconds, jwks_file, timeout_ms, mode, role_claims and [auth.introspection] onto each issuer table ([auth.issuer.introspection]); give each issuer its kind, with patients and professionals at separate issuers (a realm or tenant each), since one issuer is one kind; replace token_profile = "jwt" with token_types = ["JWT"] and the required_claims the issuer’s tokens carry, and drop token_profile = "rfc9068"; and write each scopeless_subjects entry as { issuer = "…", sub = "…" } (#5003).

  • A persons token is admitted only through a client its issuer lists in first_party_clients or delegates. Upgrade step: list the deployment’s own clients, the viewer’s among them, in first_party_clients, and a third-party client that acts for a person in delegates. The other 0.9 profile keys (person_key, tenant_claim, client_claims, app_only, guest, impersonation_marker, expect, user_claims, person_equality, unstable_claims, max_actor_chain, representation, scope_claim, app_only_scope_claim, adapter, sender_constraint and the onward_* keys) are documented in the configuration reference (#5003).

  • An array of tables, such as [[auth.issuer]], is set from the environment by element index (FERROEHR__AUTH__ISSUER__0__ISSUER), through ferrohealth-config 0.2.10 (#5003).

  • [smart] issuer_metadata_file is the metadata of the [auth] issuer it names, wherever that issuer stands in the list, and a file naming no [auth] issuer refuses the start. The SMART discovery document describes the first introspected issuer, else that named issuer, else the first issuer whose metadata is read from it, else the first issuer, so a Basic users’ issuer listed first no longer takes the discovery document (#5003).

  • The family crates move together: ferrohealth-smart 0.9.1, ferrohealth-authz 0.3.0, ferrohealth-session 0.3.1, ihe-atna and ehds-logging 0.4.0, ihe-iti 0.0.76, ferrohealth-config 0.2.10, ferrohealth-server 0.5.1 and ferrohealth-ui 0.6.9. ihe-atna and ehds-logging now escape every control and bidirectional formatting character of a value they write as its code point. With ferrohealth-ui 0.6.9 the viewer’s session watch no longer throws when the party relationship form, which holds a control named target, is submitted (#5003).

  • The terminology client moves to ferrobridge-term 0.1.143 (FerroBRIDGE v0.0.22), which takes the ferrohealth-smart 0.9 token source (#5003).

  • Every person is bound to a demographic party, with no switch. A persons issuer needs its [[auth.party]] table, two issuers of one node may not share an audience, and [authz.party_binding] provider (the healthcare provider the deployment acts for, EHDS Art. 13(4) and Annex II 3.2(a)) is required once [auth] admits a credential; each refuses the start naming what to set. A Basic user is a person: it maps to the binding key of its PERSON in [[authz.party_binding.basic_user]] (user, key_issuer, key), and a Basic user without a mapping refuses the start, naming the user. Upgrade steps: add an [[auth.party]] table to each persons issuer, set provider, and map each Basic user under the identifier_issuer of an [[auth.party]] table, which needs a persons issuer; a deployment of Basic users alone declares one whose jwks_file is a key set that signs nothing, as the quickstart and the sandbox do (#5003).

  • A token grants [authz.rbac] admin_role, emergency_access_role, import_role and identifier_reader_role only when its issuer is listed in the new [authz.rbac] role_issuers, each a persons issuer; any other kind refuses the start. Upgrade step: list the issuers whose role claims grant these roles; a Basic user keeps the roles its own table grants (#5003).

  • The compose quickstart, the dev and conformance stacks, the hosted sandbox and the Helm chart’s Basic overlays bind their Basic users under a persons issuer that signs nothing: its key set, which every FerroEHR image carries at /opt/sandbox-posture/basic-users-jwks.json, is the public half of a key pair whose private key was discarded (#5003).

  • The quickstart has one copy. docker-compose.yml on main pulls the FerroEHR images at :main and carries main’s configuration, which CI checks with the server image the change builds; the copy attached to each release pulls that release’s images, written by the release lane, which refuses a copy that still names :main. Download the release asset (releases/latest/download/docker-compose.yml) to run a release (#5003).

  • The Helm chart moves to 22.0.0. config.auth.issuer is a list of issuer tables, each with its kind, profile and audience, and values.yaml exposes config.auth.party, config.authz.party_binding, config.authz.rbac.role_issuers, config.authz.system_client and config.authz.federation.agreement. The chart refuses an issuer with sender_constraint: required beside replicaCount above 1 or autoscaling. Upgrade steps: rewrite config.auth as the [auth] upgrade above describes, set config.authz.party_binding.provider, and list the issuers whose roles grant the administrator role in config.authz.rbac.role_issuers (#5003).

  • A caller bound to a demographic PERSON commits under the committer the server writes: a PARTY_IDENTIFIED with the PERSON’s name, the login identifier (the issuer profile’s person_key value under the token issuer, type oauth2, or the Basic user under ferroehr, type basic), the provider identifier (type healthcare-provider) and an external_ref to the PERSON, on every commit path, attestations and CONTRIBUTIONs included. Upgrade: stop sending a committer, or send the placeholder {"_type": "PARTY_IDENTIFIED", "identifiers": [{"_type": "DV_IDENTIFIER", "issuer": "<iss>", "id": "<sub>"}]}, which must name the authenticated caller; a stated committer with another name, identifier or external_ref, and a stated PARTY_RELATED, is refused with 403 (#5005).

  • A patient’s committer is PARTY_SELF with no external_ref, and a representative commits as a PARTY_RELATED naming their own PERSON and the coded relationship. A patient-context token commits no demographic version. Upgrade: read the person’s own entries by the committer’s PARTY_SELF type, not by its former external_ref (#5005).

  • Importing an EHR Extract needs the role [authz.rbac] import_role names, or a system/ caller, and a wrapped committer naming a party or a login of this deployment is refused unless its version was created by a system [authz.import] trusted_systems lists. Upgrade: set import_role and give it to the accounts that import (#5005).

  • A person of a persons issuer whose login no demographic party carries is refused with 403 and refused-unbound on every request, with no fallback to a login-only committer. The problem names the identifier issuer to provision the person under, a token without the key claim is refused with a problem naming that claim, and each refusal counts into the new binding_refusals metric by issuer and outcome. The Keycloak quickstart overlay provisions its four demo users through SCIM with the ferroehr-provision-keycloak one-shot. Upgrade: provision every professional (through SCIM or the demographic API) before you add a persons issuer to the upgraded deployment (#5006).

  • A deployment whose FerroBRIDGE facade or FerroFED gateway writes to FerroEHR adds its persons issuers only after the bridge and the gateway reach it under the caller: FerroBRIDGE v0.0.23 and FerroFED v0.0.17. Until then the committer rule refuses their writes. FerroFED v0.0.17 follows this release, so a deployment with a FerroFED gateway adds its persons issuers only once that release is out. The book’s new “Party binding: bootstrap and migration” page carries the bootstrap path, the four migration steps and these prerequisites, and “Breaking changes of party binding” lists every incompatible change with its upgrade step (#5009).

  • The hosted sandbox follows the bootstrap path of party binding: its configuration declares the sandbox-scim client ([[scim.client]], with the development issuer trusted as a machines issuer for it), the box’s new ferroehr-provision service provisions the demo PERSON through /scim/v2/ after every reset, and scripts/sandbox/reseed.sh waits for the demo login to bind before it seeds, then checks the committer of the marker’s EHR_STATUS version references a PERSON. The deploy probe’s new bootstrap family (P-BOOTSTRAP-01) shows the compose quickstart does the same from an empty database: the quickstart user is a User of the SCIM client, and a commit of the Basic user names that PERSON (#5009).

  • With a party mapping configured, the parties the login binding relies on are written through the demographic API by an administrator (authz.rbac.admin_role) only: a PERSON of a mapped template carrying a binding key, userName or externalId, its professional ROLE, a representation relationship, and a GROUP of the group template. Any other caller’s write is refused with 403, a version that changes a present binding key is refused with 403, and an administrator’s version that leaves a protected identifier out is refused with 422. Upgrade: write these parties as an administrator, and change a key through POST /admin/party/binding-key (#5013).

  • FerroEHR records every DPoP proof it accepts in its PostgreSQL database until the proof’s window ends, so a proof is accepted once across all replicas, and a proof replayed to another replica is refused there (RFC 9449 §11.1). If the database cannot record a proof, the request is refused with 503. The Helm chart (22.1.0) no longer refuses an issuer with sender_constraint: required beside replicaCount above 1 or autoscaling (#5072).

  • An AQL query scoped to one EHR now takes the streaming plan shape whatever its ORDER BY, DISTINCT or aggregates, whether the EHR comes from the ehr_id request parameter or from an ehr_id/value equality in the query. On a store of 100,000 compositions such a query used to spend 16 to 64 ms in PostgreSQL’s planner for an execution of about 1 ms, on every new connection and every new statement text; it now plans in 1 to 3 ms (#5076).

  • The Helm chart (23.0.0) connects FerroBRIDGE to the CDR as a machine. FerroBRIDGE uses an OAuth 2.0 client credentials client of a machines issuer that the CDR trusts, set in bridge.cdr.oauth (issuer, clientId, and optionally scope, audience and resource). The client secret comes from the client_secret key of bridge.cdr.existingSecret. The chart no longer accepts a Basic user for this connection: from ferrohealth-smart 0.9 a Basic credential belongs to a person and holds no system/ scope. The chart refuses to render when bridge.cdr.oauth.issuer is not listed in config.auth.issuer with kind: machines. To upgrade, add that issuer, create the client, and replace the user and password keys of the Secret with client_secret (#5085).

  • A verified external person’s commit records the professional as its committer: a PARTY_IDENTIFIED with the asserted name, the hp_identifier under the issuer "<country_code>:<issuing_authority_name>" and the token’s iss and sub, with no external_ref. A country code that is no upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, or an issuing authority holding a :, control or bidi character, is refused with 403 naming the field. The COMPOSITION must name the token’s healthcare provider (provider.healthcare_provider_identifier under provider.issuing_authority_name) as its health_care_facility, or it is refused with 422. Upgrade step: map provider.issuing_authority_name in each [[auth.federation]] table whose agreements carry writes, with a constant source where the token does not carry it (#5097).

  • A system caller (an app-only token by its issuer profile’s app_only markers) holds system/ scopes only: a token carrying a user/ or patient/ scope is refused with 403. It commits into an EHR only as a client an [[authz.system_client]] table declares, under the committer PARTY_IDENTIFIED{name = <client>, identifiers = [{issuer = <iss>, id = <client>, type = "client"}]}, and each COMPOSITION it commits must be of a template its writes lists (403), name a facility its facilities lists in context.health_care_facility, or in feeder_audit.originating_system_audit.location when it has no context (422), and be either a device act from a device client or a relayed person act naming the professional by an identifier from a relay client. Upgrade: declare every client that commits in [[authz.system_client]] with its writes, facilities and origins, and give its compositions the facility identifier (#5100).

  • An attestation is accepted only from a caller bound to a professional PERSON; one from a patient, a representative, a system caller or an unbound caller is refused with 403. Upgrade: attest under the professional’s own token (#5100).

  • A guest of a persons issuer, by its profile’s guest markers, is refused with 403 (refused-guest) unless the issuer’s [[auth.party]] table sets guests = true. Upgrade: set guests = true on the issuers whose guests act under your responsibility (#5100).

  • A verified external person or organisation of a federation issuer is admitted only under the [[authz.federation.agreement]] of its issuer and accessor, holding no scope beyond the agreement’s reads, and is an access-service caller by its kind: an opted-out EHR answers 404 to it, and only an external person under an agreement with opt_out_override reaches one under an emergency purpose. It commits only a COMPOSITION of a template the agreement’s writes lists (an organisation nothing), and a read under a consent-conditioned agreement, and every request under an NL agreement, is refused until the consent decision reference and the Wabvpz Art. 15f roles can be read. Upgrade: declare an agreement for every federation issuer and accessor, list the issuer in [smart] patient_issuers, and give its tokens only the patient/ scopes the agreement reads (#5101).

  • Under an NL [[authz.federation.agreement]], Wabvpz Art. 15f now decides admission in place of the refusal of every request. A caller whose nl.role is the UZI role 01.008 (bedrijfsarts) or 01.048 (verzekeringsarts) is refused with 403 as refused-wabvpz-role, and a caller whose nl.organisation_type is missing or is not a care provider type of Nictiz’s OrganisatieTypeCodelijst is refused with 403 as refused-wabvpz-organisation-type, so an insurer is refused. Every NL agreement declares purpose = "care"; one without a purpose, or for a keuring, refuses the start. The code lists are vendored by scripts/vendor/nl-role-codes.sh into docs/specs/nl-role-codes/. Upgrade: add purpose = "care" to every NL agreement and map nl.organisation_type (and nl.role for persons) in its issuer’s [[auth.federation]] table (#5107).

  • A delegated token’s access record now has acting_mode = "delegated" where it had client, and a system caller’s system. The FHIR rendering still names a delegated access as a client one. Upgrade: a review query that selects delegated access by acting_mode = 'client' also selects 'delegated' (#5118).

  • FerroEHR builds on ferrohealth-server 0.6.1, whose public caller-rate take holds a federation caller to its agreement’s caller_rate. Its 0.6.0 break, the revocation feature’s move to der 0.8, touches no feature FerroEHR enables (#5149).

  • The source tree no longer carries the UZI role code CodeSystem (uzi-rolcode) of Nictiz’s zib 2020 package: its codes and titles reproduce the UZI-register CPS, which CIBG does not license for reproduction. scripts/vendor/nl-role-codes.sh writes it into the git-ignored .vendor-cache/nl-role-codes/, as it does the CPS, and --test-inputs fetches only what the Wabvpz tests read. Nictiz’s care provider types stay under docs/specs/nl-role-codes/. Run scripts/vendor/nl-role-codes.sh --test-inputs once before running the ferroehr-rest tests (#5175).

  • [auth] takes three boot refusals from ferrohealth-smart: a Basic user’s hash below the Argon2id floor (m=19456, t=2, p=1), an issuer that carries userinfo, and private or symmetric key material in a jwks_file. They are refused as before, with the crate’s messages. A jwks_file that is no JWK Set now refuses the start where the crate reads the key set (#5209).

  • The family crates move together to one ferrohealth-smart: 0.13.1, with ferrohealth-authz 0.7.0, ferrohealth-session 0.7.0, ihe-atna and ehds-logging 0.8.0, ihe-iti 0.0.83, ferrohealth-server 0.6.4 and ferrobridge-term 0.1.148. The 0.13 line refuses a JSON document it cannot read without quoting it (GHSA-mhv7-3975-6xq3), so a jwks_file or [smart] issuer_metadata_file that does not parse is refused at boot with the crate’s message, which names the failure class and position; 0.13.1 keeps a refused key set, introspection or metadata body out of the error (GHSA-5qm7-v4fw-p2v9). The OAuth client credentials tables ([authz.abac.remote.oauth], [ehr_index.oauth], [terminology.oauth] and [audit.fhir_feed.oauth]) read as before (#5209).

  • The API’s response security headers come from the family server stack (ferrohealth-server 0.6.2) with the same six headers and values. They now also reach the management listener on its own port, and Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000 is sent when FerroEHR or the viewer serves TLS itself ([server.tls], RFC 6797 §7.2). The viewer gains Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-site (#5210).

  • The server and the viewer read the parts of an OBJECT_VERSION_ID through openehr-base and its BASE grammar, never by cutting at ::. A value that is no OBJECT_VERSION_ID now names no version: the AQL branch refusal, the version item tags and the viewer’s version numbers leave it alone, a reference to a container is read as the whole value (so uuid::extension no longer names the container uuid), and the viewer’s deletes refuse it before calling the CDR. Every part keeps its case (#5211).

  • ETag and If-Match values are read through openehr-its’s RFC 9110 entity tag on the server and in the viewer. The server accepts the same forms as before. The viewer reads its CDR’s ETag strictly: a value that is no entity tag names no version (#5212).

  • The viewer’s audit screen reads the ITI-81 searchset and each AuditEvent as FHIR R4 resources, and a refusal’s OperationOutcome too. A searchset that is no FHIR R4 Bundle of AuditEvents now shows as a failed read, never as a page of empty rows (#5214).

  • The EHR index’s boot check reads the PIX Manager’s CapabilityStatement through ihe-iti’s PIXm client, with its transport and its client-credentials token, so a Manager behind IUA answers the probe as it answers ITI-83. A failed probe is reported as the client’s refusal: no answer, the status it answered, or no FHIR R4 CapabilityStatement (#5216).

  • [audit.syslog] reads its TLS material from [audit.syslog.tls], the outbound TLS table of every FerroHEALTH product (trust_roots_file, client_identity_file or client_identity, min_version), and hands ihe-atna the rustls configuration ferrohealth-server builds from it. The keys tls_ca_file, tls_identity_cert_file and tls_identity_key_file are retired and refused at boot by name: name the roots file as trust_roots_file, and concatenate the client certificate chain and its private key into the one PEM client_identity_file names. The client speaks TLS 1.3 unless min_version = "1.2" lowers it (#5217).

  • A SCIM Group membership is now held by the member: an inline PARTY_RELATIONSHIP from the member’s PERSON to the GROUP, stored in the PERSON’s version (RM demographic §Party Relationships). A membership change versions only that PERSON, so its cost no longer grows with the Group’s size. The GROUP is versioned only by a rename, an externalId change or its deletion. The Group’s members is read from the membership index (#5220).

  • A Group’s ETag is now its GROUP version plus a membership revision, so it still changes with every membership change. The member User’s ETag now changes too, while its body stays the same (#5220).

  • Deactivating a User (active = false) drops all of its memberships in the same version, because an inactive PERSON cannot be versioned again. A reactivated User belongs to no Group until its client adds it again (#5220).

  • Microsoft Entra ID’s disable-then-remove order now succeeds, since the later remove finds nothing to remove. An add naming an inactive User is 400 invalidValue (“reactivate the User first”) (#5220).

  • A refused SCIM write now names the rule it breaks in detail (#5220).

  • scripts/perf/scim-groups.sh keeps the database log, df -h and free -m of a failed run (#5220).

  • A party commit no longer re-derives the login binding’s side table, the reverse-relationship index and the protection check from the whole stored body. Each hook reads what the committed body holds, derived once in memory, and writes only the rows that changed, and ferroehr party-binding refill derives the rows with the same code. A party commit without a server signature no longer reassembles its body. A membership change at the cap of a 5 000-member SCIM Group went from 810 ms to 358 ms at p99 on a developer laptop (#5220).

  • openehr-rm writes the RFC 8785 canonical form a VERSION signature covers in one pass over the version, sorting each object’s members by reference. A 3.3 MB GROUP version canonicalises about seven times faster than through serde_jcs, with byte-identical output, so signed versions verify unchanged. serde_jcs remains the test oracle (#5220).

  • The stored-query service takes the typed name, version and version pattern of openehr_its::rest::stored_query end to end, so it reads one grammar with the REST layer: the three-part {namespace}::{formalism}::{query-name} name, which ITS-REST 1.1.0 Qualified_query_name.md does not define, is no longer accepted anywhere (the formalism is the query_type parameter), and DELETE /admin/query/{qualified_query_name}/{version} answers 400 for a name outside [{namespace}::]{query-name} or a version that is no exact major.minor.patch, where it answered 404 (#5223).

  • Boot and ferroehr config check refuse an [[auth.party]] table whose identifier_type is the type of no [[authz.party_binding.person.template]] key, naming the issuer, the type and the types the templates write: no login of such an issuer could ever match a party, and every one would be refused. Upgrade step: give the deployment a person template whose key carries the table’s identifier_type (or set the table to the type the template writes). The Helm CI and production values and the hosted sandbox now carry the professional PERSON and ROLE mapping, and the sandbox loads the two templates before the CDR starts (#5231).

  • openehr_query::printer::to_aql writes each WHERE comparison with one space on each side of the operator (c/name/value = $nameValue), as the QUERY 1.1.0 AQL syntax examples do; path predicates keep their unspaced form ([ehr_id/value=$ehrUid]). The query builder’s generated AQL follows (#5241).

  • openehr_sdt::flat::navigate::Navigator owns what it copies from its Web Template (the name-fallback table and the OPT2 archetype references) and carries no template lifetime, so a consumer can keep it beside the template it was built from; it is Debug, Clone, Send and Sync (#5243).

  • Breaking: the configuration tree is one table per concern. ferroehr.toml moves to [deployment], [api], [database], [auth] (with [auth.smart] and [auth.scim]), [authz] (with [[authz.origin]]), [management], [audit], [privacy] (with identifier_protection, cohort and access_delay), [record] (with subject_index, versioning, signing, query, change_feed and multimedia), [terminology] and [pixm]. FerroEHR’s own keys take one duration type ("500ms", "30s", "10min", "12h", "7d", UCUM unit codes, so a bare number and m are refused), one size type ("256KiB", "64MiB", IEC binary units, decimal units refused) and one calendar retention period ("P5Y", "P1830D", unset keeps forever). An optional feature is on when its table is present: [terminology], [pixm], [auth.scim], [audit.syslog], [audit.fhir_feed], [privacy.identifier_protection] and [privacy.access_delay] carry no enabled; [authz.abac], [record.multimedia] and [auth.smart] keep a switch because some of their keys apply while off. record.subject_index has no default, so the server refuses to start until "pixm" or "local" is chosen. [api.cors] replaces cors_permissive with the Fetch Standard response headers (allow_origins, allow_methods, allow_headers, expose_headers, allow_credentials, max_age). The environment follows the tree (FERROEHR__DB__URL is FERROEHR__DATABASE__URL, FERROEHR__EHR_INDEX__PROVIDER is FERROEHR__RECORD__SUBJECT_INDEX). The Helm chart moves to its 25 line with config: on the same tree. Every key a release before v5.7.0 read is refused at load with its replacement named, all at once, so ferroehr config check --config <old file> prints the whole move list; the refusals ship in v5.7.0 only and the next release removes them. To upgrade, run config check on the old file and move each key it names: spec_profile, deployment_profile, deployment_accepts and licence.file are deployment.spec_profile, deployment.profile, deployment.accepts and deployment.licence_file; [rest] is [api] (swagger_ui is openapi_ui, body_limit_bytes is body_limit, cors_permissive = true is [api.cors] allow_origins = ["*"], [rest.identity] is [api.options] with solution and vendor; the version keys are facts of the build), admin.enabled is api.admin and terminology.api_enabled is api.terminology; [db] is [database] (acquire_timeout_secs is acquire_timeout, statement_timeout_ms is statement_timeout, migrate is migrations), [storage.<domain>] is [database.<domain>] and [storage.migrate.<domain>] url is [database.<domain>] migrate_url; [smart] is [auth.smart] (enabled is discovery, episode.enabled is episode_launch, launch_base64_json = true is "launch-base64-json" in auth.capabilities); [scim] is [auth.scim] (max_results is filter_max_results, deactivation_window_minutes is deactivation_window, contact_erasure_minutes is contact_erasure_delay); [authz.abac.cedar] reload_secs is reload_interval, [authz.abac.remote] server, connect_timeout_ms and request_timeout_ms are url, connect_timeout and timeout, authz.party_binding.provisional_report_days is provisional_report_after, and an agreement’s discard_window_hours and chained_log_retention_years are discard_window and chained_log_retention; [[origins.registered]] is [[authz.origin]]; management.port is management.listen (an address:port) and management.profiling.max_seconds is max_duration; audit.store.retention_days and retention_years are audit.store.retention, verify_interval_seconds and full_verify_interval_seconds are verify_interval and full_verify_interval; [audit.syslog] host and port are url = "tls://host:port", spool_max_messages is spool_max_events, spool_max_bytes is spool_max_size, retry_max_ms is retry.max_backoff, and [audit.fhir_feed] poll_interval_ms and retry_max_ms are poll_interval and retry.max_backoff; [demographic.identifier_protection] is [privacy.identifier_protection], [cohort] is [privacy.cohort], and [access_delay] is [privacy.access_delay] with hours as max_delay; ehr_index.provider is record.subject_index ("ihe" is "pixm") and the rest of [ehr_index] is [pixm] (pixm_url is url, invocation is method, request_timeout_ms is timeout); versioning.skip_identical_resend is record.versioning.idempotent_resend; [signing] is [record.signing] (key_path is key_file, retired_key_paths is retired_key_files), [query] is [record.query] (timeout_ms is timeout), [outbox] is [record.change_feed] (retention_days is retention, prune_interval_secs is prune_interval), and [multimedia] is [record.multimedia] (endpoint is url, threshold_bytes is threshold, and allow_http is retired: an http:// url is plain HTTP); [terminology.server] is [terminology] (fail_on_error is on_error = "accept" | "refuse", request_timeout_ms is timeout). The family sections take the same types, from ferrohealth-server 0.8, ferrohealth-telemetry 0.4, ferrohealth-smart 0.15 and ferrohealth-session 0.9: [server] request_timeout_ms, header_read_timeout_ms, idle_timeout_ms, drain_delay_ms, shutdown_timeout_ms and retry_after_s are request_timeout, header_read_timeout, idle_timeout, drain_delay, shutdown_timeout and retry_after, body_limit_bytes and compression_min_bytes are body_limit and compression_min_size, and [server.tls] reload_interval_s is reload_interval; [telemetry.otlp] trust_roots_file and client_identity_file move into [telemetry.otlp.tls], and an https:// collector is dialed over it; [auth] ca_file is [auth.tls] trust_roots_file, an [[auth.issuer]] table’s clock_skew_seconds, jwks_max_age_seconds, jwks_refresh_interval_seconds and timeout_ms are clock_skew, jwks_max_age, jwks_refresh_interval and timeout, its introspection cache_max_age_seconds is cache_max_age, [auth.basic] cache_ttl_seconds is cache_ttl, [auth.dpop] max_age_seconds and clock_skew_seconds are max_age and clock_skew, [auth.idp.entra] timeout_ms and max_response_bytes are timeout and max_response_size, and an oauth grant’s ca_file, client_certificate_file and client_key_file are its tls table’s trust_roots_file and client_identity_file (one PEM), with refresh_margin_ms, timeout_ms and previous_key_overlap_ms as refresh_margin, timeout and previous_key_overlap. The [auth] keys v5.6 read for every issuer (audience, algorithms, token_profile, jwks_file, mode, introspection, role_claims and the rest) live on each [[auth.issuer]] table, and scopeless_subjects entries are { issuer, sub } tables. In the viewer, cdr.request_timeout_secs is cdr.timeout, [oidc] ca_file is [oidc.tls] trust_roots_file, [oidc.tls] client_certificate and client_key are client_identity_file, and [session] idle_timeout_s, absolute_timeout_s and sign_in_timeout_s are idle_timeout, absolute_timeout and sign_in_timeout. Each of these is refused in v5.7.0 naming its replacement, in the CDR and the viewer alike (#5259).

  • Breaking: a patients token that names an actor is refused. With ferrohealth-smart 0.15, a patients issuer reads a token whose top-level act (RFC 8693 §4.1) names someone other than the patient only when its [[auth.issuer]] table sets act_represents_patient = true; without it the token is refused 401, where v5.6 admitted it as the patient’s own access. With it, FerroEHR refuses the token 403 (refused-patient-representative), because it binds no party to someone acting for a patient, and the access log records the refusal (#5259).

  • SECURITY.md, security.txt (its Contact: mailto: field), the post-market record, the CRA technical documentation and the book’s compliance pages name security@cadasto.com as the email route for a vulnerability report, in place of info@cadasto.com, which stays the single point of contact for complaints and incidents, the manufacturer’s address on the running server and the address for licensing and other business questions (#5272).

  • ferroehr and ferroehr-viewer run through the FerroHEALTH family’s run path. A configuration either binary refuses (an unknown or invalid key, a broken semantic rule, an [auth] table with no mechanism, a SCIM mapping it cannot serve, or for the viewer a TLS file that does not read or an unusable [oidc] or [session] table) now exits 78 (EX_CONFIG of sysexits(3)) where it exited 1, so an orchestrator can tell a configuration to fix from a failure to retry. Every other failure still exits 1, and the failure is written to stderr as one line with its whole cause, prefixed with the binary’s name. Upgrade: a script or probe that expects exactly 1 from config check on a refused file expects 78 (#5321).

  • Breaking: the outbound integrations take the family’s endpoint table. [terminology], [pixm], [audit.fhir_feed] and [authz.abac.remote] read where they call and how from one [<x>.endpoint] table, the same keys for every outbound integration of every FerroHEALTH product: url, timeout, connect_timeout, retry (max_attempts, initial_backoff, max_backoff), tls (trust_roots_file, client_identity_file, min_version) and credentials (HTTP Basic user with password or password_file, or the client credentials grant [...credentials.oauth]). terminology.url, timeout and [terminology.oauth] are terminology.endpoint.url, timeout and [terminology.endpoint.credentials.oauth]; pixm.url, timeout, [pixm.tls] and [pixm.oauth] are pixm.endpoint.url, timeout, [pixm.endpoint.tls] and [pixm.endpoint.credentials.oauth]; audit.fhir_feed.url, [audit.fhir_feed.retry] and [audit.fhir_feed.oauth] are audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.url, [audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.retry] and [audit.fhir_feed.endpoint.credentials.oauth]; authz.abac.remote.url, connect_timeout, timeout and [authz.abac.remote.oauth] are authz.abac.remote.endpoint.url, connect_timeout, timeout and [authz.abac.remote.endpoint.credentials.oauth]. The v5.6 keys are refused naming their new home. Every client now honours retry: the terminology, PIXm and remote policy clients try a call that got no answer or a 5xx up to max_attempts times (three by default; each tried once before), so set max_attempts = 1 to keep one attempt, and the FHIR feed’s delivery rounds take max_attempts tries each, from initial_backoff, before the round waits max_backoff; the feed still never gives a record up. The environment follows the tree (FERROEHR__TERMINOLOGY__ENDPOINT__URL, FERROEHR__AUDIT__FHIR_FEED__ENDPOINT__URL), and so do the Helm chart’s values and its client secret routing, in the chart’s 25 line (#5331).

  • The FerroEHR PostgreSQL image is built on the 2026-11-09 respin of postgres:18.6 (sha256:e3d24f69…), a same-version respin with rebuilt base packages. A full scan of the rebuilt image on amd64 and arm64 finds the same findings as the image of the previous base, each judged in security/vex/postgres-os.openvex.json, and a gate scan finds no fixable HIGH or CRITICAL finding (#5332).

  • The development and Keycloak example compose files run Keycloak 26.8.2 (quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.8.2@sha256:723b1d6e…). Of the 26.8.2 upgrading notes, the shipped realm meets the ones that touch it: the Admin REST API’s new audience check passes for the master realm’s admin-cli token the browser-test harness uses, and the realm uses no token exchange, identity broker, SAML client, CIBA or dynamic client registration. The ferroehr-service client-credentials token carries the same audience and scopes as under 26.8.1 (#5333).

Removed

  • [authz.professional] (claim, client_tokens, acting_for_claim) and its 403 for a token that names no natural person. The issuer’s kind and profile classify the caller, and the access record’s acting mode and professional come from that classification: a person’s own token is the person, and a delegated token is the client acting for the person it names. Upgrade step: remove the table, which refuses the start, and list a client that acts for a person in its issuer’s delegates (#5003).

  • The named refusal of authz.rbac.user_role, which v5.6 introduced, is gone under the one-release rule for removal aids: the key is now refused as an unknown key when the configuration loads (#5259).

Fixed

  • A 553|incomplete| commit no longer refuses an empty mandatory archetype slot: RM common master06 §Incomplete Content sets every occurrences lower limit to zero, a slot’s included, while too many fillers are still refused. The OPT 1.4 writer now closes a mandatory slot once the fillers placed in it carry its lower bound, as ADL 2 §Slot Filling and Redefinition allows, and still refuses to close one they leave unmet (#5042).

  • The example of a party template whose identity the template marks optional is a party of its class carrying one identity at every detail level, where the required level answered 500: RM demographic PARTY.identities admits no party without one. A party template that constrains no identity at all answers 400 Bad Request naming its class (#5057).

  • An AQL VERSION standard predicate on commit_audit/time_committed applies its operator: VERSION v[commit_audit/time_committed/value > $t] returns every version committed after $t, where it returned the trunk version current at $t whatever the operator (QUERY 1.1.0 master03 §Standard predicate). A number, boolean or NULL literal as the bound, a string bound no ISO 8601 form reads, and a time_committed path other than the whole value or /value are refused with 400 (#5062).

  • AQL refuses a number, boolean or null parameter or literal compared with a date/time path, in WHERE and in a VERSION predicate, with the same 400 a non-ISO 8601 string gets; such a bound used to become NULL and match nothing (#5064).

  • The served OpenAPI document now lists, on both template example operations, the 400 answered for a party template that constrains no PARTY_IDENTITY (#5066).

  • The compose quickstart, the hosted sandbox and the Helm chart run FerroPIX 0.0.18 (ghcr.io/ferrohealth/ferropix:0.0.18@sha256:6fb622b5b9ade34c8a4053112c8f166ff495d8b32bf99f35529d01e512b7cc42), with the FerroPIX chart 0.3.10 built for it.
