The changelog-guard job refuses a malformed fragment and a pull request that writes under [Unreleased], so two open pull requests no longer conflict on the changelog.

  • The chart pins the FerroPIX release beside its digest. ferropix.image.tag (0.0.7) states the release whose image ferropix.image.digest pins, and scripts/checks/chart-appversion.sh now holds the tag in the chart’s Artifact Hub images entry to it, as it holds the digest. The dependency chart still deploys the digest, so the rendered manifests do not change (#4131).

  • Breaking: the viewer listens on server.listen, not LEPTOS_SITE_ADDR. The viewer reads the family’s [server] table from ferrohealth-server 0.3.5, defaulting to 127.0.0.1:3000 (the image sets 0.0.0.0:3000 through FERROEHR_VIEWER__SERVER__LISTEN). A LEPTOS_SITE_ADDR that names another address refuses the start and names the key that replaced it; unset it. server.base_path and server.caller_rate are refused, since the viewer’s pages are served at / and it mounts no per-caller limit (#4139).

  • Breaking: ferroehr-viewer healthcheck asks /health/readiness over the loopback (over TLS when server.tls is set) and exits 0 only on 200, where it asked /login at LEPTOS_SITE_ADDR and took any 2xx or 3xx. A draining viewer is now unhealthy. The Helm chart’s viewer probes ask /health/liveness and /health/readiness, where all three asked / (#4139).

  • Breaking: the viewer’s browser security headers are the family console’s. Referrer-Policy is no-referrer (was strict-origin-when-cross-origin), Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin is new, and the content-hashed bundle under /pkg/ is Cache-Control: no-cache, revalidated on each load, where it was public, max-age=31536000, immutable. Every document stays no-store under the nonce Content-Security-Policy (#4139).

  • Breaking: every request to the viewer that is not a safe method passes the family same-origin check, server function calls and the result export included, where only page form posts compared Origin with Host. The browser’s Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin passes; without it Origin or Referer must name auth.oidc.public_base_url, and a request that shows neither is refused 403. A post without a session now returns to the page it was posted to after the sign-in, rather than to the page its Referer named (#4139).

  • Breaking: the viewer’s CDR and OIDC clients speak TLS 1.3 at least by default, as every family client does; cdr.tls.min_version and auth.oidc.tls.min_version set to "1.2" lower it. A request now runs under the stack’s server.request_timeout_ms (60 s) and server.body_limit_bytes (16 MiB), and a form post’s ceiling is that limit (#4139).

  • The viewer hydrates the whole page on FerroUI 0.5: the server draws the first page and the browser draws every page after it, so a link or a filter no longer reloads the document, and the browser’s back and forward walk the pages it drew. The pages load their code in six groups as they are first opened. Every page still works with no WebAssembly, and a post still answers with the page it was posted to (#4147).

  • The book and the architecture no longer claim the openEHR Service Model as the design of the service layer (#4211). The service layer is FerroEHR’s own design, judged by what goes in and comes out (BASE, RM, AM, TERM, QUERY/AQL, ITS-REST, ITS-JSON, ITS-XML and the serialisation formats); the vendored SM text stays as reference only. No behaviour changes.

  • Breaking: the viewer logs through the family’s [telemetry] section of ferrohealth-telemetry 0.2.2, as the CDR does (#4214). The console writes to stdout where it wrote to stderr, and telemetry.format defaults to auto, which renders json when stdout is not a terminal, so a container’s log is now JSON lines; set FERROEHR_VIEWER__TELEMETRY__FORMAT=pretty for the old human lines. RUST_LOG is now the lower-priority fallback of telemetry.filter (FERROEHR_VIEWER__TELEMETRY__FILTER wins over it), the filter defaults to info,hyper=warn,tower=warn,h2=warn where it was info, and a filter that does not parse refuses the start where it fell back to info. Each request writes the CDR’s request line (method, matched route, status, latency, request id), and a panic writes the CDR’s one fixed line without the panic message. [telemetry.otlp] exports the viewer’s spans and its http.server.request.duration metric as service.name ferroehr-viewer. Helm chart 19.2.0 sets the viewer’s format and filter from viewer.telemetry, and the Compose viewer services set FERROEHR_VIEWER__TELEMETRY__FORMAT.

  • The viewer takes FerroUI 0.5.4: its skip link keeps the browser’s own fragment navigation under hydration, so the viewer no longer patches the link after the page hydrates, and a code editor’s key costs the edit, not the length of the text (#4227).

  • The quickstart Keycloak overlay names its development CA through [auth] ca_file: docker-compose.keycloak.yml sets FERROEHR__AUTH__CA_FILE in place of SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR, which only the Linux platform verifier reads (#4236).

  • The development and quickstart Keycloak moves to 26.8.1, and its realms form a complete OIDC example: both compose files pin quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.8.1 by digest, held together by scripts/checks/compose-image-tags.sh and watched weekly by the base-image watcher. In both realms the authorization-code flow requires PKCE (S256) and accepts only the viewer origins on port 3000 as redirect targets (the quickstart realm accepted any), and a service account holding USER lets a client-credentials token reach the clinical API (#4240).

  • The hosted sandbox (sandbox.ferroehr.eu) resolves patients through FerroPIX 0.0.10, the FerroHEALTH patient identity source, as the compose quickstart does: FerroPIX runs beside the CDR on loopback with its database on the database box, each EHR_STATUS names its patient by the pseudonym FerroPIX minted in the clinical domain urn:oid:2.999.7.1, and POST /query/cohort takes subjects in the synthetic hospital domain urn:oid:2.999.1.1. The nightly reseed registers the demo patients with FerroPIX through the deploy script’s new identities verb before it seeds, so after a reset the CDR’s EHRs and FerroPIX’s identities agree. FerroTERM moves from 0.1.6 to 0.3.1 on the same index layout, the viewer’s memory limit from 1536m to 1024m, and deploy/hosted/sandbox-ferropix-rollout.sh carries the operator steps on both boxes (#4242).

  • Breaking: the quickstart Keycloak realm gives the viewer and a backend service their own clients: ferroehr-viewer (ferroehr-viewer-quickstart-secret) takes the authorization-code flow with PKCE and the password grant, and ferroehr-service (ferroehr-service-quickstart-secret) takes only the client-credentials grant, with the system/ SMART on openEHR scopes and a client_id claim. Both put ferroehr in aud. The single ferroehr client and its ferroehr-quickstart-secret are gone, so a script that fetched a token with them moves to ferroehr-viewer. The overlay names ferroehr-service in [smart] backend_clients, so its system/aql-* grant runs AQL. The dev realm makes the same split and drops the unused Keycloak Authorization Services, and scripts/ui-e2e.sh keeps its scratch files under target/ui-e2e/ (#4245).

  • The Helm chart’s usageReport.enabled reaches the other products it runs: FerroTERM (FERROTERM__USAGE_REPORT__ENABLED) and a FerroBRIDGE release from 0.0.7 on ([usage_report]) follow it, each overridable with terminology.usageReport.enabled or bridge.usageReport.enabled. The FerroPIX dependency chart reads only ferropix.usageReport.enabled, so the chart now refuses to render usageReport.enabled=false while that stays true: a release you switched off sent FerroPIX’s report regardless. Upgrading a release that sets usageReport.enabled=false with FerroPIX on takes --set ferropix.usageReport.enabled=false as well. Chart 20.0.0 (#4270).

Removed

  • FerroEHR holds no identity logic (#3380): link_as_subject, the server-side subject pseudonym (mint_subject_pseudonym), the party merge and split, and resolve_ehr_for_identity, the national-identifier-to-EHR crossing, are gone. Matching, cross-referencing identifier domains and minting pseudonyms belong to the identity source.

  • Breaking: ferroehr config default is gone with no alias; the annotated template is app/ferroehr/assets/ferroehr.default.toml in the repository. ferroehr healthcheck --url and FERROEHR_HEALTHCHECK_URL are gone too: the probe follows server.listen and server.base_path. Upgrade: copy the template from the repository, and probe another URL with an HTTP client of your own (#4087).

  • Breaking: [usage_report] slow_aql_ms is removed (#4087), with the AQL series it set the threshold of. A file or variable that still sets it refuses the start; remove the key. state_dir, the shared section’s directory for the instance id, is refused: FerroEHR keeps the instance id and the counts in the clinical database. The endpoint is now refused when the configuration is read, with the same rule (https, or http to a loopback host, never with credentials).

  • Breaking: Template Data Document (TDD) import is removed (#4199). POST /message/tdd/{ehr_id} and POST /message/tdd/{ehr_id}/batch are gone and answer 404, with the service behind them, the message-tdd extension and the Tds capability in the conformance statement. TDD and the Template Data Schema (TDS) come from the template tooling of the ADL 1.4 era and are no current openEHR format; send the composition as canonical JSON or XML, or as FLAT or STRUCTURED against its Web Template. The /message group keeps the four EHR Extract routes, and server.body_limit_bytes now covers template upload and /message/import alone.

  • Breaking: openehr-sdt drops the flat::tdd module (#4199): from_tdd, from_tdd_with and TDD_TEMPLATE_NS are removed, with the FlatError::TddXml, FlatError::TddAttribute and FlatError::TddElement variants and the crate’s quick-xml dependency. The openEHR crates move to 0.0.109 together.

  • Breaking: openehr-sdt 0.0.111 no longer carries smart_scopes. The SMART on openEHR scope grammar moved, with its API and tests, to ferrohealth-smart 0.8.5 as ferrohealth_smart::openehr::smart_scopes, so a consumer of openehr_sdt::smart_scopes names that path. FerroEHR pins ferrohealth-smart 0.8.5, its scope gate and the viewer’s scope previewer (both halves) parse with it, and the build resolves one openehr-sdt. Token checking and the scopes a token grants behave as before (#4206).

Fixed

  • A Cedar policy’s principal.patient is the caller’s patient claim ([authz.abac] patient_claim) (#4038). It was the patient of the object in play, so a rule such as principal.patient == resource.patient in the shipped consent.cedar held for every object a query touched.

  • The agent guard refuses wrapped and re-ordered spellings of a force push or a recursive delete (#4046). .claude/hooks/block_dangerous.sh let through git -C . push --force … main, /usr/bin/git push, \rm -rf, rm --recursive --force, bash -c "rm -rf …", find … -delete and similar. It now normalises the command first (a path or backslash before the binary, a launcher such as env or sudo, a sh -c or eval wrapper, git’s global options before the verb), judges every rm target and every deleting find starting point against /tmp, and refuses a push that deletes main or master. block_dangerous_test.sh runs each spelling.

  • An archetype HRID’s version status reads as the VERSION_STATUS it names (#4051), on the 0.0.102 crate line. AOM2 ARCHETYPE_HRID.version_status maps -rc, -alpha, -beta and no modifier to release_candidate, alpha, beta and released, where rc and the empty modifier read as VersionStatus::Other. openehr-adl writes the HRID back with the modifier (-rc, never -release_candidate), so parse and write are inverse.

  • A party reference whose type is not the builder’s default survives a FLAT or STRUCTURED round trip (#4052). master05 gives PARTY_REF.type no row, so a _health_care_facility that is not an ORGANISATION, or a _provider, performer, composer, feeder-audit party or PARTY_PROXY datum that is not a PERSON, is now written as |raw (master04 §Raw canonical JSON) and read back whole; it came back with the default type.

  • An ADL 2 Web Template reads the ADL 1.4 term constraints of an archetype read in the ADL 1.4 dialect (#4056). openehr-adl keeps such a constraint verbatim (openehr::433, local::at0003,at0004;at0003) for its 1.4 to 2 converter, and an at-coded ADL 2 template over unconverted archetypes carried it into the ADL 2 builder, which took the whole string for one local code. The builder now reads it as the OPT 1.4 builder reads a C_CODE_PHRASE: an openehr code carries its terminology and rubric, local codes their archetype rubrics, and the assumed code becomes the default. The nine openehr-* crates move to 0.0.100.

  • An ordinal of an archetype read in the ADL 1.4 dialect lists its at-codes (#4059). The symbol of each [value, symbol] row kept the verbatim local::at0006 spelling, which the ADL 2 builder took for the code and its label; it now reads the at-code with its archetype rubric, as #4056 does for coded text. The nine openehr-* crates move to 0.0.101.

  • A BASE 1.3 TERMINOLOGY_CODE keeps its terminology_id in XML (#4076). ITS-XML 1.0.2 types TRANSLATION_DETAILS.language and the other slots that hold one as CODE_PHRASE, whose terminology_id carries a <value> child; the codec wrote and read bare text instead, so an XSD-valid document read with an empty terminology_id. It now writes and reads the TERMINOLOGY_ID shape.

  • A configuration load or check that fails keeps its cause (#4104). Fifteen sites in the server’s commands turned the failure into a string, so the error chain ended at the message; they now carry the source error.

  • Cohort queries work under the IHE patient identity source. That provider keeps no party-to-EHR map, so a cohort selected by a demographic predicate found no EHR. POST /query/cohort now takes subjects, identifiers in any domain, each resolved through the [ehr_index] provider: under the IHE provider by a PIXm (ITI-83) translation forward into the server’s clinical domain, never back. The new [cohort] subjects = true turns the surface on without a predicate. Under the IHE provider a predicate is refused 400, and a failing identity source fails the query instead of shrinking the cohort. The cohort digest takes each subject by namespace only (#4114).

  • The chart guard holds the FerroPIX Artifact Hub image to its pinned digest (#4115). scripts/checks/chart-appversion.sh checked the FerroTERM and FerroBRIDGE artifacthub.io/images entries against their pins, but not the FerroPIX entry the ferropix dependency added, so its digest could drift from ferropix.image.digest in values.yaml and Artifact Hub would scan an image the chart does not run. The guard now compares the two, and --self-test moves the digest on either side.

  • ui-screenshot-guard judges only the pull request’s own commits (#4117). It diffed the base and head commits directly, so a branch behind main failed on main’s viewer changes and passed on main’s screenshot refresh. scripts/checks/ui-screenshot.sh now reads the paths from the merge base (base...head), and its --self-test runs both cases on a branch behind main before every verdict.

  • The usage report groups a request by the route below the openEHR API mount (server.base_path followed by rest.base_path). A REST root that contains an API family word, such as /ferroehr/ehr/v1, no longer places a query or definition route under ehr, and a route outside the mount counts in no group, as before #4128 (#4132).

  • The local EHR index holds an EHR created for a subject. Under [ehr_index] provider = "local", create_ehr_for_subject now enters the subject in the local map with the EHR’s creation, as a Primary association with no location, so subject_ehrs and a subject cohort find the EHR. Before, only EHR_STATUS named the subject and the map stayed empty until add_ehr_subject ran (#4138).

  • [smart] issuer_metadata_file is read by the same parse as metadata fetched from an issuer (#4165), so a file that repeats a member name is a boot error. It used to be read as it stood, keeping whichever value the parser took.

  • The viewer draws the CDR’s refusal where it used to draw nothing: on an EHR’s Status tab when the version’s envelope read is refused, in place of the contribution, signed and lifecycle facts, and in Edit the directory’s reference picker when the composition list is refused, in place of an empty select (#4170).

  • The access record of every route that addresses one EHR names that EHR, read from the matched route’s {ehr_id} parameter: GET /message/export/{ehr_id} and POST /message/import/{ehr_id} recorded none, so a patient’s ITI-81 search missed them, and DELETE /admin/ehr/all no longer names an EHR all. The Extract record of an export or import names the requesting user where it named UNKNOWN, and a read of GET /admin/restriction is recorded against its EHR (GDPR Art. 15(1)(c), EHDS Art. 9(2)) (#4192).

  • The compose-built viewer image builds its WebAssembly bindings again: its wasm-bindgen CLI now follows the wasm-bindgen version Cargo.lock resolves instead of a separate pin that had fallen behind it. A CI guard holds every other wasm-bindgen and cargo-leptos pin to the lock and to one another, and CI builds the viewer image from source whenever its Dockerfile changes (#4222).

  • The viewer takes FerroUI 0.5.3: the top bar’s search no longer panics when a navigation leaves the page while its answer panel is being placed, and a search that finds the session over now sends every other open viewer tab to sign-in too (#4224).

  • A composition commits when an element’s value matches any one of the alternatives its template allows (#4226), on the 0.0.110 crate line. ADL 1.4 §“Single-valued Attributes” makes the object constraints under a single-valued attribute alternatives, only one of which the data needs to match. The free text of an open coded value-set (FLAT or STRUCTURED |other, a canonical DV_TEXT) was refused as expected RM type conforming to DV_CODED_TEXT but found DV_TEXT where the template allows DV_TEXT beside DV_CODED_TEXT, and a value that matched only a later alternative of the same type, such as a second DV_QUANTITY with other units, was checked against the first alone. When no alternative matches, the refusal names every alternative with what each one found, and FLAT writes a value under one of several same-type alternatives, not under each.

  • POST /query/cohort and an AQL query rooted at a demographic class now leave out every EHR the population gate leaves out: an EHR whose current EHR_STATUS.is_queryable is false and an EHR under a research objection no longer answer rows in a cohort or a demographic join, as they already did not in an ad-hoc population query (RM EHR_STATUS.is_queryable: “True if this EHR should be included in population queries”). The research objection leak was a privacy defect. A query scoped to one EHR by ehr_id and an EXTRACT’s criteria still answer the EHR they name (#4247).

  • The hosted sandbox’s database box runs a pinned image (#4252). deploy/hosted/cloud-init-postgres.yaml defaults FERROEHR_POSTGRES_IMAGE to ghcr.io/ferrohealth/ferroehr-postgres:5.4.2 by its index digest, where the box ran the moving latest tag of the image’s pre-FerroHEALTH namespace, and compose-image-tags.sh holds the default and the hosted README to one release reference. Step 6 of sandbox-ferropix-rollout.sh moves the box onto the pin: it refuses a change of PostgreSQL major, recreates the container on its data volume and checks the CDR’s readiness and a ferropix login afterwards. Step 1 of the script no longer prints an empty line for each container that is absent.

Security

Shipped with functional changes because: the patched ferrohealth-smart arrives in the same dependency move as the family mask and the lockstep releases built on it. The zstd move is a lock-only update that a security-only 5.4.3 could have carried; the maintainer chose to ship it in 5.5.0, released the day after the fix landed, instead of cutting a separate patch.

  • ferrohealth-smart 0.7.1 masks the userinfo of every URL in its grant tables, a URL no parser accepts included. With 0.7.0 a configured token_endpoint or issuer that did not parse could reach the configuration renderings and the log in full (CWE-532, GHSA-vphj-3f8c-5hpx) (#4050).

  • The zstd bindings move to zstd 0.14.3, zstd-safe 8.2.0 and zstd-sys 2.1.2, past RUSTSEC-2026-0391, RUSTSEC-2026-0398, RUSTSEC-2026-0403 and RUSTSEC-2026-0410. Response compression and the outbound clients’ response decompression reach these crates, and the affected functions were not shown unreachable (GHSA-cwhv-87pq-3c3c) (#4095).

5.4.2 - 2026-10-25

5.4.2 is a patch release with no breaking change: a deployment upgrades in place. Helm chart 14.0.1 carries appVersion 5.4.2 and changes nothing else.

Changed

  • The viewer’s search answers under the field as you type (#4024), on FerroUI 0.4.0. From the second character the panel under the top bar’s search shows the EHRs, compositions, parties, templates and stored queries that match, five of a kind, from the server function /api/find_answer, which posts the words so they stay out of the address and the log. Arrow keys move through the hits, Enter opens one, Escape closes the panel. The find page lists every hit in the page.

  • The CDR takes up ferrohealth-smart 0.5.0 (#4002), and the build holds one copy of openehr-sdt where it held two (0.0.90 for the SMART crate beside the workspace’s 0.0.98). Reading a trusted issuer’s authorization-server metadata at boot, the server now refuses a document that repeats a member name (RFC 8259 §4), naming the location that answered it.

  • SECURITY.md states the family’s response times, with fix-time targets by severity. An acknowledgement within about 5 business days and an initial assessment within about 10, both best effort as before, and now a fixed release published within 7 days of the confirmed assessment for a Critical vulnerability, 30 days for High, 90 days for Medium and with the next release for Low. The CRA risk assessment says business days where it said working days.

Fixed

  • The audit drain sends a held syslog connection’s records without a millisecond wait per record (#3954). FerroEHR moves to ihe-atna and ehds-logging 0.2.7 (FerroAUDIT). The liveness probe the syslog sink runs before each record waited for a timer tick of about a millisecond, which held one connection to roughly 880 records per second. It now answers at once, about 47 000 records per second in FerroAUDIT’s measurement.

  • A revoked Direct Key signature no longer lets the primary key sign (#3972). The PGP signer now applies a valid Certification Revocation of a Direct Key signature, created at or after it: the revoked signature is cancelled (RFC 9580 §5.2.3.10), so neither its signing flag nor its key expiration counts any more, and a version 6 primary key left with no Direct Key signature in force is not used.

  • The viewer’s Paths tab offers Build a query only on a COMPOSITION template (#4001). A node of a demographic template (a PERSON, ORGANISATION, GROUP, AGENT or ROLE root) no longer links to the query builder, whose one query shape, FROM EHR e CONTAINS COMPOSITION c, can never match a party. The viewer moves to FerroUI 0.3.7, which makes the node’s query link optional and keeps a long URL or word in a banner, a notice or a setting row inside the screen at 320 px.

  • An access record says when the patient lookup failed (#3900). When the audit drain cannot read the subject behind an EHR (the database refused or did not answer), the EHDS access record now writes the patient lookup as unavailable instead of not-found, so a reviewer can tell a record that names no patient because the lookup failed from one whose EHR has no subject (Regulation (EU) 2025/327 Art 9(1)). A failed lookup is asked again for the next record instead of being remembered.

Security

Shipped with functional changes because: no shipped artefact is affected (zip 8.6.0 ran only in a build script, as the withdrawn VEX statements recorded), so there is no security update to separate from the other changes this release carries.

  • zip 8.6.0 leaves the build (#3799; GHSA-vv5m-jxxh-4627, GHSA-4v9h-p7m9-rh26, GHSA-4684-h2q9-2vcp). utoipa-swagger-ui 10.0.2 unpacks its vendored Swagger UI archive with zip 9, so the yanked zip 8.6.0 and its three extraction advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0367, RUSTSEC-2026-0368, RUSTSEC-2026-0369) no longer reach the dependency graph, and deny.toml and security/vex/rust-advisories.openvex.json drop their exceptions for them.

5.4.1 - 2026-10-24

5.4.1 carries breaking changes for operators who use a terminology server, each with its upgrade step under Changed. Before you upgrade: move [terminology.external] to the one [terminology.server] (its url, fail_on_error, request_timeout_ms and optional oauth grant) and rename FERROEHR__TERMINOLOGY__EXTERNAL__ variables to FERROEHR__TERMINOLOGY__SERVER__; on Helm, chart 14.0.0 takes config.terminology.server and secrets.terminologyClientSecret. A deployment without an external terminology server upgrades unchanged.

Changed

  • The CDR reaches its terminology server through ferrobridge-term (#3085), FerroBRIDGE’s published FHIR terminology client, in place of its own HTTP client and the third-party fhir-model decoding, which leaves the build. The configuration is unchanged. On the wire, $lookup, $validate-code, $expand and $subsumes are now a POST of a FHIR R4B Parameters body instead of a GET with the inputs in the query string, so a code no longer travels in a URL; the CodeSystem?url=&_summary=count probe stays a GET. The SM at_date is sent as the date input of $lookup and $validate-code. Each call is made once, so request_timeout_ms still bounds it. The answers are read strictly against the R4B operation definitions: a $lookup answer without its name or display, an $expand answer without an expansion, or a $subsumes outcome outside its four codes is now an upstream fault (500, or the unresolvable branch of fail_on_error at commit) where the CDR used to fall back to the code as the term text, an empty value set, or “not subsumed”. A server that answers by the operation definitions sees no difference. The fhir feature of the internal ferroehr-ext crate is gone with the decoder it gated; the fhir features of ferroehr, ferroehr-rest and ferroehr-server keep their meaning.

  • The conformance statement declares unmatched-member-refused (#3988, register AMB-229). The server refuses a container member whose RM type the template does not allow, such as a CLUSTER committed where items[at0004] is constrained to ELEMENT (422, AM AOM 1.4 C_OBJECT.rm_type_name, ADL 1.4 cADL §Occurrences). The statement claimed the lenient unmatched-member-accepted arm, so the served and declared postures disagreed. The posture is the strict one by owner rule: FerroEHR holds to the specification and makes no allowance for other implementations’ mistakes. Catalogue case CONT-ITEM-unmatched_member_refused now applies and CONT-ITEM-unmatched_member_accepted is not applicable. A client that commits a mismatched member gets the same 422 as before.

  • Breaking: the CDR asks one terminology server, configured under [terminology.server] (#3085). All terminology beyond the openEHR support terminology is FerroTERM’s job: the CDR keeps the in-process openEHR terminology the RM validates against and one client to one FHIR R4B terminology server (BASE architecture_overview/master12-terminology.adoc §Binding Terminology Value-sets to Archetypes puts the resolver of a constraint binding in that server). [terminology.server] carries enabled, url, fail_on_error and request_timeout_ms, and the optional [terminology.server.oauth] grant takes the keys [audit.fhir_feed.oauth] already uses. Every key is a scalar, so the whole section is reachable through FERROEHR__TERMINOLOGY__SERVER__*. The fail-open default and the 422 for a resolved non-member are unchanged (register AMB-172). A configuration that still names [terminology.external] is refused at boot, naming the key. Upgrade: move [terminology.external] enabled and fail_on_error to [terminology.server]; put the one server’s base URL in [terminology.server] url (the URL of the provider you used as default, for FerroTERM http://ferroterm:8080/r4b) and its request_timeout_ms beside it; move an [terminology.external.oauth2_clients.<name>] table to [terminology.server.oauth], where scopes = [...] becomes one space-separated scope = "..." string, auth_method becomes client_auth, and refresh_leeway_secs goes; rename every FERROEHR__TERMINOLOGY__EXTERNAL__ environment variable to FERROEHR__TERMINOLOGY__SERVER__. A deployment that spread code systems over several servers loads them into FerroTERM, which serves SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD and any FHIR CodeSystem or ValueSet from one index.

  • Breaking: Helm chart 14.0.0 wires the terminology server through config.terminology.server and takes its client secret as secrets.terminologyClientSecret (#3085). terminology.enabled with terminology.wireCdr injects enabled, url and fail_on_error under config.terminology.server, and refuses a values file that sets the URL itself. secrets.terminologyClientSecret is one string, mounted at /etc/ferroehr-secrets/terminology.server.oauth.client_secret, and needs the grant declared under config.terminology.server.oauth. Upgrade: move config.terminology.external to config.terminology.server as above, and secrets.terminologyOauth2ClientSecrets.<name> to secrets.terminologyClientSecret.

  • A token endpoint URL is masked in every rendering of an outbound grant (#3085). token_url under [audit.fhir_feed.oauth], [authz.abac.remote.oauth] and [terminology.server.oauth] now keeps its host and path and masks its userinfo in ferroehr config check, /management/env, GET /admin/config and ferroehr report, as the terminology client’s own token URL already did.

  • The conformance lane and the real-release terminology probe run FerroTERM (#3085, #2236). The terminology profile of docker/sut-ferroehr.yml composes FerroTERM 0.1.6, pinned by digest, with the shaped seed of docker/terminology/seed/ mounted read-only as its code-system directory, in place of HAPI FHIR and the PUT seeder docker/terminology/seed.sh, which is gone. The opt-in PROBE_ONLY=terminology family of scripts/deploy-probe.sh builds a local SNOMED CT release into an index with the quickstart overlay’s own ferroterm-build and drives FerroTERM over it, in place of Snowstorm and Elasticsearch.

  • The conformance run composes a fourth deployment for the fail-open unresolvable-binding branch (#3985). docker/sut-terminology-failopen.yml runs the same image as its own compose project on ports 8083 and 5434, with [terminology.server] fail_on_error = false and a server URL nothing answers on, and the ixit declares it as the sut_fail_open instance. The stable-profile deployment now uses the primary’s FerroTERM, which the ixit already declared for it.

Removed

  • The terminology route map, per-server credentials and caches are gone (#3085); FerroTERM is where the capability lives. Removed keys: [terminology.external.providers.<name>] with type, operation, connect_timeout_ms, cache_ttl_secs, cache_capacity, oauth2_client, client_cert_path, client_key_path and ca_bundle_path; [terminology.external.routes]; [terminology.external.oauth2_clients]. The CDR no longer selects a server per terminology, no longer presents a per-server mutual-TLS client certificate or pins a per-server trust bundle (the server is verified against the platform’s trust store), no longer caches terminology answers, and no longer validates membership through $expand ($validate-code answers it). AQL TERMINOLOGY(), the /terminology/* routes, commit-time binding resolution and the ADL 2 VETDF check all ask the one server.

Fixed

  • A method a resource does not serve is 405 with Allow under SMART (#3987). With bearer authentication on, DELETE /ehr and every other method a route does not serve was refused 403 by the SMART on openEHR scope check before the router could answer. The gate now answers 405 with the Allow field naming the served methods once the caller has authenticated, whatever the token grants, and runs the RBAC and scope checks only on a served method (ITS-REST overview/Requests_and_responses §HTTP Methods, RFC 9110 §15.5.6). A request without a credential is still 401.

  • A ROLE operational template whose single attributes state 0..* uploads (#3994). POST /definition/template/adl1.4 refused deployed ROLE templates (Role.v2, root openEHR-DEMOGRAPHIC-ROLE.Role.v1) with 422 Members_valid, because they constrain ROLE.capabilities and CAPABILITY.credentials without a cardinality while the children state occurrences 0..*. ADL 1.4 master05-cadl.adoc §Occurrences calls that “not illegal” and reads it as at most one value, so the CDR now accepts the template and applies that cap: the Web Template gives such a node max 1, and the ADL2 conversion states the cap and records it in conversion_details, next to the template’s undefined ac0001 reference. A ROLE party built against the template, and a PERSON that holds it through PERSON.relationships, commit and read back as before. The disagreement with the stricter AOM 1.4 Members_valid invariant is reported upstream (#3996).

  • The template example of a demographic template is a party (#3995). GET /definition/template/adl1.4/{template_id}/example (and the ADL 2 twin) answered 400 the template root PERSON is not a COMPOSITION for every PERSON, ORGANISATION, GROUP, AGENT or ROLE template. It now answers an example party of the root class at every detail_level, in canonical JSON or XML, with a uid for type=output; an example ROLE carries a placeholder performer, which the RM makes mandatory. FLAT and STRUCTURED stay 406 for a party example, since the Simplified Formats map no party class. The viewer’s Example tab offers JSON and XML only for a demographic template, and for a template rooted at an ENTRY or a SECTION it says that no example exists instead of showing the CDR’s refusal.

5.4.0 - 2026-10-24

5.4.0 carries breaking changes for operators, each with its upgrade step under Changed. Before you upgrade: replace an ECDSA or Ed448 OpenPGP signing key in [signing] mode = "pgp" with an Ed25519 key, and check that the certificate’s primary key or a subkey may still sign; tell viewer users that the viewer’s addresses change, so bookmarks and links into it need updating, and that the theme falls back to the system’s until it is chosen again; and serve the viewer’s whole pkg/ directory if you serve its site from your own web server. No configuration key, database migration or image name changes.

Changed

  • Breaking: an ECDSA or Ed448 OpenPGP signing key is refused at boot (#3965). In [signing] mode = "pgp" the server no longer starts when the key’s signing component is ECDSA (P-256, P-384, P-521, secp256k1, Brainpool) or Ed448, and the error names RUSTSEC-2026-0387; see Security below. P-384, P-521 and Ed448 keys already failed the boot signature, because the server signs with SHA-256 and RFC 9580 requires a longer digest for them, so the keys that change behaviour are P-256 and secp256k1. Ed25519 and RSA keys load as before, and the RSA boot warning now recommends Ed25519 alone. Such a certificate keeps verifying the versions it signed when it is listed in signing.retired_key_paths. Upgrade: before upgrading a deployment that signs with such a key, generate an Ed25519 signing key (gpg --quick-generate-key "…" ed25519 sign), export its armored secret key to signing.key_path, and add the old certificate’s public half to signing.retired_key_paths (the book’s PGP signing page and the signing section of the configuration reference). The digest mode, the default, is unaffected.
  • The viewer is rebuilt on FerroUI 0.3.6 (#3932, #3942, #3946, #3957, FerroHEALTH/FerroUI#161). Every screen follows the FerroEHR mockups of FerroUI’s design/consoles/ferroehr/ at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark, with FerroUI’s components and none of the viewer’s own copies. The viewer now runs in islands mode: the server draws every page whole, every link is a link and every action a form that posts to its page, so the whole viewer works with JavaScript off, and the browser hydrates only the parts that add behaviour (the code editor, path trees, the chart legend, date pickers, the user menu’s keyboard pattern, the subject reveal and Copy). Editors end in a docked decision bar; a refused save keeps what you typed beside the CDR’s words. The navigation is Dashboard, EHRs, Parties, Templates, Terminology, Stored queries, Query, Server, Audit log, Subscriptions, Configuration and About, with search in the top bar. The activity charts of the dashboard and of an EHR’s contributions label their first day and every tenth day back from today, and a staged change’s Apply sits beside its What changes select.
  • Breaking: the viewer’s addresses change. /demographics/… is /parties (/parties/{kind}/{uid}, /parties/relationships/{uid}, /parties/contributions/{uid}); an EHR’s tabs are paths (/ehrs/{id}/status, /directory, /contributions, /tags) instead of ?tab=; /queries/builder and /queries/aql are /query and /query/aql; /queries/stored?load=… is /queries/{name}/{version}/run; /system and /operations are /server with its tabs, the conformance manifest moves to /about, the runtime configuration to /configuration; an ADL 2 release is /templates/adl2/{stem}/{release}. Upgrade: update bookmarks and links into the viewer; an old address answers 404.
  • Breaking: display preferences are cookies of their own. The theme is set in the user menu and on Your preferences (/preferences), and each preference is its own ferroehr-viewer-* cookie; the ferroehr-theme cookie and the /theme route are gone, so a theme chosen before the upgrade falls back to the system’s until it is chosen again.
  • Breaking: a listing that can show patient data keeps its page out of the address (FerroUI leptos-ui.md §0): the EHRs, an EHR’s compositions and contributions and the audit log page through a session cookie (/paging); ?offset= and ?page= on them are ignored. Filters stay in the address.
  • An open tab now idles out (#3057). The viewer polls nothing in the background, so session.idle_minutes measures the requests the browser makes, and a tab left untouched signs out like a closed one; the next page asked for is the sign-in page saying the session ended, and signing in returns to it. A revoked session is noticed on the next request.
  • The viewer’s site is built with cargo leptos build --split (scripts/cargo-leptos.sh adds it) and FerroUI’s split feature, so FerroUI’s lazy islands (the date pickers and the tree) load from chunks of their own on a page that draws them (FerroUI #331). A deployment that serves the site from its own web server serves the whole pkg/ directory, chunks included; the image already does.
  • The dashboard’s compositions per day count commits, read from each version’s commit_audit/time_committed, as its note says; it counted context start times before.
  • A query’s results are FerroUI’s results pane (#3942). Table and Chart sit in the Results heading and run the query again in the view chosen, which the next Run keeps; the separate Show as choice is gone. Export in the heading opens a menu of CSV and JSON (#3946), whose items post to /export/aql/csv and /export/aql/json, and /export/aql with a format field no longer answers.

Added

  • Your preferences: the theme, density, reduced motion, the language, the first day of the week, how long a revealed subject id stays shown, and the keyboard shortcut hints, each kept in its own cookie.
  • Older versions on an EHR’s directory reads further back than the newest ten versions, and a version reached that way restores.
  • The viewer’s journeys run at a phone’s 390 px in CI beside 1440 px, and the screenshot pass captures every route in both widths and both themes as the ui-route-shots artifact (#3910). Keyboard journeys cover where the focus lands after a route change, the query builder by keyboard, and the user menu’s keyboard pattern (#2793).
  • The parts the FerroEHR mockups draw and FerroUI 0.3.4 now carries (#3942): Your access in the user menu; Details on the sandbox band, leading to Server’s Overview; Copy the id (or the name) in the More menus of an EHR, a directory, a composition, a party, a relationship, a template and a stored query; Save to the CDR beside Run in Query’s header; relative times in FerroUI’s words; one editor per staged change of a new contribution, with no cap of twelve; the contribution glyph; Discard that leaves a form with an empty required field, so the relationship and subscription editors mark their required fields again; the time of each point in a chart’s figures table; Your access’s grants built from the CDR’s own reading of each scope; and the How configuration works dialog on Configuration.
  • The parts the FerroEHR mockups draw and FerroUI 0.3.5 now carries (#3946): Your access reads the OpenID Connect profile scope as the request for your profile, where it drew it refused although the CDR accepts it; a query’s exports are one Export menu; and Stored queries takes its scroll glyph in the navigation, on the dashboard and in the search’s answers. The activity charts of the dashboard and of an EHR’s contributions label their first and last day as the mockups do (22 Sep).
  • A template’s Download in its More menu (#3942): the stored ADL 1.4 operational template (.opt) or ADL2 template (.adlt) as a file, read with your session from /download/template/{family}/{id}.
  • New contribution follows its mockup more closely (#3942): the audit section is headed Contribution audit, the committer’s placeholder names who commits when it is left empty, and Terminology takes its book glyph.

Removed

  • The viewer’s Tailwind build and its own stylesheet. The viewer serves FerroUI’s stylesheet and its FerroEHR theme only; the image build no longer runs the Tailwind standalone binary.
  • The EHR status’s own tag panel. A tag on the EHR status is still listed on the EHR’s Tags tab and opens the Status tab; setting one is done over the API, as the mockup has no panel for it.
  • The stored-query listing’s pager: every stored query is listed, grouped by namespace.

Fixed

  • The OpenPGP signing subkey is the newest one that may sign (#3967). In [signing] mode = "pgp" the server took the first subkey in the file that any binding signature had ever flagged for signing, so a subkey added for rotation never signed, and a revoked or expired subkey kept signing. It now signs with the subkey created last among those whose newest valid binding grants signing, that have not expired, and that carry no valid revocation (RFC 9580 §5.2.1.12, §5.2.3.10, §5.2.3.13), and with the primary key when none qualifies. A certificate with one signing subkey signs as before. Upgrade: a deployment whose certificate holds several signing subkeys signs with a different one after the upgrade; every version signed before keeps verifying, since the certificate still carries the old subkey.
  • The OpenPGP primary key signs only when the certificate lets it (#3969). In [signing] mode = "pgp", when no subkey qualified to sign, the server signed with the primary key without checking it. It now signs with the primary key only when the primary key’s governing self-signature (the newest valid Direct Key signature when it carries key flags, else the newest valid self-signature on the primary User ID) carries the signing flag 0x02, neither that self-signature nor the key has expired, and no valid Key Revocation covers it (RFC 9580 §5.2.1.11, §5.2.3.10, §5.2.3.13, §5.2.3.29). A self-signature with no key flags grants no signing. When neither a subkey nor the primary key may sign, the server refuses to start and says what to change. Upgrade: a certificate whose primary key lacks the signing flag, or has expired or been revoked, and which has no usable signing subkey, no longer boots; add an Ed25519 signing subkey (gpg --quick-add-key <FINGERPRINT> ed25519 sign) and export the armored secret key to signing.key_path again. Every version signed before keeps verifying, since the certificate still carries the primary key. A certificate generated with signing on its primary key, or with a valid signing subkey, loads as before.
  • A signing subkey stops signing when its primary key is revoked or expires (#3971). In [signing] mode = "pgp" the server checked a signing subkey’s own binding, expiry and revocation but not the primary key’s, so the subkey of a certificate whose primary key carried a valid Key Revocation, or had passed its Key Expiration Time, kept signing. Now no subkey signs while the primary key is revoked or expired (RFC 9580 §5.2.1.11, §5.2.3.13), and with nothing left that may sign the server refuses to start. Upgrade: a deployment whose certificate’s primary key is revoked or expired no longer boots; generate a new Ed25519 certificate (gpg --quick-generate-key "…" ed25519 sign), export its armored secret key to signing.key_path, and list the old certificate’s public half in signing.retired_key_paths so the versions it signed keep verifying. To keep an expired certificate, extend its primary key’s expiry (gpg --quick-set-expire <FINGERPRINT> 1y) and export it again.
  • The audit drain no longer loses the records it sent last when it exits (#3959). It dropped its syslog connection without a TLS close_notify. With the repository’s session tickets still unread, the kernel answered with a reset, which could discard the last records, with no warning. The drain now closes the connection as RFC 5425 §4.4 asks, through FerroAUDIT 0.2.5’s Connection::close (ihe-atna and ehds-logging =0.2.5), and logs and counts a close that fails. The syslog connection also sends each record at once (TCP_NODELAY).

Security

Shipped with functional changes because: only the newest release is supported (SECURITY.md), so a security-only patch cut from 5.3.3 beside the next release would be out of support the moment that release lands and give no one a release to stay on; the fix is itself a behaviour change, refusing ECDSA and Ed448 signing keys, so there is no dependency bump to ship alone.

  • RUSTSEC-2026-0387 in crypto-bigint 0.5.5 (#3965, security/vex/rust-advisories.openvex.json). Its operations meant to be constant-time can branch on their operands, and the 0.5 line, which pgp and openidconnect still use, has no fixed release. With ECDSA and Ed448 signing keys refused, the server runs those operations only over public keys and signatures, in verification.

5.3.3 - 2026-10-23

Fixed

  • An element whose value the template leaves open keeps its FLAT path (#3933). The web template dropped an ELEMENT that carries no value constraint, or a value constrained to {*}, so the vcf_report template’s “Test method” was missing from the FLAT example and a FLAT write to …/laboratory_test_result:0/test_method/text_value was refused as an unknown simplified path. Such an element admits any data value (AOM 1.4 C_COMPLEX_OBJECT.any_allowed, ADL 1.4 “Any” constraints), so it now keeps its node with one alternative per concrete data value type, keyed by type as in the Simplified Formats CLUSTER example (…/test_method/text_value, …/test_method/quantity_value|magnitude); DV_STATE is not among them, since it has no simplified form (#3934). Web templates, FLAT and STRUCTURED examples and FLAT paths change for templates with such elements. The openehr-* crates move to 0.0.96.
  • A DV_STATE is no longer built as a coded text from FLAT or STRUCTURED (#3934). The converter read and wrote a DV_STATE with the DV_CODED_TEXT suffixes, so a write built a value the RM refuses (RM data_types §DV_STATE: value: DV_CODED_TEXT, is_terminal: Boolean) and a read emitted keys no table defines. The Simplified Formats RM mapping chapter has no DV_STATE table, so a write that decomposes a DV_STATE node is now refused with a 422 naming the node and the missing table; the node is written and read as |raw canonical JSON, and the FLAT and STRUCTURED examples leave it out. A canonical commit’s DV_STATE is now checked against the template’s code list on its value. The gap is reported upstream in #3936. The openehr-* crates move to 0.0.97.

Security

Shipped with functional changes because: only the newest release is supported (SECURITY.md), so a separate 5.3.2 patch published beside 5.3.3 would be out of support the moment 5.3.3 lands and give no one a release to stay on; the fix is a dependency bump with no behaviour change of its own.

  • ctutils 0.4.5 (RUSTSEC-2026-0385, GHSA-h46f-99p9-gwvf). Its Choice mask generation and its u128 comparisons could compile to branches on secret values; the crate sits under the aes-gcm, hmac and digest implementations the server uses.

5.3.2 - 2026-10-22

The v5.3.0 and v5.3.1 tags were pushed but neither release published: the v5.3.0 scan refused the container base’s ca-certificates (DSA-6572-1), and the v5.3.1 plan refused a CRA risk assessment with no revision for that base change. 5.3.2 is the same release on the rebuilt base, and no 5.3.0 or 5.3.1 artifacts exist.

Changed

  • The Rust toolchain moves to 1.99.1. The pinned channel, both container base images (digest re-resolved to the rust:1.99.1-slim-trixie index) and the CI job containers move together; the MSRV stays at 1.98, the toolchain minus one, the rule docs/VERSIONS.md now states for the whole FerroHEALTH family. Clippy 1.99’s new assert_is_empty lint is answered at every site with an assert_eq! or assert_ne! that prints the value on failure, two float_cmp expectations it no longer needs are removed, and the unit tests under the published crates’ src/ (and the codegen templates they are emitted from) change with it, so the openehr-* crates move to 0.0.94 with no API change.

  • The access log moves to FerroAUDIT 0.2.4 (ihe-atna and ehds-logging =0.2.4), and the record writes again what #3897 had to drop: the token’s jti at agent[user].policy, the ITS-REST operation id as a second subtype, outcomeDesc, source.type, and in the DICOM message the optional EventOutcomeDescription, AuditSourceTypeCode and ParticipantObjectDataLifeCycle. A Basic user is recorded with no issuer and no client instead of FerroEHR’s own URN and UNKNOWN, an acting mode the deployment did not establish adds no person role, the caller’s roles are written by the crate, an origin names its originating system with no invented endpoint or status, and FerroEHR’s own agent is addressed by its server_host. A record kept without end (retention_days = 0) says so and names no end date, a day-counted horizon is stated in days, and a horizon under three years, which only a deployment under no Union jurisdiction passes, names that horizon as the ground of its floor instead of claiming Art. 9(2). The category map takes every archetype id openEHR BASE 1.3.0 admits, a CKM draft’s .v0 and the namespaced ADL 2 form among them, and compares ids as openEHR BASE asks, so the evidence keeps each id as the access named it: a template id keeps its case (records written before keep the folded form), and a stored composition’s root archetype stays in the node table’s comparison form, and the map’s digest moves once with the upgrade: records keep the digest of the map that classified them (#3902).

  • The minimum supported Rust version is 1.98 (was 1.97), the version fhir-types, pulled by ihe-atna’s FHIR writer, declares. The nine openehr-* crates move to 0.0.93 with it.

  • ferrohealth-smart 0.4.0 (#3895), the version every FerroHEALTH product pins. The refusal statuses and challenges do not change.

  • The access log is written through the FerroHEALTH products’ shared audit crates (#3887). The EHDS access record, the Art. 14(1) categories and their classification, the Art. 9(2) retention floor and the Art. 11(5) emergency mark come from ehds-logging 0.1.1, and the BALP AuditEvent, the DICOM audit message, the syslog sender and the ATX: FHIR Feed client from ihe-atna 0.1.1 (FerroAUDIT). FerroEHR still decides which accesses are logged, what each record says and where it is stored.

  • [audit.categories] names categories by their HL7 Europe codes. A priority category is Patient-Summaries, Electronic-Prescriptions, Electronic-Dispensations, Medical-Imaging, Laboratory-Reports or Discharge-Reports, or <system>|<code>; a national category is declared in the new national list as <system>|<code>; a key of no category maps to the word "none" instead of ["none"]. The old spellings (patient-summary, test-results, national:<code> and the others) refuse boot. The Helm chart’s config.audit.categories takes the same values (chart 13.0.0).

  • A stored access record names each category by its <system>|<code> token, and category_basis says what the classification was read from: returned, written, queried or resource-kind (audit migration 0012). Records written before keep their spellings. Evidence ids are stored in the case-folded form the map is read in. A query whose constraints name an id the map does not hold, or bind no id to a content operand, is now recorded unclassified beside the categories that did map.

  • The retention register keys a period on the category token (clinical migration 0016). PUT {base}/admin/retention/policy takes a category as [audit.categories] names it and stores the token; periods keyed on a priority spelling move to its token, and a period keyed on a national:<code> spelling refuses the migration until it is declared again.

  • The FHIR AuditEvent follows the BALP 1.1.4 patterns ehds-logging and ihe-atna write. The person is the agent:user slice (the token’s issuer and subject, the professional’s identifier as ihe-otherId, the assurance level as ihe-assuranceLevel), the client application an agent of its own, the organisation a logical Organization reference; the categories, the retention, the security labels and the origins ride in ehds-categories and origin entities; the emergency mark is the ehds-emergency-access entity; a query’s subtype is search. The token’s jti agent, the ITS-REST operation-id subtype, the outcomeDesc and the audit source type are no longer written.

  • The DICOM audit message is written without a byte order mark, EventOutcomeDescription, AuditSourceTypeCode or ParticipantObjectDataLifeCycle (ITI TF-2 §3.20.4.1.2).

Removed

  • The UDP syslog transport ([audit.syslog] transport). The syslog feed sends RFC 5424 over RFC 5425 TLS only, on port 6514 by default, and a transport key refuses boot. The audit_syslog_udp deployment gap is gone with it.

Fixed

  • A + in a query-string parameter is read as a space (#3891). Every query parameter the REST API reads, q of GET /query/aql included, is decoded as application/x-www-form-urlencoded (WHATWG URL Standard §5.1): + and %20 are a space and %2B is a literal plus. A form-encoded AQL query that wrote its spaces as + was refused with a 400 before. A client that sends an unencoded + meaning a plus, such as a time-zone offset, encodes it as %2B, as RFC 6570 form expansion and form encoders already do.

  • An xsi:type the XML schemas do not define is refused with an error that names them (#3892). An OPT 1.4 upload whose constraint node carries a type outside the ITS-XML OPT 1.4 schemas (Template.xsd, OpenehrProfile.xsd, Archetype.xsd), such as T_ARCHETYPE_ROOT in place of C_ARCHETYPE_ROOT, answers 422 with a message saying that those schemas define no such subtype. The RM and AOM2 XML readers name their schemas the same way. The refusal itself is unchanged.

  • A Basic request the verified-credential cache admits writes no ATNA login record (#3895). Since the move to ferrohealth-smart 0.3.1 every Basic request was marked a fresh authentication, so with suppress_login_events = false each one wrote a login record (DICOM PS3.15 §A.5.1, EventID 110114). The crate’s Caller::cached now tells the cache hit apart: one login record per credential verification, as [auth.basic] cache_ttl_seconds documents.

  • A lookup by subject no longer echoes the subject id (#3906). The 404 of GET /ehr?subject_id=…&subject_namespace=… for a subject with no EHR, and the message extension’s refusal for an unknown subject_id, named the identifier, a national patient number in many deployments. Both now name only the namespace or the parameter. A test drives the lookup under a subscriber that records every log line and span attribute and asserts the identifier reaches none of them; the request log and traces already recorded the path and route without the query string. The book’s Security page says that the identifier travels in the URL and that a proxy in front of FerroEHR must not log query strings.

  • An archetype that fills two slots under different names gets the right path id in each (#3920). The web template took a slot fill’s name from whichever fill of the same archetype came first, so in a template that fills openEHR-EHR-CLUSTER.reference_sequence.v1 once as “Genome assembly” and once as “Reference sequence”, both fills were named genome_assembly and a FLAT path through the second, such as …/genomic_substitution_variant/reference_sequence/source_name, was refused as an unknown simplified path. Each fill now takes its node id from its own root term (ITS-REST Simplified Formats, Node ID Generation Rules). Web templates, FLAT and STRUCTURED examples, and FLAT paths change for templates that fill one archetype under two names. The openehr-* crates move to 0.0.95.

  • <root>/context/start_time sets the history origin and event times (#3919). A FLAT composition that gave its start time by path, without ctx/time, stored that start time but timed every untimed observation history and event with the commit time. The path spellings …/context/start_time, …/context/_end_time, …/context/_location and …/context/setting now feed the same defaults as ctx/time, ctx/end_time, ctx/location and ctx/setting (Simplified Formats, ctx/ vocabulary and RM mappings, EVENT_CONTEXT). An explicit ctx/ key still wins for the defaults.

  • A date or time pattern refusal says which parts are required, optional or not allowed (#3918). A value that breaks its template’s date, time or date-time pattern used to be refused with only the pattern, such as yyyy-mm-ddTXX:XX:XX, which reads as a match to anyone who takes XX for two digits. The refusal now names the parts in words (“the template allows a date only; a time is not allowed here”, “the template requires the second, which the value lacks”) and ends with a key to the pattern symbols. The book’s Templates & validation page explains them.

  • A stored composition’s archetype id keeps its case in the access log (#3908). The access record named a stored composition’s root archetype in lowercase, so a read of an openEHR-EHR-COMPOSITION.report.v1 composition recorded openehr-ehr-composition.report.v1 as its evidence, while template ids and ids taken from AQL text kept theirs. openEHR BASE asks identifiers to be case-preserving through persistence and case-insensitive in comparison (Composite Identifiers and Case). The node table keeps the lowercase id only as its comparison key beside the stored fragment, which has always held the id as written; the access log now reads the id from the fragment, so the evidence names the archetype as the composition wrote it, and AQL predicates and the category map still match in any case. Records written before keep the lowercase form.

Security

Shipped with functional changes because: only the newest release is supported (SECURITY.md), so a separate 5.2.1 published beside 5.3.2 would be out of support the moment 5.3.2 lands and give no one a release to stay on; the fix is a dependency and base-image bump with no behaviour change of its own.

  • rustls-webpki 0.103.16 and webpki-roots / webpki-root-certs 1.0.10 (RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2026-0382, RUSTSEC-2026-0383, GHSA-pmpg-vfwr-99qv). The outbound TLS client no longer accepts certificate paths through the distrusted emSign intermediates.
  • The ferroehr and ferroehr-viewer images move to the distroless base with ca-certificates 20250419+deb13u1 (DSA-6572-1, GHSA-pmpg-vfwr-99qv, #3926). The system trust store no longer holds the compromised eMudhra (emSign) intermediates; it is the only package that differs from the previous base.

5.2.0 - 2026-10-20

Added

  • [smart] issuer_metadata_file supplies the metadata of a jwks_file issuer (#3875). It names a JSON file with the RFC 8414 §2 metadata of the first [auth] issuer, read at boot, so a server whose key set is a file can serve the SMART discovery document with a token_endpoint. The metadata must name that issuer and every endpoint in it must be https (a loopback host excepted); a file set for an issuer whose metadata the server fetches refuses the start.

  • An authorised, audited read of a party’s protected national identifiers (#3776). GET {base}/admin/party/identifiers?version_uid=… serves a party version with the identifiers [demographic.identifier_protection] seals put back to their values, a historical version included. It needs the admin role and the new [authz.rbac] identifier_reader_role; unset, nobody may call it. Every read writes one access record per scheme expanded, naming the reader, the party and the scheme, never the value.

  • The EHDS Art. 8 restriction of access by health professionals (#3682). On the person’s instruction the controller records a restriction with POST {base}/admin/access-restriction, for a whole EHR or one versioned object (GET reads the register, POST …/lift lifts it). Restricted data then reads as absent to every professional route, query and export: a restricted composition or EHR answers 404 as an unknown one does, queries and exports leave it out, a CONTRIBUTION lists none of its versions, the event stream withholds it, and a write to it is refused as a write to an unknown target. A whole-EHR restriction covers data recorded after it. The admin routes still see everything, and nothing is deleted. A caller holding the new [authz.rbac] emergency_access_role that declares one of [audit] emergency_purpose_codes reads restricted data (EHDS Art. 11(5)), and its access record carries the emergency mark. Two migrations add the register and the marks (clinical/0015_access_restriction.sql, party/0011_access_restriction_column.sql).

Changed

  • Authentication runs on ferrohealth-smart 0.3.1 (#3875). The crate now holds what FerroEHR kept around it: the cache of verified Basic credentials, the RFC 6750 §2.1 b64token check, the refusal of a blank sub and the redacted rendering of [auth]. What changes for you:

    • [authz] basic_cache_ttl_seconds is now [auth.basic] cache_ttl_seconds (FERROEHR__AUTH__BASIC__CACHE_TTL_SECONDS), and its default is 0, which checks every request. Set 60 to keep the former behaviour. The old key is an unknown key and refuses the start.
    • [auth] scopeless_subjects is accepted: a listed subject whose token carries no resource scope meets every SMART on openEHR requirement, and a token that carries scopes gets only its scopes. It refused the start before.
    • A bearer token outside the b64token alphabet answers 401 with error="invalid_token" (RFC 6750 §3.1: a malformed token). It answered 400 invalid_request before. A header that is no scheme and credential, and two Authorization headers, still answer 400.
    • A rendered configuration (ferroehr config check, /management/env, ferroehr report) writes a Basic password hash as [redacted].
    • With [audit] suppress_login_events = false, every request a Basic credential authenticates writes a login record, since the credential is checked on each request. Before, only a request that missed the cache did.
    • The Helm chart is 12.1.2; its values document the two keys.

  • An EHR extract never carries a protected national identifier between deployments, and the refusal says what to do instead (#3777). Importing a party whose identifier another deployment sealed answers 422 naming the remedy: import the extract without the party and register the person through the receiving deployment’s party API, which seals the identifier under its own key. The book’s EHR Extract page records the decision and the steps.

Fixed

  • A FLAT OBSERVATION without a history origin takes the earliest event’s time (#3888, openehr-sdt 0.0.91). Simplified Formats master05 §OBSERVATION says /history_origin “will be set to the time of the earliest event if not explicitly set”; the builder used the composition’s context time. Times are compared as instants across offsets, ctx/history_origin still wins, and with no event time the context time stands.

5.1.0 - 2026-10-20

Added

  • The Helm chart mounts a database CA for sslmode=verify-full (#3788, chart 12.1.0). database.caConfigMap names a ConfigMap holding the CA the database certificates chain to (key database.caConfigMapKey, ca.crt by default); the server, the migration Job and the backup CronJobs mount it at /etc/ferroehr-db-ca, where a DSN’s sslrootcert names it. values-production.yaml sets it to ferroehr-db-ca and tells you to end every DSN in ?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/etc/ferroehr-db-ca/ca.crt.

  • A demographic query joins a party to the content of its EHR (#3831). FROM PERSON p CONTAINS EHR e CONTAINS COMPOSITION c (with ORGANISATION or ROLE as the root too, and party classes beside the EHR in an AND) answers a row per party and clinical row of an EHR that party is the subject of, through the party-to-EHR map. It runs as one statement per database credential, joined, ordered and paged by the server; a column, WHERE condition or ORDER BY key reading both sides, an aggregate, DISTINCT, and a half above query.max_result_rows each answer 400. The party read and the map read each leave an access record in their own domain.

  • The audit feed and the remote policy service authenticate with OAuth 2.0 client credentials (#3829). [audit.fhir_feed.oauth] and [authz.abac.remote.oauth] take a client-credentials grant (token_url or issuer, client_id, client_secret or client_secret_file, client_auth, scope, audience, resource). The server sends the token as a bearer credential, renews it before it expires, and fetches a new one once when the upstream refuses it with 401. A policy service that cannot be reached with a token fails the request closed. HTTP Basic through the URL stays, and setting both is a startup error.

  • AQL rooted at PERSON, ORGANISATION or ROLE (#3818), the subset of the experimental AQL demographic extension a client needs to find a party by what it holds. POST /query/aql answers rows over the latest version of each party, leaving out logically deleted ones, with paths inside the party in SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY (its details tree, its identities, contacts and capabilities, p/uid/value), CONTAINS CLUSTER and the other content classes inside a party, named parameters, and the offset and fetch paging. It runs under the authorisation of a Demographic API read, on the demographic database credential. GROUP, AGENT, PARTY_RELATIONSHIP, a demographic class below the root, EHR or clinical content anywhere but directly under the root, and an ehr_id scope each answer 400 naming the construct.

  • openehr-sdt validates a party against its template (#3832). rm_instance::validate_party runs the RM-invariant and terminology passes with the template’s party class (PERSON, ORGANISATION, GROUP, AGENT or ROLE) as the root type, then the archetype-conformance pass over the template, so a party missing a mandatory element is refused at that element’s path. A template rooted at another class is refused at /. The nine openehr-* crates move to 0.0.90.

Changed

  • Authentication and SMART on openEHR run on ferrohealth-smart 0.2.0 (#3872). This is a breaking change to the configuration with no deprecation period. [auth.oidc] is gone: the token issuer is configured in [auth] itself (issuer or [[auth.issuer]], audience, algorithms, token_profile, clock_skew_seconds, jwks_max_age_seconds, jwks_refresh_interval_seconds, jwks_file, timeout_ms, realm). The server reads each issuer’s metadata and key set at boot, accepts only asymmetric algorithms, requires typ: at+jwt under the default token_profile (RFC 9068 §4), and answers every invalid token with one 401 that names no reason. An issuer on plain http is accepted only on a loopback address. A Basic user is user, password_hash or password_hash_file, and scopes; its roles move to [authz.rbac.basic_roles], and the verified-credential cache to [authz] basic_cache_ttl_seconds. [auth.oidc.assurance] and [auth.oidc.professional] become [authz.assurance] and [authz.professional].

  • Every route enforces its SMART on openEHR scope whenever [auth] is on (#3872). There is no switch any more: an EHR, composition, directory or contribution route needs a composition- scope, a template route a template- scope, a query an aql- scope, the ADMIN API the [auth] product_scope (default __ferroehr.platform), and the DEMOGRAPHIC API a client listed in [smart] demographic_clients or the product scope. A credential without the scope gets 403 with the insufficient_scope challenge. A patient/ grant counts only for an issuer in [smart] patient_issuers and is bound to the EHR the token’s ehrId claim names; a system/aql-* grant counts only for a client in [smart] backend_clients.

  • The SMART configuration document is built from the issuer’s metadata (#3872). [smart] enabled serves it, needs an issuer whose metadata names a token_endpoint, and lists only the authorization_code and client_credentials grants and the S256 challenge method. Its capabilities and scopes_supported come from [auth] capabilities and [auth] scopes_supported beside what the server enforces.

  • The terminology client fetches its client-credentials token through ferrohealth-smart (#3872). The [terminology.external.oauth2_clients] keys are unchanged.

  • The Helm chart and the compose files follow the new keys (#3872, chart 12.0.0). The chart’s Basic users are keyed by user, and the CDR credential FerroBRIDGE uses is HTTP Basic only.

  • The Keycloak overlay and the development stack serve Keycloak’s issuer over TLS (#3873). A one-shot keycloak-tls service generates a development CA and Keycloak’s certificate on the first up, Keycloak serves the issuer at https://keycloak:8443/auth/realms/ferroehr, and the CDR trusts that CA through SSL_CERT_DIR with token_profile = "jwt", so a Keycloak token is accepted again. Both realms put the SMART on openEHR scopes and the product scope into every token. The token call on port 8081 is unchanged.

  • The viewer takes FerroUI 0.2.0 and reads every word it draws from its catalog (#300, #3860). The labels it hands FerroUI (table captions, column headers, pager nouns with their plurals, navigation, tabs, fields, dialogs, toasts) are looked up in locales/en/ferroehr-viewer.ftl at run time, and the stray-literal baseline drops from 1918 to 505 literals. English remains the only locale.

Removed

  • The HMAC token key and the static bearer token (#3872). hmac_secret and hmac_secret_file are unknown keys, as are the inline jwks_json key set and allow_insecure_issuer; the Helm chart drops secrets.authOidcHmacSecret and bridge.cdr.auth. Machine-to-machine callers authenticate with HTTP Basic or an OAuth 2.0 client-credentials token from the issuer. Only the asymmetric algorithms RFC 9068 §4 names verify a bearer token, so a token signed with a shared secret is refused.
  • [smart] ehr_id_claim, patient_claim, require_smart_scopes and [smart.endpoints] (#3872). The launch context is the token’s ehrId claim, enforcement is always on, and the discovery document’s endpoints come from the issuer’s metadata.
  • [auth] scopeless_subjects is refused at boot (#3872), because a SMART on openEHR requirement admits no caller without scopes.

Fixed

  • A TDD keeps two same-archetype siblings told apart by name apart (#3833). Converting a TDD of a template whose events (or other compacted nodes) share an archetype node id and differ by name, such as a Baseline and a Follow up event, now builds two nodes, each with the content the TDD spells out under its own element, where it used to merge them into one.

  • A rotated mTLS client CA takes effect without a restart (#3769). [server.tls] client_ca_file is re-read every reload_interval_secs, as the certificate and key already were, and a changed CA verifies every new handshake; a file that fails to load is logged and the previous CA stays in force.

  • An unmounted path outside the API answers 404 (#3834). With server.swagger_ui at private or admin_only, the documentation guard wrapped every unmatched path, so /.well-known/smart-configuration on a server with SMART off answered 401, and the viewer’s System screen said the CDR refused the session. The guard now covers the documentation routes only, and the viewer shows SMART as not enabled.

  • Four viewer layout defects (#3841). The Create EHR id field’s placeholder reads “UUID, or blank” and fits; the audit log’s From and To filters take a wider share of the row so an instant shows whole, its Event column keeps “REST · E” on one line, and an opened record scrolls inside a narrow box instead of widening the page. The book captures are taken with reduced motion, so the results Table/Chart toggle no longer shows mid-fade.

  • The OpenAPI family titles carry no em dash (#3865). The served documents and the viewer’s family selector read “FerroEHR: Messaging”, “openEHR: EHR” and so on.

  • No viewer string carries an em dash (#3860). The query builder’s template choice reads “Any template”, an absent value reads “(no value)”, and the hints, notes and form errors that used a dash use a colon or a full stop.

5.0.0 - 2026-10-19

Added

  • openehr-sdt builds a canonical PARTY from a party Web Template (#3810). flat::build::build_party (and flat::convert::party_from_flat / party_from_structured) turns a FLAT or STRUCTURED document of a PERSON, ORGANISATION, GROUP, AGENT or ROLE template into the party, with every list attribute of the demographic package (identities, contacts, addresses, capabilities, roles, languages, relationships) built as an array, no composition attribute, and a refusal for a ctx/ key. A ROLE takes its performer from <root>/performer|id, |namespace, |type and an optional |id_scheme. The result is decoded as the root class before it is returned, so a party the RM refuses is reported as an error. Simplified Formats define FLAT for compositions only, so this is FerroEHR’s own extension over the same template walk. flat::build::build_root is the same walk for any non-COMPOSITION root, and flat::example::example_root_instance generates an example instance of such a root class for validation and tests.
  • The openEHR terminology serves interoperability (672) as a term mapping purpose (#3838, SPECTERM-31): TERM_MAPPING.purpose validation accepts it, and the terminology endpoints list it in all five languages.
  • The openehr-sdt builders stamp the ARCHETYPED.rm_version the caller chooses (#3809). flat::build::BuildOptions carries it into build_composition_with, build_party and flat::tdd::from_tdd_with; build_composition and from_tdd keep stamping 1.2.0.

Changed

  • The viewer draws with FerroUI 0.1.7 and is ready for more languages, English the one that ships (#300). FerroUI’s words and the viewer’s come from Fluent catalogs, the viewer’s under app/ferroehr-viewer/locales/, so a language joins as a catalog file with no code change. The locale is chosen once per request, the best language of Accept-Language the viewer’s catalog holds or else the new [ui] locale (default en), and the page writes it as <html lang>. scripts/checks/stray-literals.sh fails CI on a viewer string outside the catalog beyond the per-file baseline the remaining strings hold while they move.
  • A structure the Web Template compacts away (an ITEM_TREE under a party identity or an ENTRY, for example) is rebuilt with the name its term definition gives instead of its at-code (#3810).
  • The nine openehr-* crates move to 0.0.89.
  • Only the newest release is supported (#3853). When a new release is published, every earlier release stops receiving fixes: there are no maintenance branches, no long-term-support line and no backports. If you are not on the newest release, upgrade; upgrading is free. Under the Cyber Resilience Act, Cadasto B.V. commits to keep publishing security fixes for at least five years after each release (Art 13(8)) and ships them only in the newest release (Art 13(10)). SECURITY.md, the release notes and the compliance pages say so in place of a five-year support period per release. The end month of that commitment stays on the boot banner, in ferroehr --version and in the management documents; the banner line now reads newest release only; fixes published until the end of <month>.
  • Archetype identifiers follow the BASE 1.3.0 grammar under the development profile (#3835, #3845). The namespaced ADL 2 form (org.openehr::openEHR-EHR-OBSERVATION.blood_pressure.v2.1.4, with an optional -rc, -alpha or -beta modifier and build count) is accepted wherever an ARCHETYPE_ID is read, and openehr_base::v1_3::ArchetypeId gains namespace(), minor_version() and patch_version(). A namespaceless identifier with a full version stays accepted, because AM 2.4.0 artefacts carry it (the conflict is reported upstream, #3844); every other identifier the grammar refuses, such as a malformed namespace or version modifier, is refused naming it. The stable profile keeps BASE 1.2.0’s grammar.

Fixed

  • The viewer serves its hydration bundle on a route of its own (#3849). A /pkg/ file the bundle lacks answers 404 and a read failure 500, each logged with its path and status; neither reaches the rendered app or the sign-in redirect any more, which had answered a browser 302 for its own WebAssembly and failed the ui-e2e journeys.
  • The template example endpoints answer 400 Bad Request naming the root for a template whose root is not a COMPOSITION (an OBSERVATION or a SECTION), instead of an object carrying COMPOSITION members its class does not have (#3780). The 200 body the specification defines is an instance of a versioned-object class, which such a template does not describe.
  • Same-archetype siblings told apart only by name (two EVENTs Baseline and Follow up of one archetype node, for example) stay two nodes when a FLAT or STRUCTURED document builds, so the example of such a template passes the server’s own validation (#3779).

4.3.11 - 2026-10-19

Changed

  • The viewer draws in FerroUI, the shared FerroHEALTH component library (#3802). The shell, the navigation, the theme toggle, the tables and their pager, the dialogs, the access side panel, the upload field, the charts, the document panes with their copy button, the tabs, the tree, the toasts, the alerts, the loading skeletons, the buttons, fields, cards and empty states, the icons and the document highlighter come from ferrohealth-ui, the library FerroBRIDGE, FerroFED and FerroTERM share; thaw, leptos-use and leptos-chartistry are gone. The viewer keeps its teal and slate. The moon and sun button in the top bar switches between dark and light, the viewer follows the operating system until you press it, and the choice is a server cookie the server writes on the page, so the first paint is already in your theme and nothing is kept in browser storage. The Content Security Policy drops 'unsafe-inline' from style-src: the stylesheets are the viewer’s own files.
